title: 717 claimed ransomware victims in November 2025
description: Bitdefender Labs recorded 717 organizations claimed by ransomware groups on Data Leak Sites between November 1 and November 30, 2025. The figure aggregates self-reported victim postings across all tracked RaaS operations and reflects continued high-volume extortion activity heading into year-end.

title: Qilin claimed 122 victims, down from 205
description: After running its August-to-October Korean Leaks campaign against an MSP ecosystem, Qilin's claimed victim count fell to 122 in November 2025 — a sharp drop from 205 the previous month. The sparkline contrasts the October peak with the post-campaign November cool-off, while Qilin still held the #1 position in Bitdefender's Top 10.

title: Qilin victim count: October vs November 2025
description: Qilin's monthly claimed-victim count fell from 205 in October 2025 to 122 in November 2025 — roughly a 40% month-over-month decline — as the group's Korean Leaks MSP campaign wound down. Bitdefender retains Qilin at the #1 position in its Top 10 ransomware families despite the drop.

title: Clop claimed 102 victims, reclaiming the Top 10
description: Clop posted 102 victims in November 2025, surpassing Akira to retake the #2 position in Bitdefender's Top 10. The group concentrated on manufacturing, technology and healthcare targets, repeatedly leveraging a zero-day affecting Oracle E-Business Suite (CVE-2025-61882) to compromise large numbers of systems.

title: Top ransomware families by claimed victims, Nov 2025
description: Among Bitdefender's Top 10, Qilin again led with 122 claimed victims in November 2025, followed by Clop with 102. Clop's rise was driven by exploitation of an Oracle E-Business Suite zero-day, pushing Akira out of the #2 slot. The two leading groups alone accounted for roughly 31% of the 717 total claimed victims for the month.

title: Warlock claimed 3 Russia-based victims in one month
description: Warlock listed 3 victims based in Russia during November 2025 — a highly unusual event given most Russian-aligned actors avoid domestic targets. Bitdefender notes shared TTPs with state-sponsored Storm-2603 (which abused SharePoint ToolShell flaws) and reads the incident as supporting evidence that Warlock is a China-based operation.
comparison: vs zero/near-zero Russian victims in normal months

title: Traditional RaaS profit margin: 85–90% for operators
description: Bitdefender researchers observe that the typical Ransomware-as-a-Service split leaves 85–90% of paid ransoms with operators (or affiliates, depending on the model). Kryptos' new insider-recruitment scheme is explicitly designed to expand profit-sharing beyond this baseline by paying corporate insiders for VPN, MFA and SSH access.

title: Insider payoff range
description: Bitdefender describes Kryptos' tiered profit-sharing scheme for corporate insiders — IT admins, executive assistants and third-party vendors — who hand over VPN, MFA or SSH access. Removing the need for EDR/AV-killers and infostealers, the model rewards insiders with payments scaled to the value of access provided.
quote: "The payoff for those willing to become an insider threat runs from thousands of dollars all the way up to millions of dollars."

title: 7 RaaS brands in a single alleged alliance
description: Stormous announced version 5 of its RaaS in October 2025 along with a strategic partnership purportedly tying together seven groups: Stormous, Devman, Coinbase Cartel, Nova, Radar, Desolator and Kryptos. Researchers questioned the legitimacy of the alliance citing operational-model clashes and a lack of corroborating communication from named partners.

title: React2Shell (CVE-2025-55182) hits 4 React versions
description: CVE-2025-55182 is a critical flaw in React Server Components that enables initial access and remote code execution via crafted HTTP requests containing malicious objects. React 19.0.0, 19.1.0, 19.1.1 and 19.2.0 are affected, alongside default Next.js 15.x and 16.x configurations and 14.x Canary builds. Bitdefender warns the impact may rival Log4Shell.

title: Clop exploits Oracle EBS zero-day CVE-2025-61882
description: Clop's November 2025 campaign repeatedly weaponised CVE-2025-61882, a flaw enabling compromise of Oracle Concurrent Processing in Oracle E-Business Suite versions 12.2.14 through 12.2.3. Organisations running affected EBS versions are urged to apply the vendor patch to disrupt the group's mass-exploitation pipeline.

title: Clop's primary target industries, Nov 2025
description: Of Clop's 102 claimed victims in November 2025, Bitdefender flags manufacturing, technology and healthcare as the dominant verticals — sectors aligned with the group's Oracle E-Business Suite exploitation strategy. The chart illustrates the named priority targets called out in the debrief; exact per-industry counts are not enumerated in the source text.

title: Akira: ~1 year targeting Nutanix VMs
description: CISA's updated Akira advisory underscores that the group has been targeting Nutanix VMs for nearly a year. Akira's Linux encryptor in the Nutanix AHV environment encrypts virtual disks (`.qcow2`) without first powering down VMs — a divergence from the standard ESXi attack flow.

title: Nova RaaS exposed by CBSecurity leak
description: In early December 2025 a group calling itself CBSecurity dumped Nova ransomware staff names, roles and infrastructure IPs. Bitdefender assesses the leak was likely engineered by an angry affiliate or competitor reacting to Nova's targeting of education and non-profit victims earlier in the year.
quote: "A group named CBSecurity leaked the names and roles associated with Nova staff and multiple IP addresses tied to their infrastructure."

title: ShinySp1d3r Windows encryptor capabilities
description: ShinyHunters' newly released ShinySp1d3r RaaS bundles a Windows encryptor capable of suppressing Event Viewer logging, force-killing processes, and deploying malware via SCM and WMI. Bitdefender suggests this in-house tooling — released just before Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters' August takedown — may become a template for other groups breaking away from third-party affiliates.
quote: "The encryptor's ability to hook EtwEventWrite to offset the writing of data into Windows Event Viewer, its ability to force kill open processes, and also run malware locally via actions such as deployViaSCM and deployViaWMI."

title: Korean Leaks: 30+ South Korean orgs breached
description: From August through October 2025, Qilin — working with a partner likely linked to Moonstone Sleet — leveraged a compromised MSP ecosystem to leak data from more than 30 South Korea-based organisations. Bitdefender ties this campaign directly to Qilin's October peak of 205 victims and its sharp November fall-off to 122.

title: Bitdefender Labs sees 400+ new threats per minute
description: Bitdefender Labs reports discovering more than 400 new threats every minute and validating 30 billion threat queries each day across its telemetry. With more than 180 technology brands embedding Bitdefender's stack via OEM partnerships, the vendor positions this dataset as one of the industry's broadest real-time threat-landscape feeds.

title: 30 billion threat queries validated daily
description: Bitdefender's global telemetry validates 30 billion threat queries per day across hundreds of millions of endpoints. The scale underpins the visibility behind monthly debriefs and contextualises the 717-victim ransomware tally observed in November 2025.

title: 180+ technology brands embed Bitdefender
description: Bitdefender notes more than 180 third-party technology vendors license its detection and protection engines through OEM agreements. The OEM footprint amplifies the company's visibility into the threat landscape beyond its own first-party consumer and business products.

title: Ransomware claimed-victim mix — Qilin & Clop share of 717
description: Qilin (122) and Clop (102) together accounted for 224 of November 2025's 717 claimed ransomware victims — roughly 31% of the total — with the remaining 493 victims distributed across the rest of the tracked Top 10 and long tail of smaller RaaS operations.
comparison: Top 2 vs rest of RaaS market

title: Frameworks impacted by React2Shell
description: CVE-2025-55182 affects four React releases (19.0.0, 19.1.0, 19.1.1, 19.2.0), the default configurations of Next.js 15.x and 16.x, and Canary builds of Next.js 14.x. This chart illustrates the affected-component footprint Bitdefender flags as a potential Log4Shell-style mass-exploitation risk.

title: Open source is effectively universal in commercial software
description: 98% of audited codebases contain open source components, up from 97% the prior year. Only 2% of codebases had no open source, and even those likely represent specialized legacy systems rather than new development.
pageOrSection: Open Source Adoption and Codebase Complexity

title: Codebases containing at least one vulnerability
description: 87% of audited commercial codebases contained at least one known open source vulnerability in the 2024-25 scans, up one point from 86% the prior year. Vulnerability prevalence remains near-universal across modern applications.

title: Mean vulnerabilities per codebase more than doubled
description: Average vulnerabilities per codebase reached 581 in 2024-25 scans, up 107% from 280 the prior year. This explosive growth reflects component growth, AI-assisted dependency selection, development velocity, and disclosure acceleration driven by the Linux Kernel CNA change.

title: Codebases with high-risk vulnerabilities
description: 78% of audited codebases contained at least one high-risk open source vulnerability in 2024-25 scans, down modestly from 81% the prior year. More than three-quarters of commercial software still ships with severe issues that could result in data breaches or system compromise.

title: Codebases with critical-risk vulnerabilities
description: 44% of audited codebases contained at least one critical-risk vulnerability in 2024-25 scans, down four points from 48% the prior year. Nearly half of all commercial codebases still harbor flaws where exploitation could cause significant damage.

title: Organizations hit by a software supply chain attack
description: 65% of organizations Black Duck surveyed in 2025 reported experiencing a software supply chain attack in the past year. These are active threats impacting enterprises across every major industry.

title: Malicious package breakdown: created vs hijacked
description: Of malicious packages identified across open source ecosystems, 66% were purpose-built to harm users via typosquatting, dependency confusion, or social engineering, while 34% were hijacked legitimate packages compromised after gaining community trust.

title: Credentials leaked by the Shai-Hulud npm worm
description: The self-propagating Shai-Hulud 2.0 worm compromised nearly 800 npm packages, created over 25,000 GitHub repositories containing stolen secrets, and leaked more than 400,000 credentials before npm could remove malicious versions.

title: Organizations shipping open source AI/ML models
description: 49% of organizations now incorporate open source AI/ML models directly into the software they ship, creating a new attack surface that traditional security tools were not designed to address. Over 850,000 models reached platforms like Hugging Face in 2024 alone.
pageOrSection: AI Model Risk: An Emerging Attack Surface

title: Codebases with license conflicts at historic high
description: Two-thirds of audited codebases now contain license conflicts that could create legal exposure or compliance failures. The 12-percentage-point jump from 56% to 68% is the largest single-year increase in OSSRA history.

title: Codebases with abandoned (zombie) components
description: 93% of audited codebases contain components with no development activity in over two years, up from 91% the prior year. When a vulnerability is discovered in one of these abandoned projects, there may be no one able to fix it.

title: Codebases with components 4+ years out-of-date
description: 92% of audited codebases contain components that are more than four years out-of-date, up from 90% in the prior year. Maintenance debt has become a near-universal feature of commercial software supply chains.

title: Component age distribution across audited codebases
description: More than two-thirds of all components in audited codebases are over two years old. The long tail of aging components represents years of accumulated dependency decisions that were added, never updated, and eventually forgotten.

title: Version currency: how far behind components are
description: Only 7% of components in audited codebases are running the latest available version. The plurality—41%—are 10 or more versions behind, evidence of pervasive update friction across modern software supply chains.

title: Median component age
description: The median open source component in audited codebases is now 45 months old, up from 42 months in the prior year. Components added years ago are still running unchanged in production, accumulating risk silently.

title: High- or critical-risk vulnerability prevalence by industry
description: Vulnerability profiles vary significantly by industry. EdTech leads with 100% of audited codebases carrying a high- or critical-risk vulnerability, while Hardware/Semiconductors (59%) and VR/Gaming/Media (48%) trail thanks to more controlled dependency selection and longer development cycles.

title: License conflict rates: highest vs lowest industries
description: Big Data/AI/ML (78%) and EdTech (74%) lead in license conflict rates, driven by complex dependency trees and the JavaScript ecosystem's license diversity. Safety-critical sectors—Aerospace/Auto/Transport (52%), Hardware/Semiconductors (54%), and Manufacturing (58%)—show much lower rates thanks to rigorous component vetting.

title: Top open source licenses by codebase prevalence
description: MIT (92%), Apache 2.0 (90%), and BSD licenses dominate the audited codebases, signaling pervasive use of permissive open source. But nearly half (48%) of codebases also contain LGPL components, whose weak copyleft terms can create compliance complexity—especially for embedded systems where static linking is common.

title: Components with no detected license
description: 8% of open source components carry no detected license at all. Under default copyright, authors retain all rights, meaning organizations using that code have no legal right to do so. Another 11% have custom or modified licenses requiring individual legal review.

title: Codebase complexity has quadrupled in five years
description: Mean file count per codebase grew from 24,094 in 2022 to 84,499 in 2026—a 251% increase. Beginning in 2024, file counts and component counts both accelerated dramatically, coinciding with mainstream AI coding assistant adoption.

title: Mean components per codebase
description: Mean open source components per codebase grew from 911 to 1,180 in a single year, a 30% increase. Each new dependency introduces its own vulnerability history, license obligations, and maintenance dependencies—often pulling in dozens of transitive components.
pageOrSection: Open Source Adoption and Codebase Complexity

title: Open source components pulled in as transitive dependencies
description: 64% of open source components in a typical codebase are transitive dependencies—pulled in automatically by direct dependencies. Developers never explicitly chose these components, yet their code is bound by the components' license terms and vulnerabilities.

title: How Black Duck detects open source: 16% outside package managers
description: 84% of open source components are identified through automated package manager and manifest scanning, but 16% require deeper analysis—snippet detection or binary analysis. Organizations relying only on dependency-manifest scanning are missing nearly one in six open source components in their codebases.

title: Black Duck Security Advisories beat NVD by 100 days on average
description: Of the CVEs analyzed during the November 2024 to October 2025 period, Black Duck was on average 100 days faster than NVD, and 94 days faster for critical- and high-risk vulnerabilities. 20,520 BDSAs were added in the past year alone—about 56 per day.

title: Top 10 most prevalent CVEs/BDSAs in 2025
description: BDSA-2021-3651 leads at 35% of codebases. jQuery-related vulnerabilities (CVE-2020-11022, CVE-2020-11023, CVE-2019-11358, CVE-2015-9251) continue to dominate, collectively affecting 25-28% of codebases despite patches being available for years. BDSA-2025-2047 (CVE-2025-27789) is a notable new entry appearing in over 20% of codebases within its first year.

title: AI coding assistant usage frequency
description: 44% of DevSecOps professionals now use AI coding assistants frequently or constantly, with adoption deeply integrated into daily workflows. Including occasional users, more than three-quarters of the industry has adopted AI coding tools to some degree. Only 4% have never used them or are not permitted.

title: Organizations performing comprehensive AI-code evaluation
description: Only 24% of organizations perform comprehensive IP, license, security, and quality evaluations for AI-generated code. While 76% check for security risks, just 54% evaluate IP and license risks and 56% assess quality—leaving significant oversights across the software supply chain.

title: Mean vulnerabilities per codebase have more than doubled
description: Black Duck's executive framing of the 2026 OSSRA. The 107% year-over-year jump in mean vulnerabilities per codebase—to 581—is the defining finding of this year's report, driven by component growth, AI-assisted dependency selection, and disclosure acceleration.
quote: "If there's one finding that defines the 2026 OSSRA, it's this: Mean vulnerabilities per codebase have more than doubled."

title: Discipline pays: dependency-savvy orgs are 28 points more prepared
description: Black Duck's supply chain research shows that organizations highly effective at tracking and managing open source dependencies are significantly more prepared to secure their open source software. The challenge: fewer than half of organizations rate themselves as highly effective at this fundamental practice.
quote: "Organizations highly effective at dependency management are significantly more prepared to secure their software—85% versus 57% for the overall population."

title: Adversary infrastructure is an early-warning system
description: Censys frames the 2025 State of the Internet Report around the idea that the public-internet footprint of attacker infrastructure - C2 servers, open directories, residential proxies, IoT botnets - is observable and measurable, and can be used to warn defenders before campaigns mature.
quote: "Adversary infrastructure provides an early-warning system for malicious activity, revealing where it resides, how long it persists, and how continuity is maintained across shifting services."

title: Cobalt Strike C2 servers live a median of 5 days
description: Across Censys scan data, Cobalt Strike TeamServer services exhibited an average time-to-live of 11.2 days and a median of just 5 days, with an interquartile range of 3-19 days. The short lifespan reflects active takedown pressure and operator OPSEC churn.

title: Viper C2 servers persist a median of 18.5 days
description: Viper C2 services lived substantially longer than Cobalt Strike infrastructure, with an average TTL of 17.4 days and a median of 18.5 days. Censys hypothesizes the wider variance in Cobalt Strike reflects its greater prevalence and exposure to takedowns.
comparison: vs 5 days median for Cobalt Strike

title: Cobalt Strike vs Viper C2 lifespans
description: Side-by-side TTL distribution for the two most-tracked C2 families in the report. Cobalt Strike services churn faster across every statistic, while Viper hosts remain online longer on average and at the median.

title: Cobalt Strike top ports by share of observed services
description: Censys ranks the most common ports for Cobalt Strike TeamServer services. Port 443 leads at 23.8%, closely followed by port 80 at 21.7%, with the Cobalt Strike default 50050 at 9.2%. Most beaconing still hides behind HTTP/HTTPS conventions.

title: Viper top ports by share of observed services
description: Viper deployments cluster heavily on two ports: TCP 60000 (46.6%) and TCP 80 (45.4%). Port 60000 is short-lived (median 5 days) while port 80 hosts persist for a median of 30 days, suggesting two very different operational profiles within the same C2 family.

title: Median open directory disappears in 1 day
description: Censys sampled open web directories on HTTP services during April. Half of them were network-visible for one day or less - a sign that adversaries cycle staging infrastructure aggressively, but also that defenders have an extremely short window to capture evidence.

title: Open directories: content outlives network availability
description: Using TLSH rolling-hash similarity, Censys found that while the median network lifespan of an open directory is just 1 day, its content lifespan extends to 3 days. The same payloads tend to reappear on new hosts, weakening the value of pure IP/host blocklists.

title: Even when a directory blinks offline, its content doesn't change
description: Censys highlights the asymmetry between network presence and content persistence as a key lesson for blue teams: pivoting on file hashes and directory contents catches more adversary infrastructure than chasing IP addresses alone.
quote: "Even if a web directory blips in and out in terms of network visibility, the content doesn't necessarily change."

title: 1,011 Cleo file-transfer systems were exposed to CL0P
description: Censys identified roughly 1,011 internet-exposed Cleo file transfer instances potentially vulnerable to CVE-2024-55956 and CVE-2024-50623 - about 70% of all Cleo systems it could see. CL0P weaponized the flaws starting around 3 December 2024.

title: CL0P named 378 victims from the Cleo campaign
description: By 1 July 2025, the CL0P ransomware group's data-leak site listed 378 organizations breached via the Cleo file-transfer flaws. A separate Termite gang listed roughly 12 additional victims, underscoring how a single MFT vulnerability fueled an entire year of extortion activity.

title: DragonForce scanned 250,000+ IPs for FortiOS zero-day
description: Investigating CVE-2024-55591, Censys observed a single attacker host at 91.199.163.21:8000 testing more than 250,000 IP addresses for vulnerable FortiOS / FortiProxy devices. The mass scan ultimately compromised 31 devices and exfiltrated credentials from 22 hosts, concentrated in the US and Switzerland.

title: Operation Morpheus took down 85% of pirated Cobalt Strike
description: Of 690 illegally licensed Cobalt Strike instances targeted in June 2024's Operation Morpheus, 593 were successfully disrupted - an 85% success rate. Censys observed a clear drop in unique Cobalt Strike IPs in July 2024 before partial recovery in subsequent months.

title: PolarEdge IoT botnet grew from 150 to 40,000 devices
description: First observed in June 2023 with ~150 infected devices, the PolarEdge IoT botnet expanded to approximately 40,000 active devices by August 2025. The campaign mixes enterprise gear (Cisco APIC, ASA firewalls) with consumer routers, NAS, IP cameras and VoIP phones using a custom Mbed TLS backdoor.

title: PolarEdge infections concentrate in South Korea and the US
description: Geographic distribution of PolarEdge-infected devices is sharply uneven: South Korea hosts 51.6% of compromised devices and the United States 21.1%, leaving roughly a quarter scattered across the rest of the world.

title: 2,400+ hosts serve the PolarEdge-linked RPX certificate
description: Censys' follow-up analysis of PolarEdge-adjacent residential-proxy (RPX) infrastructure identified more than 2,400 hosts presenting the suspicious Mbed TLS certificate that ties the ecosystem together - a substantial Operational Relay Box (ORB) footprint hidden in legitimate consumer networks.
comparison: single RPX server peaked at 100+ proxy nodes in Aug 2025

title: ORBs hide adversary traffic inside consumer networks
description: Operational Relay Boxes turn legitimate routers, NAS units and IP cameras into exit nodes for malicious traffic without disturbing their primary function - a tactic Censys flags as a defining feature of the 2025 threat landscape.
quote: "Operation Relay Boxes (ORBs) are compromised exit nodes that forward traffic without taking over the device's core function."

title: DPRK BeaverTail keeps ~4 control servers online at any time
description: The North Korean BeaverTail / InvisibleFerret campaign maintained a steady operational tempo from October 2024 through at least July 2025, typically running four control servers simultaneously on TCP 1224, 1225 and 3000, hosted predominantly on Cloudzy / RouterHosting infrastructure across Europe and the US.

title: DPRK campaigns succeed via adaptability, not sophistication
description: Censys' takeaway from tracking BeaverTail and the wider DPRK developer-targeting ecosystem is that low-tech but persistent operations are what keep these campaigns productive, with thousands of remote workers staged across China, Russia and Vietnam.
quote: "These campaigns remain effective not because of technical sophistication, but because of adaptability and persistence."

title: Wainscot infection persisted on Indian military host for 2 years
description: Censys' Wainscot investigation - linked to the Storm-0156 cluster - identified a modified variant of the malware running on an Indian Territorial Army system near the Pakistan border from December 2022 through November 2024, designed to survive intermittent satellite/mobile connectivity before being remediated in February 2025.

title: 57 of CL0P's Cleo victims were named in January 2025 alone
description: CL0P's January 2025 mass announcement listed 57 organizations breached via Cleo - approximately 15% of all CL0P intrusions disclosed before July. The gap between initial exploitation in December 2024 and leak-site disclosure exceeded three months for several victims.

title: Cobalt Strike content outlives network presence
description: When Censys tracked individual Cobalt Strike beacon watermarks rather than network availability, average TTL rose from 9.5 days to 11.1 days and median TTL from 4 to 6 days. The same beacon license is being moved between hosts, complicating IP-based blocklists.
comparison: content TTL ~50% longer than network TTL

title: Edge devices have become the operational layer of adversary networks
description: A summary takeaway across PolarEdge, RPX, and DPRK campaigns: residential routers, NAS units, IP cameras and small-business firewalls are now the preferred substrate for adversary infrastructure - not data centers - because they blend legitimate encrypted traffic with operator traffic.
quote: "The rise of edge-based infrastructure such as residential proxies and IoT botnets complements traditional C2 ecosystems and is reshaping how adversaries maintain continuity."

title: Risky AI prompts grew 97% in 2025
description: Check Point Research measured a 97% year-over-year increase in risky AI prompts during 2025, reflecting how widespread unsupervised GenAI use has become inside enterprises and how it amplifies prompt injection and data-leak exposure.
pageOrSection: AI as a Force Multiplier Across Cyber Attacks

title: 40% of analyzed MCPs were vulnerable
description: Check Point analyzed Model Context Protocols (MCPs) deployed by enterprises in 2025 and found 40% were vulnerable, signalling that the agentic AI tooling stack is becoming a first-class attack surface alongside traditional applications.
pageOrSection: AI as a Force Multiplier Across Cyber Attacks

title: 1 in 35 enterprise GenAI prompts risk a leak
description: Check Point's November 2025 telemetry, cited in the Cyber Security Report 2026, found that one in every 35 enterprise GenAI prompts carried a high risk of leaking sensitive data, with 22% of prompts containing sensitive information overall.
pageOrSection: AI as a Force Multiplier Across Cyber Attacks

title: 87% of GenAI-using organizations exposed
description: Among organizations actively using generative AI, 87% were affected by at least one high-risk prompt event in November 2025, and the average enterprise was running 11 different GenAI tools per month outside formal governance.
pageOrSection: AI as a Force Multiplier Across Cyber Attacks

title: Average org uses 11 GenAI tools per month
description: Check Point telemetry shows that the typical enterprise interacts with 11 different generative AI tools each month, most of them unsanctioned, creating sprawling shadow-AI footprints that defenders cannot consistently see or govern.
pageOrSection: AI as a Force Multiplier Across Cyber Attacks

title: AI is now embedded across the attack lifecycle
description: Check Point's framing of AI as both an enabler of attacker tradecraft and a direct source of enterprise risk anchors the 2026 report and is reflected across every other major trend it covers.
quote: "Artificial intelligence is now embedded across the attack lifecycle, accelerating the execution of familiar techniques at greater speed and scale."
pageOrSection: AI as a Force Multiplier Across Cyber Attacks

title: Weekly attacks per org climbed across 2025
description: Check Point ThreatCloud AI telemetry tracked the average weekly attacks per organization through 2025: ~1,925 in Q1, 1,984 in Q2, 2,003 in November and 2,027 in December. December's reading is up 9% year over year.
pageOrSection: Weekly Attacks per Organization – Quarterly and Monthly Telemetry

title: Q1 2025 attacks per org jumped 47% YoY
description: Check Point's Q1 2025 Global Cyber Attack Report — the first major data drop feeding the annual report — measured a 47% YoY surge in average weekly cyber attacks per organization, reaching roughly 1,925 attacks per week.
pageOrSection: Weekly Attacks per Organization – Quarterly and Monthly Telemetry

title: Q1 2025 ransomware attacks up 126% YoY
description: Publicly disclosed ransomware attacks rose 126% year over year in Q1 2025 according to Check Point's quarterly global cyber attack report, setting the tone for an entire year in which ransomware operations fragmented and accelerated.
pageOrSection: Ransomware Operations Become More Fragmented and Targeted

title: December 2025 ransomware up 60% YoY
description: Check Point recorded 945 publicly reported ransomware attacks in December 2025, a 60% increase versus December 2024, closing the year on the highest monthly disclosure volume Check Point had ever measured.
pageOrSection: Ransomware Operations Become More Fragmented and Targeted

title: Publicly disclosed ransomware attacks across 2025
description: Check Point's quarterly and monthly ransomware leak-site counts climbed steadily across 2025: ~1,600 incidents in Q2, 727 in November alone and 945 in December — illustrating that despite law enforcement takedowns, disclosures grew throughout the year.
pageOrSection: Ransomware Operations Become More Fragmented and Targeted

title: Ransomware disclosures concentrate in North America
description: Region share of publicly disclosed ransomware attacks tracked by Check Point Research stayed heavily tilted toward North America across 2025: 53% in Q2 vs 25% Europe, then 55% vs 18% in November, with the United States alone accounting for 52% of November incidents.
pageOrSection: Ransomware Operations Become More Fragmented and Targeted

title: Top ransomware groups – November 2025
description: By share of publicly disclosed ransomware attacks in November 2025, Qilin and Clop tied at 15% each, followed by Akira at 12%. The same Russian Qilin RaaS jumped to 18% of disclosures in December 2025, becoming the single most active group of the month.
pageOrSection: Ransomware Operations Become More Fragmented and Targeted

title: Qilin = 18% of December ransomware
description: Qilin, the Russian Ransomware-as-a-Service operator active since 2022, was responsible for 18% of all publicly disclosed ransomware attacks in December 2025 — making it the most active group of the month per Check Point Research.
pageOrSection: Ransomware Operations Become More Fragmented and Targeted

title: Ransomware-impacted business sectors – November 2025
description: Industrial Manufacturing led ransomware leak-site disclosures in November 2025 with 12% of victims, followed by Business Services at 11% and Consumer Goods & Services at 10%, reflecting attackers' continued focus on operationally sensitive industries.
pageOrSection: Ransomware Operations Become More Fragmented and Targeted

title: Education stayed #1 target all year
description: Education was the most-attacked industry in every 2025 reporting window feeding the annual report, averaging more than double the global weekly attack rate: 4,484 (Q1), 4,388 (Q2), 4,656 (Nov) and 4,349 (Dec) weekly attacks per organization.
pageOrSection: Industry / Sector Targeting (Weekly Attacks per Organization)

title: Weekly attacks per organization by industry – 2025
description: Side-by-side comparison of the most-attacked industries in Check Point's monthly and quarterly 2025 telemetry. Education stayed the runaway leader across Q1, Q2, November and December, while Government held a stable second place and Associations/Non-Profits surged late in the year.
comparison: Q1 vs Q2 vs Nov vs Dec 2025

title: Associations & Non-Profits +57% YoY

title: Education sector +31% YoY in Q2 2025
description: Education absorbed 4,388 weekly attacks per organization in Q2 2025 — a 31% jump versus Q2 2024. Check Point attributes the surge to underfunded defenses combined with the high black-market value of student and staff credentials.
pageOrSection: Industry / Sector Targeting (Weekly Attacks per Organization)

title: Regional weekly attacks per organization – November 2025
description: Latin America led every region in November 2025 with 3,048 weekly attacks per organization — a 17% YoY increase, the largest globally. Africa ran second at 2,696, although it actually fell 13% YoY as attention shifted to Latin America.

title: Regional YoY change in weekly attacks – November 2025
description: Year-over-year change in average weekly attacks per organization in November 2025: Latin America +17%, North America +9%, APAC -0.1%, Europe -1%, Africa -13%. Latin America registered the largest regional surge globally.

title: LATAM +26% YoY in December 2025
description: Latin America extended its lead in December 2025 with 3,065 weekly attacks per organization, a 26% year-over-year jump and the largest regional surge of any region tracked by Check Point Research — capping a year of accelerating attacks across the region.

title: Europe +22% YoY in Q2 2025
description: Europe posted the largest year-over-year increase of any region in Q2 2025 at 22%, despite not topping absolute volumes. Check Point attributes the rise to attackers exploiting geopolitical tensions, regulatory fragmentation and the region's concentration of high-value data.

title: Edge devices are the new initial-access pillar
description: Check Point Research positions routers, gateways and VPN appliances as the highest-yield foothold for both criminal and Chinese-nexus operators in 2025, citing limited monitoring and patching coverage as the structural driver.
quote: "Unmonitored devices played a growing role in intrusion activity, particularly in large-scale and targeted attacks."
pageOrSection: Unmonitored Devices as High-Value Initial Access Targets

title: Chinese-nexus operations are industrialized
description: Check Point characterizes 2025 Chinese-nexus activity as routine, edge-focused and global by design, with zero-day exploitation and one-day weaponization treated as standard operating procedure rather than exceptional tradecraft.
quote: "During 2025 the Chinese-nexus activity was global by design… Operations are industrialized, not opportunistic."

title: Cyber ops sync with geopolitical conflicts
description: Check Point flags 2025 as the year in which cyber espionage, disruption and influence campaigns moved in lockstep with kinetic events, with compromised IoT and surveillance systems repurposed to support physical-world operations.
pageOrSection: Cyber Activity Aligns More Closely with Geopolitical Conflicts

title: Ransomware fragments into smaller crews
description: Check Point's headline narrative for 2026 is that ransomware power is decentralizing — law-enforcement disruption of brands like LockBit and BlackCat has pushed the ecosystem toward smaller affiliates, data-only extortion and AI-accelerated negotiation timelines.
quote: "A shift away from centralized ransomware brands toward smaller, decentralized operators… increased use of data-only extortion without encryption."
pageOrSection: Ransomware Operations Become More Fragmented and Targeted

title: 22% of GenAI prompts contained sensitive data
description: Across enterprise tenants monitored by Check Point in November 2025, 22% of generative AI prompts contained sensitive information — credentials, source code, customer data or other regulated content — feeding the report's central thesis that ungoverned AI is now a measurable enterprise risk.
pageOrSection: AI as a Force Multiplier Across Cyber Attacks

title: United States = 52% of November ransomware
description: The United States alone accounted for 52% of all publicly reported ransomware incidents tracked by Check Point in November 2025, underscoring how concentrated North-American victims remain in extortion leak-site activity even as criminal operators decentralize.
pageOrSection: Ransomware Operations Become More Fragmented and Targeted

title: 1,600+ cybersecurity products published
description: In 2025, CISA published more than 1,600 cybersecurity products to support the nation's security with proactive guidance, advisories, and threat resources strengthening collective defense for systems Americans rely on daily.
pageOrSection: Introduction from CISA Acting Director Gottumukkala

title: 30,000+ incidents triaged at 24/7 operations center
description: CISA's 24/7 Operations Center triaged more than 30,000 incidents reported in 2025, delivering a proactive response posture that safeguards the systems Americans depend on every day.
pageOrSection: Introduction from CISA Acting Director Gottumukkala

title: 2M+ priority emergency calls connected
description: CISA connected more than 2 million priority calls for authorized users of its priority telecommunications capability, enabling essential personnel to communicate during emergencies, saving lives, critical infrastructure, and property.
pageOrSection: Introduction from CISA Acting Director Gottumukkala

title: Director on CISA's renewed mission focus
description: Acting Director Dr. Madhu Gottumukkala frames CISA's 2025 priorities around mission discipline and modernized operations to defend America's critical infrastructure from cyber and physical threats.
quote: "In 2025, CISA approached its mission with a renewed sense of purpose, focusing tightly on the agency's core mission: protecting America's critical infrastructure from cyber and physical threats."
pageOrSection: Introduction from CISA Acting Director Gottumukkala

title: Endpoint Detection and Response scale across federal agencies
description: CISA scaled Endpoint Detection and Response with Persistent Access Capability to more than 60 agencies covering over 500,000 endpoints, enabling near real-time detection and investigation of advanced persistent threats across the federal civilian network.
pageOrSection: Staying Ahead of the Threat - Endpoint Detection and Response Technology

title: Malicious connections blocked across federal and critical infrastructure networks
description: CISA blocked 2.62 billion malicious connections within the federal civilian network and an additional 371 million malicious connections within critical infrastructure, illustrating the vast scale of automated threats facing protected environments.
pageOrSection: Staying Ahead of the Threat - Endpoint Detection and Response Technology

title: 42 critical infrastructure partners in CyberSentry program
description: CISA expanded the CyberSentry Program to 42 voluntary critical infrastructure partners, delivering advanced threat detection and monitoring for networks supporting National Critical Functions.
pageOrSection: Staying Ahead of the Threat - Protecting National Critical Functions

title: 238 high-risk vulnerabilities added to KEV catalog
description: In FY 2025, CISA added 238 high-risk vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, helping federal agencies, state, local, tribal, and territorial governments, and private sector organizations identify and patch threats quickly.
