description: CISA assessed and scored more than 43,000 vulnerabilities using Stakeholder-Specific Vulnerability Categorization, translating complex technical data into clear, actionable priorities for IT defenders.
pageOrSection: Staying Ahead of the Threat - Known Exploited Vulnerabilities

title: Joint cybersecurity products published with partners
description: CISA published 42 joint cybersecurity products with federal partners in 2025, including 23 issued in collaboration with both federal and international partners, delivering actionable insights and technical guidance across the threat landscape.

title: Vulnerability Disclosure Policy Platform pipeline
description: Federal agencies participating in CISA's Vulnerability Disclosure Policy Platform received over 12,800 vulnerability reports from public security researchers, including over 1,200 valid reports, of which agencies remediated 1,099 (90%).
pageOrSection: Hardening the Terrain - Vulnerability Disclosure Policy Platform

title: 90% of valid VDP reports remediated
description: Of the over 1,200 valid vulnerability disclosure reports submitted via CISA's VDP Platform, 1,099 (90%) were remediated by participating federal agencies, evidencing strong follow-through with the security researcher community.
pageOrSection: Hardening the Terrain - Vulnerability Disclosure Policy Platform

title: $345K awarded across federal bug bounty programs
description: CISA supported four agencies running 7 bug bounty programs that identified 28 critical vulnerabilities, with over $345K in federal agency bounties awarded to researchers for their contributions.
pageOrSection: Hardening the Terrain - Vulnerability Disclosure Policy Platform

title: 25% reduction in red team cloud infrastructure cost
description: CISA's Red Team Capabilities team reduced overall cloud infrastructure costs by 25% in 2025 through strategic downsizing and optimization, freeing resources for higher-impact mission work.
pageOrSection: Hardening the Terrain - Proactive Assessments: Red Team Capabilities

title: Emergency Directive 25-02 Microsoft Exchange compliance
description: In response to CVE-2025-53786 in Microsoft Exchange hybrid configurations, CISA executed Emergency Directive 25-02. Of 557 in-scope devices across 47 agencies, 93% were running the latest cumulative update, illustrating rapid federal compliance.
pageOrSection: Real World Response - Microsoft Exchange Vulnerability

title: Cisco ASA Emergency Directive 25-03 remediation
description: During Operation THUNDERSTRUCK, a nation-state campaign targeting Cisco ASA edge devices, CISA issued Emergency Directive 25-03. 93% of more than 7,000 in-scope devices across 53 federal agencies were patched or disconnected within 54 days.

title: 148 cyber and physical security exercises
description: CISA conducted 148 cyber and physical security exercises with more than 10,000 participants in FY 2025, with 94% of participants reporting improved preparedness and 96% saying they would recommend similar exercises.

title: Participant feedback on CISA exercises
description: Among more than 10,000 participants in CISA's 148 cyber and physical security exercises, 94% reported improved preparedness and 96% said they would recommend similar exercises, validating the practical value of CISA-led drills.

title: FIFA World Cup full-scale exercise in Philadelphia
description: Ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, CISA convened 730+ participants from 40+ agencies at Lincoln Financial Field, producing 15 areas for improvement and 30 actionable recommendations to enhance coordination, communication, and public safety.
pageOrSection: Securing America - FIFA World Cup Preparations

title: Cybersecurity grant funding for SLTT entities
description: DHS released grant funding for the State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program ($91.7M to states and territories) and the Tribal Cybersecurity Grant Program ($12.6M to Tribal Governments), administered by FEMA with substantial CISA support.
pageOrSection: Securing America - Securing Communities - SLTT Cybersecurity Grants

title: Counter-IED training reach and effectiveness
description: CISA delivered 1,057 counter-improvised explosive device and risk mitigation training courses to more than 25,000 participants in 2025, with 94% reporting the training enhanced their preparedness.
pageOrSection: Securing America - Securing Communities - Protecting Communities from Explosives

title: Empowered Trainer Program multiplier
description: Through the Empowered Trainer Program, CISA sustained 118 active trainers across 53 organizations in 27 states, who delivered 376 counter-IED courses to 6,136 participants, multiplying CISA's community-resilience footprint.
pageOrSection: Securing America - Securing Communities - Protecting Communities from Explosives

title: Active shooter and conflict prevention training
description: CISA delivered 58 Active Shooter Preparedness webinars to over 14,000 registrants (93% will use the training in risk-based decisions) and 14 Conflict Prevention webinars to 7,200 registrants (87% expect improved prevention capabilities).

title: K-12 school safety program outputs
description: Through SchoolSafety.gov, CISA hosted 45 training events for over 10,000 school leaders, added 102 new resources, and promoted more than 80 funding opportunities in FY 2025 to create safer learning environments.
pageOrSection: Securing America - Securing Communities - Protecting K-12 Education

title: 2,500+ threat and incident reports shared with sectors
description: CISA shared more than 2,500 threat and incident reports with critical infrastructure sectors, coordinating intelligence across the federal government and strengthening resilience for food and agriculture, transportation, water, and other sectors.
pageOrSection: Securing America - Infrastructure and Cybersecurity Assessments

title: 400 infrastructure security assessments delivered
description: CISA delivered 400 infrastructure security assessments to stakeholders in 2025, identifying facility-level security measures, preparedness dependencies, and resilience recommendations for critical sites.
pageOrSection: Securing America - Infrastructure and Cybersecurity Assessments

title: 100+ atomic countermeasures in COUN7ER database
description: CISA's Adversary Eviction Strategies Tool launched in July 2025 includes COUN7ER, a database of 100+ atomic countermeasures mapped to MITRE ATT&CK and D3FEND, enabling defenders to generate customized incident response playbooks in minutes.
pageOrSection: Innovating to Fuel the Mission - Adversary Eviction Strategies Tool

title: Industry Engagement Platform first-month adoption
description: Launched December 4, 2025, CISA's Industry Engagement Platform approved 134 access requests, hosted 113 new organization profiles, and completed 16 capability briefings in its first month, helping CISA track market trends and innovation.
pageOrSection: Innovating to Fuel the Mission - Leaning into Industry

title: 54 agencies on Dashboard-as-a-Service
description: Through the Continuous Diagnostics and Mitigation Program, 54 agencies migrated to a Dashboard-as-a-Service model, lowering hosting costs and accelerating updates that improve federal end-users' cyber posture awareness.
pageOrSection: Modernizing to Scale Security and Shrink Costs - Continuous Diagnostics and Mitigation Program

title: On transparency in coordinated vulnerability disclosure
description: CISA frames its Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure Program as a transparency engine across IT, OT, ICS, medical devices, IoT, AI systems, operating systems, and open-source software.
quote: "By publicly sharing vulnerabilities and mitigation strategies, CISA helps owners and operators reduce risk and protect the systems Americans rely on every day."
pageOrSection: Hardening the Terrain - Vulnerability Disclosure Policy Platform

title: Fraudulent device registrations surge 178%
description: User-reported fraudulent MFA device registration events jumped 178% from 2024 to 2025, as attackers raced to register their own hardware as a trusted MFA factor and gain persistent, high-trust account access.
pageOrSection: Attacks against MFA — Device compromise attacks

title: Attackers target the person who holds the key
description: Talos' MITRE ATT&CK analysis of ransomware engagements crystallized 2025's defining theme: identity is the new perimeter, and threat actors are bypassing infrastructure entirely by hijacking valid users.
quote: "Actors predominately targeted the person who holds the key rather than the lock itself."

title: Network infrastructure as identity control point
description: Talos found attackers prioritized identity gateways — ADCs, VPNs, network management platforms — over individual devices, weaponizing the systems that broker trust to bypass MFA and traverse networks.
quote: "In 2025, the majority of attacker activity against network infrastructure focused on the systems that validate, enforce, or broker identity."

title: Speed of weaponization defines 2025
description: React2Shell, disclosed in December, became the #1 most-targeted CVE of 2025, illustrating near-instant weaponization that left defenders almost no patch window.
quote: "The speed of weaponization and the longevity of exposure are defining characteristics of today's threat landscape."

title: 40% of top-100 CVEs hit EOL devices
description: Nearly 40% of the 100 top-targeted vulnerabilities in 2025 directly impacted end-of-life devices — perimeter gear like VPN appliances and routers that organizations can no longer patch.

title: China-nexus investigations up 74%
description: Talos investigations into China-nexus campaigns increased nearly 74% in 2025 versus 2024, reflecting both the rising volume and growing operational sophistication of PRC-linked actors.

title: $1.5B Bybit crypto heist by North Korea
description: North Korean cyber actors pulled off the largest cryptocurrency heist in history in February 2025, stealing $1.5 billion in Ethereum from the Bybit exchange to fund weapons programs and counteract sanctions.

title: Phishing drove 40% of IR cases
description: Talos Incident Response observed phishing as the initial access vector in 40% of 2025 cases, with attackers commonly leveraging compromised internal or partner accounts to exploit trusted relationships.

title: Iranian hacktivism activity up 60%
description: Activity from the top Iranian hacktivist groups Talos tracks increased 60% in 2025, with collectives surging around Israel-Hamas escalations and U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear sites.

title: 75% of Q2 phishing cases used trusted accounts
description: In Q2 2025, a staggering 75% of phishing-based initial-access cases involved emails originating from already-compromised internal users or external business partners, exploiting established trust to bypass controls.

title: 80% of top-targeted CVEs are RCE
description: Remote code execution dominated Talos' top 100 dataset at 80%, the preferred class for both APTs and commodity botnets because it bypasses identity controls, scales via automation, and works on segmented networks.

title: Top 100 vulnerabilities by type
description: Remote code execution overwhelms every other vulnerability class in Talos' top 100 dataset, with authentication bypass a distant second — a profile tailor-made for automated mass exploitation.

title: CVE age distribution
description: Despite headlines around React2Shell and ToolShell, only 15% of the top 100 CVEs are 0–2 years old; a full third are at least 10+ years old, underscoring how patch-management debt fuels modern intrusions.

title: Network infrastructure vulnerability scope
description: Device-specific firmware dominates by volume (66%), but the high-leverage classes — platform software, embedded services, and management plane — together account for one-third of CVEs and produce outsized blast radius.
pageOrSection: Top-targeted vulnerabilities — Vulnerability scope and risk

title: Ransomware data-leak posts by group
description: Qilin led 2025 with 17% of all data-leak site posts, while Akira (10%) and Play (6%) demonstrated rare second-year longevity. LockBit 3.0 collapsed from #1 to #35 after Operation Cronos.

title: Qilin affiliates take home up to 85%
description: Qilin's RaaS model pays affiliates 80–85% of the ransom — well above typical industry splits — helping fuel its rise to the most active ransomware operation in 2025.

title: Application types targeted in MFA attacks
description: Identity and access management apps absorbed 30% of all MFA spray attacks in 2025 (up 6 points from 2024), as attackers concentrated on SSO and conditional-access flows that unlock the entire estate.
pageOrSection: Attacks against MFA — MFA spray attacks

title: MFA spray targeting shifts, 2024 vs 2025
description: Attackers piled into IAM (+6pts), PAM (+3pts), and operating system (+2pts) MFA spray targets while pulling back from legacy app delivery (-4pts) and remote access (-3pts) as orgs migrated VPN to cloud identity.
pageOrSection: Attacks against MFA — MFA spray attacks

title: Top access vectors in device-compromise attacks
description: Administrator-managed registration accounted for 77% of fraudulent device-compromise events, a 3:1 dominance over user flows that points squarely at vishing of IT help desks as the primary playbook.
pageOrSection: Attacks against MFA — Device compromise attacks

title: MFA spray attacks by industry
description: Technology dominated MFA spray targeting at 36%, with manufacturing a distant second — both industries offering the predictable, uniform identity environments that automated credential guessing thrives on.

title: Device-compromise attacks by industry
description: Higher education ranked #1 for device-compromise attacks at 24% — a stark inverse of MFA spray patterns, driven by heterogeneous BYOD ecosystems and lax registration controls.

title: Ransomware activity by month
description: January was the lowest-volume month two years running, likely reflecting Eastern European Orthodox-Christmas holidays. Activity peaked in spring and again in October, giving defenders a clear seasonal test window.

title: Qilin: 40+ victims every month except January
description: Qilin's double-extortion machine claimed more than 40 victims every month of 2025 except January, signaling the group will remain a structural threat heading into 2026.

title: Top ransomware-targeted industries
description: Manufacturing remained the most-targeted ransomware sector for a third consecutive year, driven by low downtime tolerance and hybrid IT/OT attack surfaces. Professional services and wholesale trade follow.

title: 35% of phishing cases used internal phishing
description: Once inside, attackers continued the lure: 35% of 2025 Talos IR phishing cases involved internal phishing from compromised accounts, used to clone MFA tokens, harvest credentials, and deploy malware deeper.

title: North Korea's Contagious Interview at scale
description: Famous Chollima's fake-recruiter campaign spread through the npm ecosystem: 338+ malicious packages, 50,000+ downloads, and 180+ AI-built personas behind hundreds of confirmed victims.

title: Chinese hackers-for-hire: $10K–$75K per inbox
description: The March 2025 i-Soon indictment revealed Chinese cybercriminals charging $10,000 to $75,000 per compromised email account, blurring the line between state espionage and commercial intrusion services.

title: Russian cyber activity 4x in May
description: May's Western sanctions spike coincided with a fourfold increase in observed Russian cyber activity, confirming that geopolitical pressure remains a leading indicator for heightened APT operations.

title: Vishing of admins outpaced user fraud 3:1
description: In device-compromise attacks, attackers targeted the admin-managed registration flow at a 3-to-1 rate over user-managed registration, leaning heavily on voice phishing of overworked help desks.
pageOrSection: Attacks against MFA — Device compromise attacks

title: 22% of top network CVEs hit ADCs
description: Application delivery controllers like Citrix ADC and F5 BIG-IP accounted for 22% of the top 50 targeted network devices — compromise of one ADC can expose dozens of downstream apps via SAML/OAuth flows.

title: Record-setting DDoS peak in Q4 2025
description: Cloudflare mitigated a record 31.4 Tbps DDoS attack during Q4 2025, the largest publicly disclosed DDoS attack to date. The assault lasted only 35 seconds but defined the year's escalation in attack scale.
comparison: new record vs. prior public peaks

title: Total DDoS attacks mitigated in 2025
description: Cloudflare mitigated 47.1 million DDoS attacks across 2025, more than doubling year over year. This represents a 121% surge versus 2024 and a 236% increase since 2023.

title: Average DDoS attacks mitigated per hour (2025)
description: Cloudflare's autonomous systems mitigated 5,376 DDoS attacks every hour on average across 2025, split between network-layer (L3/4) and HTTP-layer (L7) traffic. Network-layer attacks dominate the hourly mix.

title: Network-layer DDoS attacks tripled in 2025
description: Network-layer (L3/4) DDoS attacks rose from 11.4 million in 2024 to 34.4 million in 2025, more than tripling year over year. The category drove most of the year's overall growth.

title: Network-layer share of Q4 DDoS incidents
description: In Q4 2025, network-layer (L3/4) attacks made up 78% of all DDoS incidents Cloudflare mitigated, with HTTP DDoS attacks comprising the remainder.

title: Q4 2025 DDoS attack growth vs Q3
description: Total DDoS attack volume rose 31% from Q3 to Q4 2025, and was 58% higher than the equivalent Q4 in 2024, marking sustained quarterly escalation.

title: Hyper-volumetric attack size growth since late 2024
description: The size of hyper-volumetric DDoS attacks ballooned more than 700% in 2025 compared with the largest attacks observed in late 2024, with Q4 alone adding a 40% jump over Q3.

title: Peak HTTP DDoS rate during Q4 campaign
description: The Aisuru-Kimwolf 'Night Before Christmas' campaign drove peak HTTP DDoS rates of 205 million requests per second — Cloudflare compares this to the combined populations of the UK, Germany and Spain all hitting Enter simultaneously.

title: 'Night Before Christmas' hyper-volumetric attack mix
description: Starting December 19, 2025, the Aisuru-Kimwolf botnet launched 902 hyper-volumetric DDoS incidents averaging 53 per day, split across packet-, bit-, and request-intensive vectors.

title: Aisuru-Kimwolf campaign: average vs peak attack size
description: Across the Q4 hyper-volumetric campaign, average attack sizes reached 4 Tbps, 3 Bpps and 54 Mrps, while peaks hit 24 Tbps, 9 Bpps and 205 Mrps. Bit-rate values normalized to Tbps for visualization.

title: Aisuru-Kimwolf botnet size
description: The Aisuru-Kimwolf botnet powering the Q4 hyper-volumetric campaign is estimated at 1 to 4 million compromised Android TV devices distributed worldwide.

title: Q1 2025 18-day network-layer campaign targets
description: An 18-day Q1 2025 multi-vector campaign generated 13.5 million attacks, divided between Magic Transit customers (6.9M) and Cloudflare's own infrastructure (6.6M). Vectors included SYN floods, Mirai-generated attacks and SSDP amplification.

title: Top targeted industries in Q4 2025
description: Telecommunications and Service Providers became the most-attacked industry in Q4 2025, displacing IT & Services. Gambling, Gaming, Computer Software and Business Services round out the top six.

title: Top 10 most-attacked locations in Q4 2025
description: China remained the top targeted location in Q4 2025, with Hong Kong jumping 12 spots to #2 and the UK leaping 36 places to #6. Values are inverse rank (11 minus rank) so taller bars represent more-attacked locations.

title: Top 10 attack source countries in Q4 2025
description: Bangladesh dethroned Indonesia as the top DDoS source country in Q4 2025, while Argentina jumped 20 spots to #4. Values are inverse rank so taller bars represent larger attack origination.

title: Top 5 attack source ASNs in Q4 2025
description: Cloud computing platforms dominated DDoS origination in Q4 2025. DigitalOcean led, followed by Microsoft, Tencent, Oracle and Hetzner — underlining cloud abuse as a primary attack pipeline.

title: Duration of the record 31.4 Tbps attack
description: The record 31.4 Tbps Q4 2025 DDoS attack lasted just 35 seconds, illustrating the trend toward extremely high-intensity, short-duration hyper-volumetric assaults.

title: Hourly DDoS mitigation rate growth
description: Cloudflare's average hourly DDoS mitigation rate climbed steadily through 2025, finishing at 5,376 attacks blocked every hour. The sparkline traces an approximate quarterly progression.

title: DDoS attack growth since 2023
description: Cloudflare's mitigated DDoS attacks have grown 236% since 2023, reflecting both a larger Internet footprint and increasingly aggressive botnet activity led by Mirai-class and Aisuru-Kimwolf variants.

title: Networks subscribed to Cloudflare's DDoS Botnet Threat Feed
description: Over 800 networks worldwide have adopted Cloudflare's free DDoS Botnet Threat Feed for Service Providers, using it to identify and take down abusive IPs and compromised accounts upstream.

title: On the scale of a 205 Mrps assault
description: Cloudflare's analogy for the peak HTTP DDoS rate underscores the human scale of hyper-volumetric Layer 7 attacks driven by the Aisuru-Kimwolf botnet.
quote: "The scale of a 205 Mrps DDoS attack is comparable to the combined populations of the UK, Germany, and Spain all simultaneously typing a website address and hitting 'enter' at the same second."

title: Network-layer attacks 'more than tripled'
description: Cloudforce One's framing of 2025's defining network-layer trend captures the shift from incremental growth to multi-fold escalation.
quote: "Network-layer attacks experienced the most substantial growth, more than tripled year over year, reaching 34.4 million incidents compared to 11.4 million in 2024."

title: Hyper-volumetric attack QoQ growth in Q4
description: Hyper-volumetric DDoS incidents rose 40% from Q3 to Q4 2025, capping a year of record-setting attack scale led by the Aisuru-Kimwolf botnet.

title: Global internet traffic grew 19% in 2025
description: Cloudflare measured a 19% year-over-year increase in global Internet traffic across 2025, accelerating roughly 10% faster than 2024's 17% rate. Most of the growth materialized after mid-April, with significant acceleration starting in August.

title: Almost half of major outages were government-directed shutdowns
description: Cloudflare's headline narrative on 2025 connectivity disruptions emphasizes how state-imposed shutdowns drove nearly half of the 174 major outages observed worldwide.
quote: "Almost half of the 174 major Internet outages observed around the world in 2025 were due to government-directed regional and national shutdowns."

title: 6% of global traffic was mitigated by Cloudflare
description: Cloudflare's systems mitigated 6% of global traffic across its network in 2025, either as potentially malicious or for customer-defined reasons. This represents a small decrease from 6.2% in 2024, while DDoS/WAF mitigations grew slightly to 3.3%.

title: Record 31.4 Tbps DDoS attack in November
description: Hyper-volumetric DDoS attack sizes grew dramatically throughout 2025, culminating in a record 31.4 Tbps attack in November. Cloudflare observed its first >10 Tbps attack in late August, multiple >20 Tbps attacks in September, and a 29.7 Tbps attack in October.

title: Over 5% of email messages were malicious
description: Cloudflare's email security analysis classified more than 5% of analyzed messages as malicious in 2025. Deceptive links emerged as the most common threat type, followed by identity deception and brand impersonation.

title: Post-quantum encryption surged to 52% of human web traffic
description: The share of human-generated web traffic protected by post-quantum encryption nearly doubled to 52% in 2025, up from 29% at the start of the year. Apple's iOS 26 release in September drove a step-change in adoption.

title: AI 'user action' crawling grew 15x in 2025
description: AI user-action crawling, driven primarily by OpenAI's ChatGPT-User bot, increased more than 15x throughout 2025. Request volumes peaked roughly 16x higher than year-start levels.

title: Anthropic's crawl-to-refer ratio hit 500,000:1
description: Anthropic recorded the highest crawl-to-refer ratio among major AI and search platforms in 2025, reaching as high as 500,000:1. Perplexity, by contrast, maintained the lowest ratios, staying below 400:1 after September.

title: 40% of global bot traffic originated in the United States
description: The United States dominated bot traffic origin in 2025 with 40% share, followed by Germany at 6.5%. AWS and Google Cloud combined accounted for roughly a quarter of all global bot traffic.

title: Bot traffic origin by cloud provider, 2024 vs 2025
description: Cloud platforms continued to be major sources of bot traffic in 2025. AWS led with 14.4% (combined across two ASes), Google Cloud reached 9.7%, and Microsoft Azure rose to 5.5% — all three increased compared to 2024.

title: Share of verified bot traffic by crawler
description: Googlebot dominated verified bot traffic in 2025, accounting for over 28% of all verified bot activity. OpenAI's GPTBot reached approximately 7.5% and Microsoft's Bingbot held around 6%.

title: HTTP version distribution of global web requests
description: HTTP/2 remained the dominant protocol version at 50% of global web requests in 2025, with HTTP/3 reaching 21% and legacy HTTP/1.x at 29%. The shares of HTTP/3 and HTTP/2 both increased slightly during the year.
comparison: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 both slightly up YoY

title: IPv6 adoption: top countries vs global
description: India led IPv6 adoption with 67% of dual-stack requests using IPv6, while the global average was 29%. Only Malaysia, Saudi Arabia, and Uruguay also exceeded 50%, and 94 countries remained below 10%.

title: RPKI valid routes: start vs end of 2025
description: Routing security improved across the board in 2025. IPv4 valid routes increased from 50% to 53.9% and IPv6 valid routes climbed 4.7 percentage points to 60.1%. IPv4 routes and address space coverage have grown approximately 3x since 2020.

title: iOS vs Android share of mobile device traffic
description: Globally, iOS generated 35% of mobile device traffic in 2025, with Android at 65%. Country leaders diverged sharply: Monaco hit 70% iOS share while Papua New Guinea registered 97% Android.

title: Global search engine referral share
description: Google retained dominant search referral share globally at approximately 90% in 2025, with Bing, Yandex, Baidu, and DuckDuckGo distant followers. Russia remained the outlier, where Yandex captured 65% versus Google's 34%.

title: API client language share, 2024 vs 2025
description: API client traffic composition shifted significantly in 2025. Go-based clients climbed from 12% to 20%, Python rose from 9.6% to 17%, and Java from 7.4% to 11.2%. Node.js fell from its prior second-place position to 8.3%.

title: Top Workers AI models by account share
description: Meta's llama-3-8b-instruct was the most-used model on Workers AI in 2025, capturing 36.3% of accounts. OpenAI's whisper followed at 10.1% and Stability AI's stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0 at 9.8%.

title: Top countries by average download speed
description: European countries dominated download performance in 2025. Spain and Hungary both exceeded 300 Mbps average download speeds, with Portugal, Denmark, Romania, and France all above 200 Mbps.

title: Lowest idle latency by country
description: Iceland recorded the lowest idle latency at 13 ms in 2025, followed by Moldova at 15 ms. Portugal, Spain, and Hungary all stayed below 20 ms.

title: Major internet outage causes in 2025
description: Of 174 major internet outages tracked by Cloudflare in 2025, government-directed shutdowns accounted for roughly half (~87), followed by cable cuts, equipment failures (notably a Cairo telecom fire), and weather events such as Hurricane Melissa in Jamaica.

title: Hyper-volumetric DDoS attacks (>1 Tbps) by month
description: Cloudflare observed more than 500 attacks above 1 Tbps in July, the year's peak. February had the fewest (~150), and the largest individual attacks scaled up dramatically: 10 Tbps (Aug), 20+ Tbps (Sep), 29.7 Tbps (Oct), 31.4 Tbps (Nov).

title: WordPress holds 47% of CMS share
description: WordPress remained the dominant content management system in 2025 with 47% share of CMS-using sites, though this represents a continued decline from previous years as alternative platforms gain ground.

title: Almost all .christmas and .lol email was spam or malicious
description: Cloudflare singled out two TLDs as near-total vectors for unwanted email — both .christmas and .lol domains delivered email that was almost entirely spam or malicious during 2025.
quote: "Nearly all of the email messages from the .christmas and .lol Top Level Domains were found to be either spam or malicious."

title: 'People and Society' became 2025's most-attacked vertical
description: Organizations in the 'People and Society' vertical absorbed 4.4% of global mitigated traffic in 2025, peaking at 23.2% in early July. Gambling/Games, the prior year's leader, fell over 50% to 2.6%.

title: Active Insurance delivers YoY claims stability
description: Coalition's executive summary frames 2024 as a year of remarkable year-over-year stability in cyber claims despite an ever-changing threat landscape, attributing the result to its Active Insurance model.
quote: "In 2024, despite this ever-changing landscape, we observed remarkable year-over-year (YoY) stability, a clear testament to the power of Active Insurance."

title: Coalition policyholders see 73% fewer claims than industry
description: Coalition policyholders experience 73% fewer claims than the industry average, based on NAIC 2023 standalone cyber claims-frequency data compared against Coalition's own policyholder data.

title: Global claims frequency fell 7% YoY in 2024
description: Global cyber claims frequency decreased 7% year-over-year in 2024 to 1.48%, with a notable dip in the second half. US frequency (1.54%) was higher than the global average, while Canada (1.13%) and the UK (1.09%) were lower.

title: Average global claims severity reached $115K
description: Global claims severity remained essentially flat YoY in 2024 with an average loss of $115,000. Severity in Canada was nearly double ($226K), while the UK was significantly lower ($35K). Ransomware was the leading severity driver across regions.

title: 56% of matters handled without policyholder out-of-pocket cost
description: 56% of all matters reported to Coalition in 2024 were handled without any out-of-pocket payments by the policyholder, illustrating how proactive engagement reduces financial burden on businesses.

title: Global claims frequency trend (H1 2022 to H2 2024)
description: Half-year global claims frequency from H1 2022 through H2 2024 shows a peak in H1 2023 and a steady decline through the second half of 2024 to 1.41%.

title: Global claims severity trend (H1 2022 to H2 2024)
description: Average loss per claim across half-year periods from H1 2022 through H2 2024 shows a peak in H1 2022 ($123,990) and a notable drop in H2 2024 to $84,738.

title: Claims by event type, 2024
description: Breakdown of Coalition cyber insurance claims by event type in 2024. BEC and FTF together account for nearly 60% of all claims, while ransomware represents 21.1%.

title: BEC and FTF accounted for 60% of all claims
description: Email-based attacks dominated Coalition's 2024 claims data: business email compromise (BEC) and funds transfer fraud (FTF) together represented 60% of all cyber insurance claims, a trend that has persisted for three years.

title: Claims frequency by industry, 2024
description: Consumer staples (2.60%) and materials (2.20%) experienced the highest claims frequency among Coalition policyholders in 2024, while real estate (1.02%) saw the lowest.

title: Claims severity by industry, 2024
description: Energy ($292,193) had by far the highest average claims severity, more than 1,200% higher YoY due to volatility in H1 2024. Nonprofit ($73,498) had the lowest. Healthcare severity rose 32% YoY to $144,662.

title: Claims frequency by revenue segment, 2024
description: Larger businesses experience claims more often: $100M+ revenue segment hit 5.97% frequency in 2024, vs 3.99% for $25M-$100M and 1.07% for sub-$25M businesses. Frequency declined YoY across every segment.

title: Claims severity by revenue segment, 2024
description: Average loss per claim by revenue band: sub-$25M businesses lost $79K on average (-8% YoY), $25M-$100M lost $139K (-1% YoY), and $100M+ businesses lost $228K (+21% YoY).

title: BEC average loss jumped 23% YoY to $35K
description: BEC claims severity increased 23% YoY to an average loss of $35,000 in 2024, driven by a spike in the second half. Higher legal expenses, incident response, data mining, and notifications contributed to the increase.

title: BEC claims severity trend (H1 2022 to H2 2024)
description: BEC severity per half-year across three years. After dropping into the low $20Ks in H1 and H2 2023, BEC severity climbed back to $44,497 in H2 2024.

title: 29% of BEC events escalated into FTF
description: Across all BEC events in 2024, 29% resulted in a funds transfer fraud event with an average loss of $106,000, illustrating how email compromises frequently cascade into direct financial theft.

title: FTF initial severity fell 46% YoY to $185K
description: FTF initial claims severity (excluding clawbacks) decreased 46% YoY in 2024 to an average loss of $185,000, following an all-time high in 2023 when full-year FTF initial severity topped $340,000.

title: Coalition clawed back $31M in stolen funds in 2024
description: Coalition's cooperative efforts with authorities and panel partners contributed to the successful clawback of $31 million in 2024, with an average recovery of $278,000 per FTF event.

title: FTF recovery outcomes, 2024
description: Among Coalition-reported FTF events in 2024, 24% saw at least a partial recovery and 12% achieved a full recovery of the stolen funds, demonstrating the impact of rapid intervention.

title: Ransomware severity averaged $292K, down 7% YoY
description: Ransomware claims severity decreased 7% YoY in 2024 to an average loss of $292,000, well below the 2023 high of $393,000. Severity in Canada was more than double the global average ($665K), while the UK was significantly lower ($82K).

title: Ransomware claims severity trend (H1 2022 to H2 2024)
description: Half-year ransomware severity from H1 2022 through H2 2024 peaked at $393,245 in H1 2023 then declined to $249,902 in H2 2024 as ransom demands eased.

title: Initial ransom demands fell 22% YoY to $1.1M
description: Initial ransom demands fell 22% YoY in 2024 to an average of $1.1 million. Notably, the average demand in the second half of 2024 dropped below $1 million for the first time in more than two years.

title: Initial ransom demand trend (H1 2022 to H2 2024)
description: Average initial ransom demand per half-year from H1 2022 through H2 2024 peaked at over $1.52M in H1 2022 and dropped to $932,714 in H2 2024, the first sub-$1M half in more than two years.

title: Coalition negotiated 60% average reduction in ransom
description: When 44% of policyholders opted to pay the ransom in 2024, Coalition Incident Response engaged threat actors directly and on average negotiated a 60% reduction relative to the initial demand.

title: Top ransomware variants among Coalition claims, 2024
description: Akira (13.4%) was the most prevalent ransomware variant among Coalition policyholders in 2024, followed by Play (6.2%) and MedusaLocker (5.7%). Black Basta accounted for just 2.6% of claims but had the highest average demand at $4 million.

title: Drivers of ransomware loss beyond the ransom
description: Beyond ransom payments, the largest ransomware loss drivers are business interruption ($102K average), forensic vendor costs ($58K), and digital asset restoration ($18K). Business interruption figures are based on 2023 claims data due to development time.

title: 52% of misc. first-party losses stem from third-party breach
description: Among all miscellaneous first-party loss claims in 2024, 52% were caused by a third-party breach where a policyholder's vendor or partner was compromised. The average severity of a third-party breach was $42,000.

title: Risk aggregation event severity, 2024
description: Two notable third-party risk aggregation events drove cascading losses in 2024. Coalition policyholders impacted by the CDK Global ransomware attack experienced average severity of $63,000, vs $22,000 for those affected by Change Healthcare.

title: Active Insurance impact: alerts and avoided losses, 2024
description: Coalition issued 85,000+ security alerts in 2024 that helped resolve 32,000+ security issues. Conversely, 614 businesses that declined to remediate critical issues went on to suffer ransomware attacks with estimated losses of $307 million.

labels: Businesses attacked after refusing to fix issues

title: Coalition: prevention must be prioritized over reaction
description: Coalition's closing message in the executive summary stresses that proactive cyber risk management, not reactive response, will define the winners in the next era of cyber insurance.
quote: "Prevention must be prioritized over reaction. The companies that embrace continuous cybersecurity improvements, strategic risk management, and early threat detection will be best positioned to withstand future attacks."

title: 107.1B identity records exposed in 2024
description: Constella's threat intelligence team identified more than 107.1 billion exposed records circulating across the deep and dark web in 2024, drawn from 219K breach events. Records grew 55.72% year-over-year, underscoring the industrialization of identity compromise.

title: 219K breach events tracked in 2024
description: Constella hunted down more than 219,000 breach events in 2024, a 45.10% increase over 2023. The volume reflects both genuine new compromises and re-circulated combo lists across underground markets.

title: 30M infostealer device logs circulating
description: Constella's telemetry observed over 30 million infostealer device logs circulating on dark web marketplaces in the past year. Each log can contain saved credentials, session cookies, autofill data, system info, and screenshots from a single infected machine.
pageOrSection: Infostealers Now Mass-Harvest Identities at Scale

title: 99.33% of breaches expose PII
description: Personally identifiable information appeared in 99.33% of 2024 breaches, up from 96.6% the year prior. Nearly every breach now leaks names, phone numbers, addresses, birthdates, SSNs, or credit card data alongside credentials.
pageOrSection: Identity Breach Impact Goes Far Beyond IT

title: 95.29% of breaches contain plaintext passwords
description: Plaintext passwords appeared in 95.29% of breaches Constella analyzed in 2024, up from 70.99% in 2023 — a 24+ percentage point jump. The vast majority of stolen passwords are now immediately exploitable without cracking.

title: 27% of executive attacks involved deepfakes
description: An increasingly common element of executive-targeting campaigns is AI-driven impersonation: 27% of attacks on execs involved deepfakes. With as little as 16 seconds of audio, attackers can clone voices to deceive employees, investors, and partners.

title: $364.86M in 2024 data-breach losses
description: The FBI's 2024 Internet Crime Report tallied $364,855,818 in losses attributed to data breaches, ranking 8th of 26 crime categories by dollar value despite ranking 19th in complaint volume. Identity-driven crime is small in count but huge in financial impact.

title: Attackers log in, they don't hack in
description: Constella frames 2024 as the year credentials became the new perimeter. With over a billion identity records exposed via breaches and infostealers, the cost of buying valid logins outpaced the effort of breaking in.
quote: "Credentials are the new perimeter, and they're under attack. Attackers no longer break in, they log in."
pageOrSection: Identity is the New Attack Surface

title: Fewer breaches, far greater damage
description: The Identity Theft Resource Center, cited by Constella, observes that reported breach counts plateaued in 2024 while the scale of records exposed per incident exploded. Breach severity, not breach count, is the more meaningful signal.
quote: "Fewer breaches, but far greater damage. It's no longer about how many breaches occur, but how extensive their reach is."

title: Defenders must move to agentic AI
description: Constella COO/CISO Andres Andreu argues that reactive security models can't keep pace with adversaries already leveraging AI to automate vulnerability discovery and campaign delivery. Agentic AI must shift defenders from reaction to proactive neutralization.
quote: "Defenders must move from adaptive or reactive models to models of agentic AI that proactively neutralizes threats."

title: Records exposed YoY surge
description: Constella's records-exposed counter climbed sharply through 2024, ending at 107.1B with a 55.72% year-over-year growth rate. The sparkline approximates the cumulative quarterly ramp.

title: FBI data-breach complaints trend
description: FBI IC3 data-breach complaints more than doubled from 2021 to 2023 then plateaued in 2024. The trajectory: 1,287 (2021), 2,795 (2022), 3,727 (2023), 3,204 (2024) — staying elevated despite a slight retreat.

title: Combo-list share of breach intake
description: Credential compilations rose from 43% of Constella-ingested breaches in 2023 to 60% in 2024. Only 7.4% of breaches in Constella's data lake represent truly unique events — the rest is recycled material.

title: Top breaches by records exposed (2024)
description: The largest 2024 breaches Constella tracked were tencent.com (668M) and National Public Data (647M), then a steep drop to 1win.com (195M). Nine breaches surpassed 75M records vs seven in 2023.

title: Top PII attributes exposed in breaches
description: Emails (54.16%) and passwords (38.89%) remained the most frequently exposed data types in 2024 breaches, followed by phone numbers (35.33%) and usernames (23.58%). Birthdates, SSNs, and credit card numbers continue to leak at material rates.

title: Sensitive PII record counts (2024)
description: 2024 breaches exposed over 4.2B phone numbers, 2.9B addresses/cities, and 2B full names, alongside 1.05B birthdates, 519M SSNs, and 225M credit card numbers. The composition shows how identity kits are assembled from many sources.

title: Countries most impacted by breaches (2024)
description: The U.S. accounted for 25.47% of breaches, nearly doubling from 13.9% in 2023. Russia and Germany rounded out the top three. Indicates a continued concentration of victim entities in North America and Europe.

title: Breach distribution by continent (2024)
description: Continent-level distribution of 2024 breaches: North America (40.88%) leads, followed by Asia (28.89%) and Europe (22.34%). South America, Oceania, and Africa together account for under 8%.

title: Sectors most impacted by breaches
description: Email providers surged to 22.17% of breaches (+16.34 pp YoY), eclipsing all other sectors as adversaries target identity gateways. Retail, services, and news segments shrank meaningfully year over year.

title: Top compromised webmail domains
description: Gmail led 2024 webmail compromise with 3.1B accounts exposed, followed by hotmail.com (1.45B) and yahoo.com (1.38B). Russian services (mail.ru, yandex.ru) appear prominently, signalling geopolitically motivated credential harvesting.

title: Top detected password algorithms in breaches
description: Plaintext dominated 2024 with 95.29% prevalence; MySQL323 (74.61%) and MD2 (41.57%) — both legacy/weak — also appeared at alarming rates. Several breaches contain multiple algorithms, so percentages don't sum to 100%.

title: FBI 2024 cybercrime complaints by type
description: From 859,532 FBI IC3 complaints in 2024, phishing/spoofing (193,407) and extortion (86,415) led by volume, with personal data breach (64,882) third. Identity-relevant categories dominate the complaint mix.

title: FBI 2024 cybercrime losses by category
description: Investment fraud ($6.57B) and BEC ($2.77B) dwarfed other 2024 FBI IC3 loss categories. Data breach ($364.86M) ranked 8/26 in dollar value despite ranking 19/26 in complaint volume.

title: Top social media attributes exposed
description: Of 2024 social-media-related breach records, Facebook profiles dominated at 49.7%, with Twitter (14%), LinkedIn (13.6%), ICQ (3.9%), and other platforms trailing. Threat actors use these profiles for impersonation and reconnaissance.

title: Combo breaches vs unique breaches (2024)
description: Combo breaches (recompiled/recycled lists) made up 88.98% of 2024 breach intake versus 11.02% genuinely unique breaches. Only 7.4% of Constella's lake represents truly novel breach events; the rest is recycled content.

title: Executive targeting indicators (2024)
description: A 2024 GetApp survey shows 72% of cybersecurity pros observed senior executives being targeted recently, 54% of U.S. companies had an identity-fraud incident affecting an executive, and 27% of those attacks involved deepfakes.

title: 417K North American employees in infostealer logs
description: Constella's 2024 data identified over 417,000 North American employees and approximately 15,000 Asia-based employees with identities surfaced in infostealer logs, including high-privilege executive domains.

title: +84% phishing campaigns deliver infostealers (YoY)
description: IBM reported an 84% year-over-year increase in phishing campaigns that deliver infostealer malware, cited by Constella. Email threats have shifted heavily toward dropping stealers to harvest credentials at scale.

title: 78% of recently breached companies had infostealer logs
description: Of 50 recently breached companies studied, 78% had corporate credentials surface in infostealer logs within the six-month window around their breach. Infostealer infections are increasingly the precursor to enterprise compromise.

title: 165 companies hit via Snowflake identity chain
description: The UNC5537 campaign used infostealer-harvested credentials to access data belonging to roughly 165 Snowflake customer tenants in 2024. Constella highlights it as the textbook supply chain identity compromise.

title: Ransom payment rate hits new historical low
description: Only roughly 20% of ransomware victims paid a ransom in Q4 2025, the lowest share Coveware has recorded. The drop extends a multi-year downward trajectory observed since 2020, as improved backups and recovery planning let more organizations restore operations without engaging attackers.

title: Median ransom payment jumps 132% QoQ
description: The median ransom payment rose to $325,000 in Q4 2025, a 132% increase from Q3 2025. The spike reflects fewer but larger settlements concentrated on cases involving encryption-related operational disruption rather than data-exfiltration pressure.

title: Average ransom payment climbs to $591,988
description: Coveware's average ransom payment reached $591,988 in Q4 2025, up 57% from Q3 2025. The divergence from the median underscores skewed economics, with a small number of outsized settlements pulling the mean upward.

title: Data exfiltration-only payment rate stuck at ~25%
description: Even in cases without encryption, only about a quarter of victims paid in Q4 2025. Coveware notes this rate is structurally low and demonstrates that pure data-exfiltration extortion continues to convert poorly for threat actors.

title: Median victim shrinks to 200 employees
description: The median size of organizations impacted dropped 45% from Q3 2025 to just 200 employees. Coveware says ransomware actors continue to skew toward smaller, operationally constrained targets where downtime pressure is acute and defenses thinner.

title: Lateral movement observed in 65% of incidents
description: Lateral Movement (MITRE ATT&CK TA0008) was the most frequently observed tactic in Q4 2025 cases, appearing in 65% of intrusions. The dominance underscores how readily attackers expand from initial footholds once inside.

title: Exfiltration confirmed in 94% of cases overall
description: Data exfiltration was confirmed in 94% of all Coveware-handled incidents in Q4 2025, including 62% of cases where encryption was also present. The number reflects quieter, faster theft methods and the entrenchment of extortion-only pressure models.

title: DXF-only extortion is a legal problem, not a negotiation
description: Coveware reframes data-exfiltration-only extortion as something to be managed through legal, regulatory, and communications planning rather than ransom negotiation. The framing captures the report's central strategic conclusion for Q4 2025.
quote: "DXF-only extortion is best managed as a legal, regulatory, and communications challenge, not a negotiation problem."

title: Attackers operating within controls, not breaking them
description: Coveware highlights that remote access compromise dominates Q4 2025 entry vectors because adversaries are abusing legitimate provisioning, OAuth, and delegated-trust workflows. This shifts the defensive challenge from prevention of intrusion to scrutiny of granted access.
quote: "Attackers are not breaking controls so much as operating within them: logging in, being provisioned, or inheriting access through workflows designed for legitimate use."

title: Top ransomware variants by market share
description: Akira (14%) and Qilin (13%) led Coveware's Q4 2025 variant rankings, with the encryption-focused groups outperforming exfiltration-only operators. CL0P and Silent Ransom are new to the top variants list this quarter; Shiny Hunters slipped two positions.

title: Most targeted industries in Q4 2025
description: Professional Services (18.92%) and Healthcare (15.32%) absorbed the largest share of ransomware cases handled by Coveware in Q4 2025. The mix reflects attackers' preference for downtime-sensitive verticals with strong pressure to restore operations quickly.

title: Ransomware victims skew to small and mid-size firms
description: More than two-thirds of Q4 2025 ransomware incidents hit organizations with fewer than 1,000 employees: 38% had 11-100 employees and 31% had 101-1,000. Coveware reads this as evidence that attackers continue to target smaller, operationally constrained organizations rather than global enterprises.

title: MITRE ATT&CK tactics observed in Q4 2025
description: Coveware mapped Q4 2025 case telemetry to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, with Lateral Movement (65%) and Exfiltration (61% observed) appearing in most engagements. Defense Evasion, Impact, and Credential Access round out the top five recurring tactics.

title: CL0P mass-exploitation campaigns yield diminishing returns
description: Coveware tracks CL0P's five major mass-exploitation campaigns and shows payment rates collapsing from ~25% on Accellion (2021) to ~0% on Cleo MFT (2024), with the Q4 2025 Oracle EBS campaign generating one of the lowest engagement levels yet despite ideal extortion conditions.

title: Average vs median ransom payments diverge sharply
description: Coveware's Q4 2025 data shows the gap between average and median payments widening as a small number of outsized settlements pull the mean far above the typical case. The divergence underscores skewed economics where most victims pay modestly, but a few pay very large sums.

title: Encryption confirmed in 68% of Impact cases
description: Of the 41% of Q4 2025 cases where MITRE Impact (TA0040) tactics were observed, encryption was confirmed in 68% of them. The figure reinforces Coveware's view that encryption-based operational disruption remains the strongest lever for inducing payment.

title: Akira reclaims top variant slot at 14%
description: Akira led all ransomware variants Coveware tracked in Q4 2025, accounting for 14% of cases. Coveware expects encryption-reliant actors like Akira and Qilin to continue outperforming data-exfiltration-only operators on conversion to payment.

title: Professional services hit hardest at 18.9%
description: Professional Services firms absorbed the largest share of Coveware's Q4 2025 ransomware caseload at 18.92%. Coveware attributes the concentration to high downtime sensitivity and pressure to restore client-facing operations quickly.

title: Healthcare 15.3% of Q4 ransomware caseload
description: Healthcare organizations accounted for 15.32% of ransomware cases handled by Coveware in Q4 2025, the second-most targeted sector. Pressure to restore patient-care systems quickly keeps the sector firmly in attackers' sights.

title: Initial access shifts toward remote and identity abuse
description: Coveware's qualitative ranking of Q4 2025 initial attack vectors places Remote Access Compromise far in front, followed by Software Vulnerability Exploitation and Phishing / Social Engineering. The mix reflects attackers abusing legitimate access workflows and exploiting unpatched edge systems rather than relying on user-clicked malware.

title: Stolen data is retained, resold, or re-leveraged
description: Coveware argues that even paying victims gain little durable protection because exfiltrated data continues to circulate. The view is reshaping how legal counsel and incident responders frame the value of payment.
quote: "Stolen data is frequently retained, resold, or re-leveraged, regardless of payment."
pageOrSection: Why Data Exfiltration Pressure Has Failed

title: Largest defensive shift in five years
description: Coveware describes the steady decline in ransom payment rates as one of the most meaningful defensive evolutions of the past five years, driven by better backups, mature legal counsel, and a clearer view of payment's long-term risks.

title: Vishing attacks surged 442% between H1 and H2 2024
description: Voice phishing (vishing) attacks, where adversaries call victims with persuasive social engineering, saw explosive growth in the second half of 2024. CrowdStrike observed a 442% increase between H1 and H2 2024.

title: Average eCrime breakout time fell to 48 minutes
description: The average breakout time for interactive eCrime intrusions fell to 48 minutes in 2024, down from 62 minutes in 2023. Defenders have an ever-shrinking window to detect and respond before adversaries move laterally.
pageOrSection: Breakout Time: The Race Against Adversaries

title: Fastest observed breakout time dropped to 51 seconds
description: The fastest breakout time CrowdStrike observed in 2024 was just 51 seconds, meaning defenders may have less than a minute to detect and respond before attackers establish deeper control.
pageOrSection: Breakout Time: The Race Against Adversaries

title: China-nexus activity surged 150% across all sectors
description: China-nexus intrusions increased 150% across all sectors on average compared to 2023 and represent the most active targeted intrusion threats CrowdStrike Intelligence tracks. China-nexus adversaries continued to operate in every sector and region globally.
pageOrSection: China-Nexus Adversaries Dominate the Global Threat Landscape

title: Key sectors saw 200-300% more China-nexus attacks
description: Financial services, media, manufacturing, and industrials and engineering sectors all experienced 200-300% increases in observed China-nexus intrusions compared to previous years.
pageOrSection: China-Nexus Adversaries Dominate the Global Threat Landscape

title: 79% of detections in 2024 were malware-free
description: In 2024, 79% of the detections CrowdStrike observed were malware-free, up from 40% in 2019. Adversaries are increasingly using hands-on-keyboard techniques that blend in with legitimate user activity and impede detection.

title: Access broker advertisements increased 50% YoY
description: Providing access as a service became a thriving business in 2024, as advertisements for access brokers increased 50% year-over-year. Access brokers acquire access to organizations and sell it to other threat actors, including ransomware operators.
pageOrSection: The Growing Reliance on Identity Attacks

title: 52% of observed vulnerabilities tied to initial access
description: Attacks related to initial access boomed, accounting for 52% of vulnerabilities observed by CrowdStrike in 2024. This reinforces the need to secure exposed systems before attackers establish a foothold.
pageOrSection: The Growing Reliance on Identity Attacks

title: Valid account abuse drove 35% of cloud incidents
description: Abusing valid accounts has become the primary initial access vector to the cloud, accounting for 35% of cloud incidents in the first half of 2024. Attackers favor stealth-oriented credential tactics that don't trigger alerts.
pageOrSection: Access to Valid Accounts Facilitates Initial Access

title: New cloud intrusions grew 26% in 2024
description: In 2024, new and unattributed cloud intrusions increased 26% compared to 2023, indicating more threat actors seek to exploit cloud services. CrowdStrike observed more attackers gaining initial access via valid accounts and abusing cloud command line tools.
pageOrSection: Cloud-Conscious Threat Actors Continue to Innovate

title: Interactive intrusion campaigns grew 35% YoY
description: In 2024, CrowdStrike observed a 35% year-over-year increase in interactive intrusion campaigns. For the seventh consecutive year, the technology sector remained the most targeted industry.
pageOrSection: The Continued Rise of Interactive Intrusions

title: CrowdStrike now tracks 257 named adversaries
description: During 2024, CrowdStrike Intelligence introduced 26 newly named adversaries — including the new Kazakhstan-based COMRADE SAIGA — raising the total number of named adversaries tracked across all motivations to 257.

title: 304 FAMOUS CHOLLIMA incidents in 2024
description: During 2024, CrowdStrike Falcon Adversary OverWatch threat hunters responded to 304 FAMOUS CHOLLIMA incidents, with nearly 40% of these representing insider threat operations driven by the DPRK's IT worker schemes.

title: $25.6M lost to a deepfake CFO scam
description: In February 2024, unidentified threat actors used public footage of a target company's CFO and other employees to create credible deepfake video clones and socially engineered the victim into transferring 25.6 million USD.

title: LLM-generated phishing click-through rate hit 54%
description: A 2024 study of phishing email click-through rates indicated LLM-generated phishing messages had a significantly higher click-through rate (54%) than likely human-written phishing messages (12%).

title: SCATTERED SPIDER share of cloud intrusions fell to 13%
description: In 2023, prolific eCrime adversary SCATTERED SPIDER accounted for 30% of all cloud-based intrusions. This number fell to 13% in 2024, partly because numerous nation-state and opportunistic threat actors are increasingly targeting the cloud control plane.
pageOrSection: New Cloud-Conscious Threat Actors Emerge in 2024

title: SCATTERED SPIDER sent 700,000+ malicious SMS
description: In 2024, SCATTERED SPIDER obtained API keys to a commercial SMS distribution application from a compromised email inbox and subsequently used it to send more than 700,000 SMS messages containing links to AITM phishing and cryptocurrency drainer pages.

title: Adversaries are becoming more business-like
description: CrowdStrike's CEO underscores the central theme of the 2025 report: adversaries are no longer ad-hoc operators but enterprising, business-focused organizations.
quote: Adversaries are becoming more efficient, focused, and business-like in their approach — in many ways, more like the enterprise organizations they prey upon.

title: In 2025, attackers will only move faster
description: CrowdStrike's call to action for defenders entering 2025, emphasizing the closing detection-and-response window.
quote: In 2025, attackers will only move faster. Will defenders keep up?

title: Valid accounts are the primary cloud access vector
description: CrowdStrike's headline finding on identity-driven cloud compromise: legitimate credentials, not malware, are the front door.
quote: Abusing valid accounts has become the primary initial access vector to the cloud, accounting for 35% of cloud incidents in the first half of 2024.
pageOrSection: Access to Valid Accounts Facilitates Initial Access

title: Vishing intrusions per month, 2024
description: Monthly vishing intrusions detected by CrowdStrike OverWatch in 2024, showing the sharp ramp through H2 that culminated in 93 detections by year-end.

title: Malware-free detections rose to 79% by 2024
description: Six-year trend of CrowdStrike detections that were malware-free, climbing from 40% in 2019 to 79% in 2024, defining the shift toward hands-on-keyboard attacks.
pageOrSection: Top 10 Industries Targeted by Interactive Intrusions

title: Access broker advertisements by month, 2024
description: Monthly count of access broker advertisements observed by CrowdStrike in 2024, totaling 4,486 ads. May and December represented the largest peaks of access-as-a-service activity.
pageOrSection: The Growing Reliance on Identity Attacks

title: Vishing detections by month, 2024
description: Monthly vishing intrusions detected by CrowdStrike OverWatch in 2024. The latter half of 2024 saw a 442% increase compared to H1, with December reaching 93 detections.

title: Interactive intrusions by region, 2024
description: Share of interactive intrusions by region observed by CrowdStrike in January-December 2024. North America dominated with 53% of activity, followed by Europe (14%) and East Asia (11%).

title: Top 10 industries targeted by interactive intrusions, 2024
description: Share of interactive intrusions by industry vertical observed by CrowdStrike in 2024. Technology remained the most targeted industry for the seventh consecutive year.
pageOrSection: Top 10 Industries Targeted by Interactive Intrusions

title: Malware-free detections, 2019-2024
description: Percentage of CrowdStrike detections classified as malware-free over six years, rising from 40% in 2019 to 79% in 2024. This shift defines the move toward hands-on-keyboard attacks that mimic legitimate user activity.
pageOrSection: Top 10 Industries Targeted by Interactive Intrusions

title: Average eCrime breakout time, 2023 vs 2024
description: Average eCrime breakout time, in minutes, fell from 62 minutes in 2023 to 48 minutes in 2024 — a 23% acceleration. The fastest observed breakout was just 51 seconds.
pageOrSection: Breakout Time: The Race Against Adversaries

title: Microsoft 365 services accessed in cloud intrusions, H1 2024
description: Microsoft 365 has become a popular target for cloud-conscious threat actors. SharePoint and Outlook were accessed in 22% and 17%, respectively, of relevant intrusions in the first half of 2024.

title: Phishing click-through rate: LLM-generated vs human-written
description: A 2024 academic study found LLM-generated phishing messages achieved a 54% click-through rate versus 12% for likely human-written phishing messages — a 4.5x increase in effectiveness.

title: SCATTERED SPIDER share of cloud intrusions, 2023 vs 2024
description: SCATTERED SPIDER's share of cloud-based intrusions fell from 30% in 2023 to 13% in 2024 as more nation-state and opportunistic threat actors entered the cloud control plane.
