title: Red Menshen suspected origin
description: CYFIRMA attributes Red Menshen (also tracked as Earth Bluecrow) to China-linked operators conducting long-running espionage against telecommunications infrastructure. The group has been active since at least 2021.

title: Red Menshen active since
description: CYFIRMA reports Red Menshen operations going back to at least 2021, with sustained focus on long-term, low-noise intrusions into telecom networks rather than disruptive payloads.

title: Primary motivation
description: Red Menshen's tradecraft is built around information theft and espionage, with operations optimized for dwell and intelligence collection rather than financial or destructive outcomes.

title: Flagship malware
description: BPFDoor is Red Menshen's signature implant: a Linux backdoor operating at the kernel level using Berkeley Packet Filter (BPF) functionality. It avoids open ports and persistent C2 by waking up on packet triggers.

title: Countries targeted
description: CYFIRMA documents Red Menshen victimology spanning ten countries across Asia Pacific, the Middle East, and North America, consistent with telecommunications-focused intelligence gathering.

title: Red Menshen target geography by region
description: Distribution of the ten Red Menshen target countries CYFIRMA lists, grouped by region. Asia Pacific dominates with six countries, followed by the Middle East/MENA cluster, with one US target rounding out the footprint.

title: Red Menshen target countries (full list)
description: All ten countries CYFIRMA lists as targeted by Red Menshen, represented as a uniform-weight victim map. Telecom-heavy APAC nations dominate, with Egypt, Turkey, and the broader Middle East representing MENA exposure and the United States the lone North American entry.

title: MITRE ATT&CK techniques mapped
description: CYFIRMA maps Red Menshen tradecraft to 34 distinct MITRE ATT&CK technique entries spanning 11 tactic categories, reflecting a full-spectrum espionage toolkit from initial access through exfiltration.

title: Red Menshen techniques by ATT&CK tactic
description: Distribution of Red Menshen's 34 mapped techniques across MITRE ATT&CK tactic categories. Defense Evasion (6) and Command and Control (5) dominate, reflecting the group's stealth-first, network-layer tradecraft built around BPFDoor.

title: Share of techniques in Defense Evasion
description: Six of Red Menshen's 34 mapped ATT&CK techniques sit in the Defense Evasion tactic, the single largest category. This reflects the group's emphasis on low-noise, packet-triggered tradecraft and on hiding artifacts via NTFS attributes, masquerading, and indicator removal.

title: Command-and-control techniques observed
description: Red Menshen's command-and-control footprint spans five distinct ATT&CK techniques. The mix combines covert protocol tunneling and non-application-layer channels with traditional HTTP/S beacons and ingress tool transfer — atypical breadth for a stealth-first actor.

title: Initial access vectors
description: Red Menshen leans on two initial-access primitives: exploiting public-facing applications (notably internet-exposed VPN appliances, firewalls, and enterprise network gear) and abusing valid accounts harvested earlier in the kill chain.

title: Why telecoms are the prize
description: CYFIRMA frames Red Menshen's telecom obsession as a route to government and enterprise traffic at scale — the strategic value of a single carrier compromise outstrips dozens of endpoint intrusions.
quote: "The group gains access to large volumes of data traversing these systems, including communications and metadata associated with government entities and enterprises."

title: BPFDoor's stealth model
description: BPFDoor's defining trick is that it never needs to listen on an open port. By hooking the Berkeley Packet Filter at the kernel level it can stay invisible to standard port scans and netflow analytics until a magic packet activates it.
quote: "BPFDoor, a Linux-based backdoor that operates at the kernel level using Berkeley Packet Filter (BPF) functionality, enables covert persistence without relying on open ports or standard command-and-control communication."

title: Pre-positioning over exploitation
description: CYFIRMA emphasizes that Red Menshen optimizes for years of dwell rather than rapid monetization, a profile consistent with state-aligned strategic intelligence collection.
quote: "The group focuses on sustaining undetected access over long periods, enabling continuous intelligence collection."

title: Primary initial-access surface
description: Red Menshen's preferred entry path is exploitation of internet-facing network edge devices — VPN appliances, firewalls, and enterprise network equipment — rather than user-targeted phishing. This places patch posture on perimeter hardware at the center of defensive strategy.

title: Targeted operating systems
description: Red Menshen operates on a cross-platform footing. Linux is the strategic target — that's where BPFDoor lives and where carrier infrastructure runs — with Windows used as a secondary surface for credential harvesting and lateral movement in enterprise environments.

title: Shift toward infrastructure-level espionage
description: CYFIRMA flags a broader strategic trend evident in Red Menshen's operations: state-aligned actors are moving target focus from endpoints to the network backbone where they can monitor traffic in bulk.
quote: "Red Menshen demonstrates movement from endpoint-focused attacks to compromising core network infrastructure, particularly within the telecommunications sector."

title: Stealth-first operating doctrine
description: Red Menshen's tradecraft is built around blending into normal traffic. Avoiding detectable artifacts is treated as a design constraint rather than a post-hoc tactic.
quote: "The group prioritizes low-noise operations, avoiding techniques that generate detectable traffic."

title: Operating below the monitoring layer
description: CYFIRMA highlights Red Menshen's network-level sophistication — by leveraging BPF, the malware effectively bypasses higher-level security telemetry that most defenders rely on.
quote: "BPF-based malware reflects sophisticated understanding that enables operations below traditional security monitoring layers."

title: APAC share of Red Menshen targeting
description: Six of the ten countries CYFIRMA lists as Red Menshen targets are in Asia Pacific (India, Myanmar, South Korea, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia), giving the region a 60% share of named victimology and confirming the group's regional priorities.

title: ATT&CK tactic categories covered
description: Red Menshen's tradecraft touches 11 of the 14 enterprise ATT&CK tactic categories — full-spectrum coverage from initial access through exfiltration, with no observed activity in tactics like Impact, Reconnaissance, or Resource Development in this profile.

title: 4,875 EU incidents curated by ENISA analysts
description: Across the 1 July 2024 – 30 June 2025 reporting period, ENISA analysts collected and curated 4,875 incidents impacting EU Member States and EU-based organisations, drawn primarily from open sources and ENISA Cyber Partnership Programme contributions.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: Hacktivism reached 79% of total EU incidents
description: Despite minimal real-world impact, hacktivist activity continued to dominate ENISA reporting, accounting for almost 80% of recorded incidents — driven primarily by ideology-motivated DDoS waves.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: DDoS dominates EU incident types at 76.7%
description: The distribution of incident types in ENISA's EU dataset is dominated by DDoS attacks (about 76.7%), overwhelmingly driven by hacktivist groups, with cybercrime extortion-led ransom-DDoS playing a marginal role.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: Phishing drives 60% of initial intrusions
description: Social-engineering tactics remain the primary entry point for threat actors in the EU, with phishing (including vishing, malspam and malvertising) accounting for roughly 60% of observed intrusion-vector cases.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: Vulnerability exploitation 21.3% of intrusions
description: Exploitation of vulnerabilities remains a cornerstone of initial access (21.3%) in the EU dataset, with widespread campaigns weaponising newly disclosed flaws within days of publication.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: Public administration is the top targeted sector (38%)
description: Public administration remained the most targeted sector in the EU at 38% of incidents, with the increase primarily driven by hacktivist-led DDoS attacks against government websites and portals.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: AI-supported phishing tops 80% of social engineering
description: By early 2025, AI-supported phishing campaigns reportedly represented more than 80% of observed social-engineering activity worldwide, with adversaries leveraging jailbroken LLMs, synthetic media and model-poisoning techniques.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: Akira drives 48.7% of EU manufacturing ransomware
description: Among ransomware strains deployed against EU manufacturing organisations, Akira dominated at 48.7%, followed by Qilin (20.5%) and FOG (10.3%), reinforcing Akira's status as a top-of-mind threat to industrial operators.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: 42,595 new vulnerabilities disclosed (+27% YoY)
description: ENISA recorded 42,595 new vulnerabilities disclosed over the reporting period — a 27% rise on the prior year. CVSS triage showed 7% Critical, 26% High, 43% Medium, 3% Low and 21% unscored. The sparkline approximates the implied severity distribution.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: Lumma stealer hit 394,000 Windows machines
description: Assessed as the most prevalent info-stealer in 2025, Lumma was reportedly deployed on 394,000 Windows machines globally between March and May 2025, with strong prevalence in the EU before Europol-coordinated takedowns of ~2,300 malicious domains.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: Shift toward mixed, convergent cyber pressure
description: ENISA's headline narrative for 2025: the threat picture is shifting from rare high-impact events to a continuous, diversified campaign environment that steadily erodes EU resilience.
quote: "The cyber threat landscape is shifting toward mixed, possibly convergent pressure, with fewer single high impact incidents, and more continuous, diversified and convergent campaigns that collectively erode resilience."
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: Initial intrusion vectors in the EU
description: Phishing dominates initial intrusion in ENISA's EU dataset, followed by exploitation of vulnerabilities, botnets, malicious applications and insider misuse — a mix that underscores the continued primacy of social engineering alongside technical exploitation.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: Distribution of EU incident types
description: DDoS attacks dwarf all other recorded incident categories in the EU dataset, followed by intrusions (cybercrime and state-aligned), with defacements remaining a small, almost exclusively hacktivist tactic.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: Top five EU sectors targeted
description: Once unspecified targeting is set aside, public administration far outstrips other verticals as the most targeted EU sector, followed by transport, digital infrastructure, finance and manufacturing. Essential entities under NIS2 represent 53.7% of all recorded incidents.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: EU member states with most public-administration hits
description: Within the public-administration sector, France, Italy and Germany absorbed the highest recorded incident shares, followed by Spain and Poland — patterns shaped by hacktivist-led DDoS targeting governmental websites.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: Top EU member states named in ransomware & breach claims
description: Germany leads ransomware and data-breach claims affecting EU organisations at 23.4%, followed by Italy, Spain, France and Belgium — largely tracking each market's economic weight as a target of opportunity.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: Most-deployed ransomware strains in the EU
description: Ransomware activity in the EU has fragmented sharply post-LockBit. Akira leads at 11.6% of deployments, followed by SafePay and Qilin, illustrating a more evenly distributed but professionalised RaaS ecosystem.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity
comparison: 82 ransomware variants observed against EU MSs

title: Most active hacktivist groups against EU
description: Pro-Russia NoName057(16) overwhelmingly dominates EU-targeted hacktivism at 63.1% of attacks, with Keymous+, Dark Storm Team, Mr Hamza and RipperSec rounding out the top five.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: Hacktivist targeting by EU sector
description: Hacktivist activity in the EU is heavily concentrated on public administration (63.1%), followed by transport, finance, digital infrastructure and a tie between manufacturing and media/entertainment.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: Hacktivist attack mix is DDoS-first
description: Within hacktivist activity targeting EU Member States, DDoS attacks account for 91.5% of incidents, with claimed intrusions at just 5.1% and data breaches at 3.4% — underscoring DDoS as a low-skill, high-visibility tactic.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: EU transport incidents concentrate in air and logistics
description: Within the transport sector, ENISA records a concentration of incidents in air transport (58.4%) and logistics (20.8%) — reflecting both hacktivist DDoS waves and ransomware impacts on maritime, freight and airport operators.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: Threat category mix across the EU
description: ENISA's threat-category distribution highlights mobile threats as the largest share (42.4%), followed by web threats, operational-technology threats and supply-chain risks — evidence that attackers exploit both digital surfaces and indirect dependencies.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: Adversary objectives behind EU incidents
description: Most EU-targeting activity is ideology-driven (hacktivist DDoS), followed by financially motivated cybercrime, with state-aligned cyberespionage representing 7.2% but remaining a primary medium-to-long-term concern.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: CVSS severity breakdown of disclosed vulnerabilities
description: Of the 42,595 vulnerabilities disclosed during the period, ENISA classifies 7% Critical, 26% High, 43% Medium, 3% Low and 21% unscored — highlighting both the volume and the triage backlog facing EU defenders.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: Top Russia-aligned FIMI operators against the EU
description: Out of 86 FIMI operations targeting EU entities and Member States captured by EEAS, Matryoshka led with 18 cases, followed by Doppelgänger, Storm-1516 and the Russian Foundation to Battle Injustice; Portal Kombat infrastructure was used in 19 cases to amplify content.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: State-aligned activity = 7.2% of EU incidents
description: Between July 2024 and June 2025, 7.2% of recorded EU-targeted incidents were associated with state-aligned activities — led by Russia-nexus, then China-nexus and DPRK-nexus intrusion sets, plus emerging India-nexus targeting.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: 64% of CVEs are network-exploitable
description: When considering the CVSS Attack Vector metric, 64% of newly documented vulnerabilities can be exploited over the network — underscoring the systemic risk posed by Internet-facing systems across EU organisations.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: 68.6% of intrusions ended in saleable data breaches
description: Out of recorded intrusions in the EU, 68.6% resulted in data leaked or advertised on cybercriminal forums for sale (2.8% of those tied directly to a ransomware claim), while 30.2% led to data exfiltration including credential theft and strategic collection.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: Ransomware, banking trojans & infostealers = 87.3% of post-intrusion code
description: Combined, ransomware, banking trojans and infostealers account for 87.3% of malicious code observed after EU intrusions — cementing the financially motivated cybercriminal ecosystem as the principal beneficiary of successful breaches.
source: ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity

title: First known AI-powered ransomware emerges
description: ESET researchers discovered PromptLock, the first known AI-driven ransomware, on VirusTotal in H2 2025. It uses an OpenAI model via the Ollama API to generate malicious Lua scripts on the fly that can enumerate files, exfiltrate, encrypt, or destroy data. ESET assessed it as a proof of concept, later confirmed by NYU academics.
quote: "The emergence of tools like PromptLock highlights a significant shift in the cyberthreat landscape. With the help of AI, launching sophisticated attacks has become dramatically easier, eliminating the need for teams of skilled developers."

title: Lumma Stealer detections collapse after May takedown
description: Following the global disruption of Lumma Stealer in May 2025 by law enforcement and cybersecurity companies including ESET, attack attempts using this MaaS infostealer fell 86% in H2 2025 versus H1 2025. Lumma briefly resurfaced twice but its glory days appear over.

title: Lumma Stealer attack attempts collapse: H1 vs H2 2025
description: ESET telemetry shows Lumma Stealer attack attempts fell from more than 60,000 in H1 2025 to fewer than 9,000 in H2 2025, an 86% drop after the May 2025 disruption operation.

title: ClickFix delivery vector for Lumma nearly vanishes
description: HTML/FakeCaptcha trojan — a key ClickFix distribution vector for Lumma Stealer — collapsed by nearly 100%, from more than 1.6 million detections in H1 2025 to fewer than 60,000 in H2 2025. Several threat actors appear to have abandoned this vector after the takedown efforts.

title: CloudEyE/GuLoader detections skyrocket ~30x
description: Phishing-delivered CloudEyE (also known as GuLoader), a MaaS downloader and cryptor used to deploy Rescoms, Formbook, Agent Tesla, and ransomware, increased nearly thirtyfold in ESET telemetry in H2 2025, surpassing 100,000 detections during the period.

title: Poland absorbs ~32% of CloudEyE attacks
description: Poland was the top target country for CloudEyE attacks in H2 2025, with roughly every third attack attempt (about 32%) seen there. The peak day was September 18, part of a wave of Central and Eastern European phishing campaigns observed in September and October 2025.

title: PowerShell downloaders rise 59%
description: Attack attempts using PowerShell variants of CloudEyE's initial stage drove PowerShell downloader detections up 59% in H2 2025, making PowerShell scripts account for 9% of all downloader detections during the period.

title: Ransomware victims projected up 40% YoY in 2025
description: Based on dedicated leak site (DLS) data collected via ecrime.ch, the cumulative number of publicly named ransomware victims in 2025 reached 6,937 — over 1,700 more than the 2024 total — implying roughly +40% year-over-year growth. The data only includes victims who refused to pay and were named by gangs themselves.

title: 6,937 publicly named ransomware victims in 2025
description: ESET cites ecrime.ch DLS monitoring showing 6,937 known ransomware victims in 2025, exceeding 2024's total by more than 1,700 victims. DLS data only includes victims who refused to pay; true victim counts are higher.

title: Top countries targeted in ESET-analyzed ransomware attacks
description: Of hundreds of hands-on-keyboard ransomware attacks analyzed by ESET in 2025, organizations in the United States accounted for the largest share, followed by Spain, France, Italy, and Canada.

title: Top RaaS gangs in ESET-analyzed attacks: Akira and Qilin lead
description: In hands-on-keyboard ransomware attacks analyzed by ESET in 2025, Akira and Qilin tied for the largest share at 10% each in the ransomware-as-a-service arena, followed by MedusaLocker at 7%. By year-end, Qilin emerged as the dominant public force after the H1 2025 collapse of RansomHub.

title: Jaguar Land Rover ransomware costs ~$2.5B
description: The H2 2025 ransomware attack on Jaguar Land Rover forced a global production and IT shutdown, disrupted approximately 5,000 supply-chain businesses, and caused financial damage of nearly USD 2.5 billion — making it the costliest cyberincident in UK history. A group linked to Scattered Spider, Lapsus$, and ShinyHunters claimed responsibility.

title: Android NFC threats grow 87%
description: Detections of NFC-abusing Android malware grew 87% between H1 and H2 2025 — a slowdown vs the 30x+ growth in H1 but still a notable rise. Notable upgrades observed: NGate added contact stealing, PhantomCard expanded NFC fraud into Brazil, and RatOn fused RAT, banking trojan, ATS, and NFC relay capabilities.

title: Nomani investment scams grew 62% YoY
description: ESET telemetry shows HTML/Nomani investment scam detections grew 62% year-over-year in 2025, with more than 64,000 unique URLs blocked across the year. H2 2025 detections fell 37% versus H1 — a hint of improvement. Scammers use higher-resolution deepfakes, AI-generated phishing pages, and ultra-short ad campaigns to evade detection.

title: Meta projected $16B from scam ads (Reuters)
description: Reuters, citing Meta internal documents in late H2 2025, reported that Meta anticipated earning approximately USD 16 billion — or 10% of its 2024 revenue — from scam advertising. The documents also estimated users were exposed to 15 billion deceptive ads daily across Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp. Meta's automated systems reportedly ban advertisers only when at least 95% certain they are scammers. Meta disputes the framing.

title: Top 10 infostealer families in H2 2025
description: Win/Formbook trojan led infostealer detections in H2 2025 at 17.3%, followed by MSIL/Spy.AgentTesla and MSIL/Spy.Agent. Overall infostealer detections fell 18% H1 to H2 as Lumma Stealer collapsed.

title: Top 10 Android detections in H2 2025
description: Android/TrojanDropper.Agent led Android detections in H2 2025 at 18.9%, followed by AdDisplay.Generic PUA (17.6%) and AdDisplay.MobiDash PUA (11.5%). Android/Spy.Banker — the trojan category covering NGate and PhantomCard variants — held 4.3%. Overall Android detections fell 15% H1 to H2.

title: Top 10 ransomware detections in H2 2025
description: Win/RiskWare.LockScreen application led ransomware detections at 18.8%, followed by Win/Filecoder trojan (12.3%) and Win/Filecoder.BlackMatter (6.9%). Overall ransomware category detections rose 13% from H1 to H2 2025.

title: Top 10 email-borne threats in H2 2025
description: HTML/Phishing.Agent dominated email-borne threats at 30.8%, followed by DOC/Fraud (10.7%) and HTML/Phishing (5.7%). Email threat detections rose 36% H1 to H2 2025, even as spam detections fell 23%.

title: Malicious email attachment types in H2 2025
description: Script files dominated malicious email attachments at 41.5% in H2 2025, followed by executables (23.4%), Office documents (11.1%), PDFs (9.7%), archives (7.2%), and batch files (6.6%).

title: Top external network intrusion vectors in H2 2025
description: Password guessing accounted for 43.3% of external network intrusion vectors reported by unique ESET clients in H2 2025, far outpacing CVE-driven exploitation. The top exploit-based vectors were Apache Log4j (CVE-2021-44228) at 16.2%, Apache Struts2 (CVE-2017-5638) at 14.4%, and PHP CVE-2024-4577 at 8.4%.

title: RDP, SMB, and SQL password-guessing attempts surge
description: ESET telemetry shows continued growth in password-guessing attack attempts against exposed network services in H2 2025 vs H1 2025: RDP +62%, SQL +27%, and SMB +19%.

title: Detection-category trends: H2 vs H1 2025
description: Cross-category H2 2025 detection changes from ESET telemetry: unique URL blocks +78%, email threats +36%, downloaders +24%, ransomware +13%, all threats +10%, Android -15%, cryptocurrency threats -18%, infostealers -18%, web threats -22%, spam -23%, macOS -31%.

title: Top 10 overall malware detections in H2 2025
description: HTML/Phishing.Agent led overall ESET malware detections in H2 2025 at 9.2%, followed by JS/Agent adware (8.6%), JS/Packed.Agent (6.4%), and JS/Redirector (6.1%). HTML and JavaScript dominate the top of the list, reflecting heavy reliance on web-based delivery.

title: EDR killers proliferate among Akira, Qilin, Warlock affiliates
description: Over three months in H2 2025, ESET Research discovered more than a dozen new EDR-killer tools in the wild, mostly used by Akira and Qilin affiliates, followed by Warlock. Most rely on bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver (BYOVD); rapid adoption of EDR-Freeze (abusing WerFaultSecure) was observed mainly with Akira and Chaos affiliates.
quote: "The rising popularity of EDR killers highlights that endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools remain a significant obstacle for ransomware operators."

title: APT activity: Sednit weaponizes AI; Gamaredon teams with Turla
description: ESET research in H2 2025 highlighted multiple nation-state operations: Russia-aligned Sednit/APT28/Fancy Bear was linked (medium confidence by CERT-UA) to the LLM-querying PromptSteal/LameHug data miner against Poland and Lithuania; Gamaredon collaborated with Turla against Ukrainian targets; North Korea-aligned Lazarus targeted the UAV sector via Operation DreamJob; China-aligned PlushDaemon and GhostRedirector compromised network devices and Windows servers; MuddyWater (Iran-aligned) targeted Israel and Egypt; RomCom exploited a WinRAR zero-day.
quote: "Russia-aligned Sednit (aka APT28, Fancy Bear) used PromptSteal in cyberespionage and reconnaissance attacks against Ukraine."

title: Bots are 10.2% of all HTTP traffic across F5 customers
description: Out of 200+ billion web and API transactions analyzed (Nov 2023 - Sep 2024), 10.2% (21.22B requests) were automated traffic. F5 mitigated 4.8% as unwanted bots, 3.5% were monitoring-mode flagged automation, and 2.0% were known financial aggregators.

title: Composition of automated HTTP traffic in F5 dataset
description: Breakdown of the 10.2% automated share of HTTP traffic: 4.8% unwanted bots mitigated by F5, 3.5% flagged automation in monitoring mode, and 2.0% known financial aggregators - across 200+ billion transactions.

title: Web automation share by industry (top sectors)
description: Hospitality leads all web sectors at 44.8% automated traffic, followed by Technology at 33.5% (login endpoints), Healthcare at 32.6%, and eCommerce at 22.7%. Insurance recorded the lowest rate of automated attacks.

title: Mobile API automation by industry
description: Entertainment dominates mobile-API automation at 23.0% (down from 34.5% in 2023), while eCommerce mobile APIs run at 4.5%. Telecommunications mobile APIs show the highest advanced-bot sophistication of any sector.

series.name: Automated share of mobile API traffic (%)

title: Year-over-year change in web automation by sector
description: 60% of industry-platform combos saw decreased automation. Telecom (-18.5%), Healthcare (-10.0%), and Airlines (-9.2%) posted the largest declines, while Hospitality (+18.3%) and QSR (+11.2%) saw automation surge.

title: Bot sophistication on web platforms
description: 24.0% of automated web traffic is advanced bots, 21.5% intermediate, and approximately 54.5% basic. Advanced bots execute JavaScript, simulate full browser user behavior, and generate device telemetry.

title: Bot sophistication on mobile APIs
description: Mobile APIs see a different mix than the web: 40.0% intermediate, 13.5% advanced, and approximately 46.5% basic bots. Operators tune sophistication to bypass mobile SDK token defenses.

series.name: Share of automated mobile API traffic (%)

title: Sectors with most advanced bots on the web
description: General Retail leads at 47.78% advanced bots, followed by Airlines at 43.10% and Banking at 37.90%. These verticals attract the most resourced bot operators thanks to direct monetization paths.

title: Credential stuffing share of web auth traffic
description: On web platforms, 10.6% of authentication traffic was credential stuffing across F5 customers. Technology logins peaked at 33.5%, General Retail at 25.7%, and Gaming at 19.6%.

title: Credential stuffing on mobile APIs by industry
description: Mobile API auth traffic ran 5.2% credential stuffing overall, but Entertainment and eCommerce both peaked at 24.0% - signaling concentrated account-takeover pressure on consumer apps.

series.name: Credential stuffing share of auth traffic (%)

title: Telecom mobile APIs face 50% advanced credential stuffing
description: Half of all credential-stuffing attempts on Telecommunications mobile APIs come from advanced bots - the highest advanced-attack share of any sector. eCommerce mobile APIs follow at 44.82% advanced.

title: Bots make up 50%+ of web content requests
description: Web scrapers are the single largest bot category, accounting for more than half of all content requests on protected web properties. Ratings flows run 91.44% advanced bots, while pure scraping is 90.48% basic.

title: AI agents drive 47.7% YoY rise in web content scraping
description: Web content-scraping traffic grew 47.7% year over year, with F5 attributing the surge to AI-agent activity from OpenAI, Anthropic, Perplexity, and Google. Gift Card flows (-13.6%) and Web Shop (-7.6%) declined over the same period.

title: Layer-7 web flow automation by use case
description: Automation concentrates in specific layer-7 flows: 50%+ of content requests, ~25% of Search, and 20%+ of Add-to-Cart traffic comes from bots - especially reseller bots competing for inventory.

title: Every cellular IP now carries some bot traffic
description: F5 monitors 20+ distinct proxyware families. Marketing claims of 100M+ residential proxy nodes are overstated - in practice only 2-3 million nodes are reachable per day, but coverage of cellular IP space is near-total.
quote: Virtually every single cellular IP address passes some bot traffic.

title: PROXYLIB ecosystem spans 28+ repackaged Android apps
description: F5 documented at least 28 repackaged Android applications using the PROXYLIB SDK, communicating with 7+ primary C2 domains and reselling residential exit nodes under 6+ rebrands (asocks.com, ake.net, blackproxy.io, nexusnet.io, sx.org, any-page.io).

title: Mobile API automation drops 85% once mitigation is enabled
description: Median unauthorized automation on mobile APIs falls from 6.11% in monitoring mode to 0.90% when F5 mitigation is enabled. Zero unauthorized bots reached origin servers across the dataset.

title: 71.4% of web flows see MORE bot retries after mitigation
description: On the web, the median unauthorized automation actually ticked up from 7.04% (monitoring) to 7.94% (mitigation enabled) - and 71.4% of flows saw increased automation attempts post-mitigation. The rise reflects persistent operator retries, not control failure: zero unauthorized bots reached origin servers.

title: Hospitality web automation peaks at 55% in July
description: Hospitality web bot traffic swings from a 34.01% low in May to a 54.90% peak in July, tracking summer travel booking activity. The seasonality pattern signals scraping and account-stuffing against loyalty programs.

title: Entertainment mobile API automation swings 5x by month
description: Entertainment mobile API bot traffic ranges from a 41.29% high in November to an 8.21% low in June, recovering to 14.82% by September. Streaming launch cycles drive the peaks.

title: Total reported cybercrime losses hit $20.9B in 2025
description: Losses reported to IC3 surpassed the $20 billion mark for the first time in 2025, climbing to $20.877 billion. This represents a 26% jump from the $16.6 billion lost in 2024.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: IC3 received over 1 million complaints in 2025
description: The Internet Crime Complaint Center logged 1,008,597 complaints in 2025, averaging nearly 3,000 complaints filed per day. It is the first time IC3 has crossed the seven-figure annual complaint threshold.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Average reported loss per victim was $20,699
description: Across all complaints in 2025, the average reported loss climbed to $20,699 per victim. The figure reflects the rising effectiveness of high-value scams such as investment fraud, BEC and tech-support fraud.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Cyber-enabled fraud drove 85% of all reported losses
description: Cyber-enabled fraud — schemes that use the internet or technology to steal money, data, or identities — generated $17.697 billion in losses across 452,868 complaints. That is 45% of IC3 complaints but 85% of total dollar losses for the year.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Investment fraud losses topped $8.6B — largest category
description: Investment fraud was once again the costliest crime type reported to IC3, with $8.65 billion in losses across 72,984 complaints. Crypto-investment 'pig-butchering' schemes drove a large share of these losses.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: BEC losses reached $3.05B in 2025
description: Business Email Compromise (BEC) was the second-largest source of reported losses at $3.046 billion. BEC remained a top target for the IC3 Recovery Asset Team's Financial Fraud Kill Chain process.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Tech/customer support scams cost $2.13B
description: Tech and customer-support impersonation scams generated $2.135 billion in losses across 47,794 complaints. Call-center based fraud rose so sharply that BEC was no longer the dominant Financial Fraud Kill Chain category in 2025.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Cryptocurrency-nexus losses reached $11.4B
description: Complaints with a cryptocurrency nexus totalled 181,565 (a 21% increase from 2024) and accounted for $11.367 billion in losses — a 22% YoY rise. The average crypto-related loss hit $62,604.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Victims aged 60+ lost $7.7B — a 59% YoY spike
description: Complainants aged 60 and older filed 201,266 complaints (up 37% YoY) and reported losses of $7.748 billion, a 59% increase from 2024. The average elder-fraud loss was $38,500, with 12,444 seniors losing more than $100,000 each.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Recovery Asset Team froze $679M of fraudulent transfers
description: The IC3 Recovery Asset Team initiated 3,900 Financial Fraud Kill Chain (FFKC) incidents covering $1.16 billion in attempted theft. The team helped freeze $679 million — a 58% recovery rate.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Losses surpass $20 billion for the first time
description: The FBI emphasized the acceleration of cyber-enabled fraud in its 2025 introduction, noting that investment fraud — and crypto investment scams in particular — were the dominant loss driver.
quote: "In 2025, losses reported to IC3 continued to climb, surpassing the $20 billion mark. Investment-related fraud was once again the largest component of these losses."
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Annual IC3 losses 2020–2025
description: IC3's reported annual losses climbed from $4.2B in 2020 to $20.9B in 2025 — roughly a 5x increase in six years. The growth has been driven primarily by crypto investment fraud and BEC.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Annual complaints crossed 1M in 2025
description: Yearly complaints to IC3 have grown steadily, doubling from roughly 467K in 2019 to over 1 million in 2025. Volume reflects both improving public awareness and the worsening cybercrime landscape.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Top crime types by reported losses (2025)
description: Investment fraud dwarfs every other reported crime category, exceeding BEC by more than 2.8x. Tech-support, personal data breach, and confidence/romance scams round out the top five by dollar losses.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Top crime types by complaint count (2025)
description: Phishing/spoofing remains by far the most-reported crime, with 191,561 complaints — more than 2x the next category. Extortion, investment, personal data breach and non-payment/non-delivery follow.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Reported losses by victim age group
description: Older Americans bore the brunt of cybercrime in 2025: victims aged 60+ reported $7.7B in losses, more than 36% of the national total. Losses climb steeply with age while complaint volumes are more evenly distributed.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Complaint counts by victim age group
description: Victims aged 60+ filed the most complaints (201,266), but the 40–49 cohort was a close second at 167,066. Younger Americans (under 30) accounted for roughly 14% of all 2025 IC3 complaints.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Top 10 U.S. states by reported losses
description: California led all states with $3.675 billion in reported cybercrime losses in 2025, more than 2x runner-up Texas. The top four (California, Texas, Florida, New York) together account for over $8 billion in reported losses.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Top 10 U.S. states by complaint count
description: California (116,414) and Texas (97,912) topped state-level complaint volumes, followed by Florida and New York. The top 10 states collectively filed over 500,000 IC3 complaints in 2025.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Top 10 reported ransomware variants (2025)
description: Akira topped the IC3 ransomware leaderboard for 2025, followed by Qilin and the INC/Lynx/Sinobi family. These ten variants accounted for nearly half (49.8%) of all reported ransomware losses.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: 3,600+ ransomware complaints reported $32M in losses
description: IC3 received more than 3,600 ransomware complaints in 2025 with reported losses exceeding $32 million. The figure excludes lost business, downtime, remediation costs, and unreported incidents — likely understating true impact significantly.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Non-critical sector ransomware complaints by industry
description: IC3 received over 1,400 ransomware complaints from organizations outside the 16 critical infrastructure sectors. Legal services topped the list (18%), with contracting, engineering, and consulting firms also heavily targeted.

series.name: Share of non-critical sector ransomware complaints (%)

source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Financial Fraud Kill Chain success rate by critical sector
description: Among 655 FFKC actions for critical infrastructure victims, recovery success varied widely. Emergency Services and Energy showed near-perfect recovery (92%, 95%), while Critical Manufacturing trailed at 31%.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Top 5 cyber-enabled fraud types by loss
description: Among cyber-enabled fraud schemes, investment fraud led with $8.65 billion in losses — nearly 3x BEC's $3.05 billion. Tech-support, romance, and government-impersonation scams round out the top five.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Top 5 cyber-enabled fraud types by complaint count
description: Extortion (89,129 complaints) was the most-reported cyber-enabled fraud type in 2025, followed by investment, non-payment/non-delivery, tech support, and government impersonation. Volume rankings differ markedly from loss rankings.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Operation Level Up saved $500M+ from crypto scams
description: Since launching in January 2024, the FBI-led Operation Level Up has notified more than 8,000 cryptocurrency-investment-fraud victims and prevented over $500 million in losses. In 2025 alone, 3,780 victims were notified — 78% of whom were unaware they were being scammed.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: AI-enabled BEC scams cost businesses over $30M
description: In 2025, businesses reported losses exceeding $30 million to BEC scams involving AI. Generative-AI chat tools are being used to craft official-sounding emails that mimic executive or vendor communications.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Call-center fraud generated $2.9B in losses
description: Tech/customer support and government-impersonation scams — typically run from illegal call centers in Southeast Asia and India — generated more than 80,000 complaints and over $2.9 billion in losses in 2025.
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Elder fraud emerges as a national crisis
description: Per accessibility narration of IC3's elder fraud chart, victims aged 60+ saw their losses balloon almost 60% year-over-year, with more than 12,000 seniors each losing six figures.
quote: "201,266 complaints (37% increase from 2024); $7.748 billion losses (59% increase from 2024); $38,500 average loss; 12,444 complainants lost more than $100K."
source: FBI IC3 — Internet Crime Complaint Center

title: Over 97 billion exploitation attempts recorded in 2024
description: Fortinet IPS sensors detected more than 97 billion exploitation attempts during 2024, reflecting how cybercriminals are continuously probing exposed systems. The volume highlights increased automation and broader cross-industry targeting.
pageOrSection: From Exposure to Initial Access and Exploitation

title: Active scanning rose 16.7% worldwide in 2024
description: Reconnaissance reached unprecedented levels in 2024 with active scanning growing 16.71% year over year. FortiGuard Labs observed 1.16 trillion current detections versus 993 billion in 2024.

title: Adversaries hit 36,000 scans per second globally
description: FortiGuard Labs observed billions of scan attempts each month in 2024, equating to roughly 36,000 scans per second. This reflects intensified focus on mapping exposed services such as SIP, RDP, and OT/IoT protocols like Modbus TCP.

title: 100 billion compromised credential records shared on darknet
description: In 2024, more than 100 billion records were shared in underground forums, a 42% increase over 2023. Combo lists dominate, with over 50% of darknet posts tied to leaked databases that fuel credential stuffing.

title: 500% surge in infostealer credential logs
description: FortiGuard Labs observed a 500% increase in logs from systems compromised by infostealer malware in 2024, with 1.7 billion stolen credential records shared in underground forums. Redline, Vidar and Racoon led the market.

title: CVEs grew 39% from 2023 to 2024
description: More than 40,000 vulnerabilities were added to the National Vulnerability Database in 2024, representing a 39% increase over 2023. Despite the surge, zero-day attacks account for only a small share of observed threats.

title: FortiGuard on the accelerating adversary advantage
description: Fortinet frames the 2024 threat environment as one where automation, commoditization, and AI systematically erode the traditional advantages held by defenders. The report argues for a shift from reactive defense to continuous threat exposure management.
quote: "Threat actors are leveraging automation, commoditized tools, and AI to erode the traditional advantages held by defenders systematically."

title: Ivanti CVE-2024-21887 weaponized in 6 days
description: CVE-2024-21887, a command injection vulnerability in Ivanti products, was exploited just six days after disclosure. It underscores how quickly adversaries act when opportunity aligns with impact, while the 2024 average time-to-exploit held near the 5.4-day 2023 baseline.

title: 70% of cloud incidents involved logins from unfamiliar geographies
description: Lacework FortiCNAPP telemetry shows that in 70% of observed cloud incidents, attackers gained access via logins from unfamiliar geographies. The finding underscores the critical role of identity monitoring in cloud defense.

title: SIP dominates protocol scanning at 49%
description: FortiGuard Labs broke down scanning traffic by protocol. SIP (VoIP) accounted for more than 49% of detected scans, while Modbus TCP showed 1.6%, reflecting industrial control concerns. Other widely scanned services include RDP and IoT protocols.

title: SIPVicious drives nearly half of all scanning events
description: FortiGuard observed that SIPVicious accounts for nearly 50% of scanning events, followed by Qualys at 2.5%. Nmap, Nessus and OpenVAS appear in smaller shares but remain commonly used for vulnerability discovery.

title: APAC absorbs 42% of global exploitation attempts
description: Of more than 97 billion exploitation attempts recorded in 2024, APAC accounted for 42.4%, followed by EMEA at 26.3%, North America at 20.2% and LATAM at 11.1%. The geographic spread highlights that attackers operate without borders.

title: Top exploited CVEs of 2024 by share of attempts
description: FortiGuard IPS telemetry surfaced the most attractive entry points for adversaries. The Windows SMB Information Disclosure flaw (CVE-2017-0147) led with 26.7% of attempts, followed by Apache Log4j (CVE-2021-44228) at 11.6% and the Netcore Netis hardcoded password issue (CVE-2019-18935) at 8%.

title: IoT exploitation centers on routers and cameras
description: Over 20% of all recorded exploitation attempts targeted IoT devices. Netcore Netis routers led at 18.4%, with WiFi P2P GoAhead cameras at 10.5%, Zyxel firewalls and routers at 3.2%, TP-Link Archer AX21 at 2.1%, and GPON routers at 0.9%.

title: Initial Access Brokers favor VPNs and RDP
description: Underground IAB listings centered on enterprise access pathways. Corporate VPN credentials made up 20% of sought-after assets, with RDP at 19%, admin panels at 13% and webshells at 12% rounding out the top categories.

title: Redline dominates the infostealer market
description: Among infostealers driving the 500% surge in credential logs, Redline led with 60% share, Vidar followed at 27% and Racoon held 12%. Redline's affordability and ease of use have made it the IAB favorite for ransomware operators.

title: Most darknet zero-days ship with working exploit code
description: Of the 331 zero-day vulnerabilities identified in darknet forums in 2024, 55% had publicly available proof-of-concept code, 32% featured fully functional exploits, and 30% were actively being used in ransomware and APT campaigns.

title: Top four ransomware groups drive 37% of victims
description: Out of 1,638 identified ransomware victims in 2024, the top four groups concentrated attacks: RansomHub at 13%, LockBit 3.0 at 12%, Play at 8% and Medusa at 4%. Together they account for 37% of all observed activity despite a fragmented landscape.

title: Manufacturing leads ransomware target sectors
description: Among 1,638 identified ransomware victims, manufacturing was the most targeted at 17%, followed by business services at 11%, construction at 9% and retail at 9%. The mix reflects ransomware's continued focus on operationally sensitive verticals.

title: United States bears 61% of ransomware victim load
description: Ransomware victim geography skewed heavily toward English-speaking markets in 2024. The United States accounted for 61% of identified victims, with the United Kingdom at 6% and Canada at 5%.

title: Lazarus and Kimsuky lead APT activity
description: Fortinet's adversary analysis ranked nation-state activity by share of observed APT campaigns. Lazarus led at 21%, followed by Kimsuky at 18%, APT28 at 13%, Volt Typhoon at 12% and APT29 at 10%; the remaining 26% belonged to other groups.

title: Discovery dominates cloud attack tactics
description: Lacework FortiCNAPP mapped 2024 cloud incidents to MITRE ATT&CK tactics. Discovery led at 25.3%, followed by Initial Access at 14.7%, Persistence at 12.3%, Privilege Escalation at 10.6%, Impact at 8.4%, Credential Access at 7.9%, Lateral Movement at 6.8%, Defense Evasion at 6.1%, Collection at 3.5%, Exfiltration at 3.3% and Execution at 1.2%.
pageOrSection: Cloud Battlefield - Distribution of MITRE ATT&CK Tactics

title: BestCombo leads darknet credential trade
description: Among the most active credential-supplier groups, BestCombo accounted for 20% of activity, followed by BloddyMery at 12% and ValidMail at 12%. IAB leaders sandocan, F13 and JefryG anchored the corporate-access market at 26%, 16% and 12% respectively.

title: RipperSec leads hacktivist Telegram coordination
description: Hacktivists adopted more aggressive tactics in 2024 using Telegram as their primary coordination platform. RipperSec accounted for 20% of campaigns, Z-BL4CX-H4T 14%, and DATABASE LEAKS CYBER TEAM INDONESIA 11%, with over 60% of campaigns tied to geopolitical causes.

title: Scanning detections climbed past 1.16 trillion
description: FortiGuard Labs' behavioral trend analysis shows scan detections rose steadily through 2024, reaching 1.16 trillion current detections — a 16.7% increase over the 993 billion logged in 2024 baselines. The trend reflects industrialized reconnaissance.

title: RDP-based lateral movement seen in 88% of incidents
description: In 2024 incident investigations, RDP-based lateral movement appeared in 88% of cases. Attackers continue to abuse credential-based RDP for east-west movement, leveraging valid accounts to bypass signature detection.

title: 13 new ransomware groups emerged in 2024
description: The ransomware ecosystem fragmented further with 13 new leak-site operators including RansomHub, HellCat, Argonauts, InterLock, Bashe (APT73/Eraleig), Termite, Sarcoma, Nitrogen, Lynx, Ransomcortex and Valencia. At least six new RaaS services were advertised.

title: Cloud identity compromise signals
description: Lacework FortiCNAPP analysis surfaces the dominant early-warning indicators of cloud identity compromise. New logins from unfamiliar geographies appeared in 70% of cases, while new API activity from existing users surfaced in 20% of cases.

labels: New API activity for existing user

pageOrSection: Silent breach: identity compromise in the cloud

title: FortiGuard on industrialized cybercrime
description: Fortinet calls out the maturing Cybercrime-as-a-Service economy, where specialization across the attack chain has lowered the technical barrier to entry while raising the speed and scale of attacks.
quote: "Cybercrime-as-a-Service (CaaS) groups are using these new tools to embrace specialization, doubling down on specific segments of the attack chain."

title: Constant threats to global financial stability
description: FS-ISAC frames the financial sector as under continuous pressure from lone hackers, organized crime, and nation-state actors. The 2024 review emphasizes that tiny errors can cascade into widespread disruption across an interdependent digital economy.
quote: "The stability and continuity of the global financial system are under constant threat. Lone hackers in a basement, organized criminal gangs, and nation-state threat actors – motivated by profit, espionage, or politics – challenge the operational resilience of the financial sector and its supplier ecosystem on a daily basis."

title: Global Cyber Threat Level remained GUARDED in 2024
description: FS-ISAC's Global Cyber Threat Level (CTL), based on a holistic worldview from regional Threat Intelligence Committees, stayed at GUARDED throughout 2024 — reflecting stability despite ongoing concerns in specific threat areas.

title: AMER CTL temporarily elevated for Scattered Spider
description: On 2 May 2024, the AMER regional CTL was raised from GUARDED to ELEVATED via an out-of-cycle TIC vote due to escalating Scattered Spider activity. It returned to GUARDED on 23 May 2024 after FS-ISAC published mitigation guidance.

title: Largest ransomware payment on record
description: An undisclosed victim made the largest ransomware payment on record in 2024, totaling $75M USD. The figure illustrates how big-game hunting is driving higher payouts even as overall attack volume reportedly fell.

title: Financial & insurance share of ransomware leak sites
description: Leak site data from 2024 shows the NAICS 'financial and insurance' sector accounted for roughly 8% of all identified leaks, making it the fourth most affected sector. Ransomware attacks are now more dispersed across a wider pool of threat actors.

title: Professional services dominate ransomware victims
description: Almost 19% of ransomware victims fell within the NAICS Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services sector — many of them third-party providers to financial firms. This highlights the financial sector's heightened exposure via supply-chain incidents.

title: Financial services share of DDoS attacks
description: Per Akamai data cited by FS-ISAC, financial services was the most frequently targeted sector for DDoS attacks in 2024, absorbing 34% of all attacks — over a third of the global total.

title: EMEA share of financial-sector DDoS attacks fell in 2024
description: Akamai data cited by FS-ISAC shows that EMEA's share of DDoS attacks on the financial sector dropped from 66% in 2023 to 49% in 2024, signaling a redistribution of attacker focus across regions.

title: Top 10 fraud attack patterns (Jul–Dec 2024)
description: FS-ISAC member reporting from July to December 2024 ranks the most common fraud attack patterns. Business email scams and impersonation lead the list, ahead of account takeover, payroll diversion, and card fraud.

title: Hong Kong deepfake CFO scam loss
description: A Hong Kong finance worker paid cybercriminals $25M USD in February 2024 after being tricked by a deepfake of the company's CFO during a video conference. The incident underscores GenAI's role in scaling C-suite impersonation fraud.

title: Cryptocurrency stolen by DPRK actors in 2024
description: Per Chainalysis data cited by FS-ISAC, DPRK-linked threat actors stole $2.2B USD from cryptocurrency platforms in 2024 — funding state operations and weapons programs through skilled social engineering and supply-chain attacks.

title: DPRK share of all stolen cryptocurrency
description: DPRK cybercriminals accounted for 61% of all stolen cryptocurrency in 2024 according to Chainalysis. That share highlights how heavily North Korea relies on crypto theft to evade sanctions and finance the regime.

title: DPRK IT workers fraudulently hired in US
description: In May 2024, the US Department of Justice reported that over 300 fraudulent DPRK workers had been hired by US companies, including banks and other financial service providers — embedding insider risk inside critical institutions.

title: Mexico's share of Latin American cyber attacks
description: Mexico experienced over half of all cyber attacks in Latin America, driven largely by its economic proximity to the United States. Concentration in one market intensifies cross-border spillover risk for regional financial institutions.

title: Major 2024 supply-chain & infrastructure incidents
description: FS-ISAC's 2024 incident timeline tracks high-impact events shaping the financial sector, from January's Ivanti zero-day to December's BeyondTrust breach impacting the US Treasury — clustering heavily around mid-year supply-chain compromises.

title: Microsoft DDoS outage impact
description: A 10-hour Office, Outlook, and Azure outage triggered by a DDoS attack on Microsoft impacted financial sector users in July 2024. The disruption illustrates concentration risk inherent in heavily shared productivity and cloud platforms.

title: Snowflake customers exposed via stolen credentials
description: Up to 165 Snowflake customer databases were accessed via stolen login credentials in 2024, attributed to UNC5537. The campaign reinforced infostealer risk and the need for strong identity controls on cloud data platforms.

title: FortiGate systems breached by Chinese actors
description: State-sponsored Chinese threat actors compromised approximately 20,000 FortiGate VPN firewall systems worldwide via a single vulnerability. The campaign showcases how perimeter device flaws can be weaponized at massive scale.

title: GenAI business use cases in financial services
description: FS-ISAC outlines six headline GenAI use cases gaining traction across financial services firms and vendors in 2024 — spanning fraud detection, document summarization, financial reporting, customer support, market research, and coding.

title: Geopolitically-driven cyber activity by nation-state
description: FS-ISAC tracks four primary nation-state ecosystems impacting financial services in 2024 — the PRC (espionage & pre-positioning), Russia (disruption & disinformation), Iran (regional warfare), and DPRK (financially motivated crypto theft).

title: Supply-chain concentration is a top concern
description: FS-ISAC underscores that many financial firms share the same providers, meaning a single outage can cascade across the sector. Concentration risk persists throughout the supply chain even with third-party risk management investments.
quote: "Supply chain risk is one of the top concerns of the financial sector globally. Because many firms rely on the same service providers, an outage at one can impact many firms simultaneously. This concentration risk applies throughout the supply chain."

title: APAC DDoS campaign intensity (Oct 2024 onward)
description: FS-ISAC describes coordinated DDoS campaigns against Australia, Japan, and India starting in October 2024 — record-high volumetric attacks with a notably sustained surge through the final quarter of 2024.

title: DORA effective date
description: The EU's Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) entered into force on 17 January 2025, bringing ICT critical third-party providers into direct scope of financial regulation. Article 45 mandates structured intelligence sharing — a role FS-ISAC explicitly supports.

title: NIS2 directive sector coverage
description: By 17 October 2024, the EU's NIS2 Directive required member states to regulate cybersecurity across 18 sectors at national level. NIS2 and DORA frequently overlap, but DORA takes precedence for financial firms.

title: Regional close-up — estimated DDoS pressure share
description: Combining Akamai data and FS-ISAC's regional close-ups, EMEA remained the leading region for financial-sector DDoS in 2024 with 49% share, followed by APAC's late-2024 surge and growing pressure on NAM and LATAM.

title: Ransomware groups continually rebrand and adapt
description: FS-ISAC emphasizes ransomware operators' adaptability — including BYOVD evasion, GenAI-assisted automation, and rebranding to escape sanctions. Affiliates of high-impact groups often re-emerge under new names to evade law enforcement.
quote: "Ransomware operators have shown their ability to rebrand, re-organize, and adapt their tactics despite, and in some cases because of, law enforcement's disruptive actions."

title: AI social engineering — fight fire with fire
description: Hoxhunt's co-founder and CTO frames the 2026 outlook: generative AI is accelerating social engineering at scale, but the same tooling can power adaptive, behavior-based defenses. Sets the tone for the report's pivot from awareness to measurable human-risk reduction.
quote: "AI is fueling a new era of social engineering tactics, but it can also be the white hat that helps us fight back."

title: December 2025 AI phishing surge
description: After holding below 5% of monthly attacks for the first 11 months of 2025, AI-generated phishing exploded to 56% of reported attacks in December 2025 — a 14x increase that Hoxhunt dubbed a 'Phishmas Anti-Miracle'. The surge persisted into early 2026.

title: AI-generated share of phishing — Nov 2025 to Jan 2026
description: Surface-indicator analysis of Hoxhunt-reported phishing across three consecutive months captures the holiday-season spike: AI-tell signals jumped from 4% of emails in November to 56% in December before partially retreating to 40% in January.

title: Callback phishing campaigns Q4 2025
description: Callback phishing — emails that lure victims into calling attacker-controlled phone numbers — surged 500% in Q4 2025 per VIPRE Security telemetry cited by Hoxhunt. Phone numbers bypass email filters and enable live social engineering on the call.

title: SVG malicious attachments — 50x rise
description: Malicious SVG attachments grew 50-fold versus 2024, now representing 5% of all malicious attachments and the 3rd most common file type behind PDF and HTML. SVGs can carry embedded scripts and bypass many anti-spam tools.

title: Malicious attachment mix — H1 2025
description: PDFs dominate the malicious attachment landscape at 23.7% of all blocked files, with SVGs surging into third place at 5% (up 50-fold from 2024). HTML attachments declined sharply from ~10% in 2024 to 5.6% as defenders caught up with smuggling techniques.

title: Attachment mix shift — 2024 vs 2025
description: Year-over-year comparison shows attackers rotating away from HTML smuggling (~10% to 5.6%) and toward SVG-based payloads (~0.1% to 5%) as defenders patched HTML handling but left SVG inline rendering and attachments largely unmonitored until Microsoft disabled inline SVG in September 2025.

title: Calendar-invite phishing is 6x more effective
description: Malicious .ics calendar invites trigger a 24% failure rate versus a 4% global baseline — a 6x improvement for attackers. Auto-population of calendars before the recipient reads the email and recurring reminders are the structural advantages.

title: Quishing (QR code phishing) growth
description: QR-code phishing attacks rose 25% year-over-year in 2024, reflecting attackers' shift to image-based payloads that slip past URL filters and force users onto mobile devices outside enterprise controls.

title: Organizations reporting vishing incidents
description: 30% of organizations reported voice-phishing (vishing) incidents in 2024, with attackers increasingly combining email lures and follow-up calls (the callback phishing pattern) to defeat technical controls and harvest credentials live.

title: AI phishing — top themes
description: Generative-AI phishing concentrates on commercial lures: fake offers and promotions lead (18.6%), followed by financial-service impersonation (13.1%), invoice scams (8.3%), and HR impersonations (8.2%). The mix reflects what LLMs produce most fluently with minimal prompting.

title: AI phishing — delivery mechanism mix
description: Inside AI-generated campaigns, malicious links remain the dominant payload (43.1%), followed by open redirects (20.3%), attachments (11%), and callback-phone lures (4.9%). Links and redirects together account for nearly two-thirds of AI campaigns.

title: Callback phishing — top themes
description: Callback phishing lures concentrate on financial-service impersonation (27.1%) and invoice or subscription notices (26.6%), together driving more than half of all callback campaigns. Common brand spoofs include PayPal, Venmo, Bank of America, McAfee, eBay, and Zelle.

title: Sender-domain mix by victim mailbox provider
description: Gmail dominates malicious sending across both ecosystems: 17.9% of confirmed malicious emails into Microsoft environments and 30.1% into Google environments originate from Gmail addresses, versus 2.5% and 5.7% from Outlook respectively. Free, easy account creation drives the imbalance.

title: Top causes of ransomware infection
description: Phishing remains the single largest entry vector for ransomware infections at 54%, dwarfing poor user practices (27%), lack of cybersecurity training (26%), and malicious-website visits (14%). Categories overlap because incidents often have multiple contributing causes.

title: Average phishing breach cost
description: IBM/Ponemon's 2024 figure put the average phishing-driven breach at $4.88M, up 10% from $4.45M in 2023 and the largest year-over-year jump since the pandemic. Hoxhunt frames the trajectory as accelerating despite improved detection.

title: Average BEC loss per incident
description: Business Email Compromise hit 64% of organizations in 2024 with an average loss of $150,000 per incident. BEC remains the highest-dollar phishing variant because attackers redirect payments rather than steal credentials.

title: Breaches initiated by phishing
description: Between 80% and 95% of all breaches start with a phishing email, per the Comcast Business 2025 report cited by Hoxhunt. The wide range reflects how analysts attribute multi-stage incidents, but the floor still places phishing first among initial-access vectors.

title: Business vs personal target mix
description: Two-thirds of phishing attacks target organizational assets — credentials, invoices, and finance workflows — while one-third aim at personal accounts and bank details. The personal share ticks up in summer as attackers retool around vacation themes.

title: Real-threat reporting rises with training
description: Hoxhunt's adaptive program drives steady gains in real-threat reporting: 13% of employees report real phishing in month zero, rising to 64% at 12 months and 71% at 24 months. The curve underpins the report's '10x rise in real threat detection' headline.

title: Malicious-attachment training curve
description: On malicious-attachment simulations, reporting climbs from 34% pre-training to 80% at 14 months while failure rates collapse from 11% to under 2% — a 5.5x reduction. The pair shows how reporting and failure improve in lockstep.

title: 12-month training success by industry
description: After 12 months of Hoxhunt adaptive training, Financial Services leads with a 74% phishing-simulation success rate, while Healthcare (62%) and Retail (61%) trail — Hoxhunt attributes the gap to less time at the keyboard and higher operational stress.

title: 45x more behavioral data points
description: A 10,000-person company running a Behavior Change Program (50% engagement, 36 simulations/year) generates 180,000 behavioral data points annually versus 4,000 for quarterly SAT — a 45x insights multiplier that Hoxhunt cites as the foundation of personalised coaching.

title: Recent training quadruples reporting
description: Hoxhunt cites Verizon's 2025 DBIR finding that users with recent security training report phishing emails at 21% versus a 5% baseline — a 4x relative increase that establishes the macro link between training cadence and resilience.
quote: "Users who had more recent training reported phishing emails at 21% vs. 5% baseline — a 4x relative increase."

title: Communications fail 40% more than Finance
description: Communications, Sales & Marketing and Business Development teams record the highest phishing-simulation failure rates — Communications alone fails 40% more often than Finance. High inbound email volume and divided attention explain the gap.

title: Sophistication gap has all but disappeared
description: Huntress's executive summary highlights how attackers are standardizing enterprise-grade tradecraft across businesses of all sizes. Advanced techniques like BYOVD, defense tampering, and UAC bypasses have become the norm even against SMBs.
quote: "The gap between sophistication in attacks on large enterprises and smaller businesses has narrowed—in fact, it's all but disappeared."

title: RATs drove 75% of remote access incidents
description: Remote Access Trojans maintained their top spot for remote access delivery in 2024. AsyncRAT, NetSupport RAT, and Jupyter dominated the landscape, with three RATs accounting for one-third of all RAT types observed.
pageOrSection: Attacker Tools and Techniques / Remote Access Trojans

title: Top 3 ransomware groups drove 54% of incidents
description: RansomHub, Lynx (formerly Inc), and Akira collectively accounted for 54% of Huntress's ransomware incidents in 2024. All three target SMBs and offer high affiliate payouts, often 80-90% of ransom paid.

title: Average time-to-ransom is nearly 17 hours
description: Across investigated incidents, Huntress measured an average time-to-ransom (TTR) of 16.88 hours from initial access to ransomware deployment. Some groups like Play, Dharma/Crysis, and Akira deploy ransomware in around six hours.

title: 18 malicious actions on average before ransomware
description: Ransomware groups performed an average of 18 identifiable malicious actions in the 48 hours before deploying ransomware. Extortion-focused groups like Phobos performed up to 37 actions, while smash-and-grab groups like Play averaged only 8.

title: ConnectWise ScreenConnect abused in 74.5% of RMM incidents
description: ConnectWise ScreenConnect was the most abused remote access tool in 2024, accounting for nearly three out of four RMM-abuse incidents. The February SlashAndGrab campaign (CVE-2024-1709/1708) was the largest driver.

title: 65.5% of Huntress detections occurred at execution phase
description: Huntress's strongest catch point in 2024 was the MITRE ATT&CK Execution tactic (TA0002), where attackers had to run their payload. Persistence (15.5%) and Defense Evasion (8.6%) followed.

title: 90.5% of BYOVD use went to privilege elevation
description: When attackers brought their own vulnerable drivers (BYOVD) in 2024, over 90% used them to elevate privileges to ring 0 rather than to tamper with EDR. Huntress attributes this to less-sophisticated EDR in non-enterprise environments.

title: Top threat categories in 2024
description: Infostealers led all observed incidents at 24%, followed closely by malicious scripts at 22%. Malware and RATs rounded out the top four threat categories observed across Huntress telemetry in 2024.

title: Industries targeted in 2024
description: Education (21%) and Healthcare (17%) were the most targeted industries, making up 38% of all incidents. Technology, Government, and Manufacturing each saw double-digit shares.

title: Threats targeting healthcare
description: Healthcare environments faced malicious scripts (22%) as their top risk, followed by infostealers (19%) and malware (16%). Java-based RATs like JRat/Adwind and STRRAT were notably prevalent in this sector.

title: Most prevalent ransomware operators in 2024
description: RansomHub topped Huntress's 2024 list at 21.4% as ex-LockBit affiliates migrated in. Inc/Lynx and Akira followed at 16.8% and 15.8%, while older brands like LockBit (1.4%) and Cl0p (1.2%) shrank dramatically.

title: Average time-to-ransom by group (hours)
description: Rapid (43.42h) and Sodinokibi (38.46h) were the slowest; Play (4.22h), Dharma/Crysis (4.44h), and Akira (6.10h) the fastest. Smash-and-grab groups deploy ransomware within hours of initial access.

title: Most used hacking tools in 2024
description: Cobalt Strike (31.7%) remains the dominant hacking tool, followed by Mimikatz (17.6%) and Sysinternals abuse (17.1%). Advanced IP Scanner and Metasploit round out the top five.

title: Most common remote access methods
description: Generic RATs (42.7%) and ScreenConnect (12.3%) dominated remote access methods in 2024. Three named RAT families (AsyncRAT, NetSupport, Jupyter) collectively accounted for nearly 25%.

title: Top abused RMM and remote tools
description: ConnectWise ScreenConnect dominated RMM abuse with 74.5% of incidents. RDP (14.6%), LogMeIn (4.7%), and TeamViewer (4.4%) made up the bulk of the remainder.

title: Most witnessed CVE exploitation
description: ScreenConnect (60.1%) led traditional exploitation in 2024, followed by CrushFTP (42.7%) and Microsoft Exchange (30.1%). BYOVD driver exploitation reached 14.6%, signaling its mainstreaming.

title: LockBit activity collapsed after February 2024 takedown
description: 87% of 2024's LockBit activity occurred between February 17 and March 1, after Operation Cronos disrupted the group. LockBit then shifted focus to enterprise targets, leaving SMB activity to splinter groups like RansomHub.

title: LockBit drove 87.1% of ScreenConnect campaign payloads
description: During the February 2024 SlashAndGrab campaign exploiting CVE-2024-1709, LockBit was the dominant payload at 87.1% of attempted deliveries. Dridex, WinZip PUP, Emotet, Trickbot, and miners made up the rest.

title: MITRE ATT&CK phase where Huntress detected attackers
description: Huntress catches attackers most often at Execution (65.5%), followed by Persistence (15.5%) and Defense Evasion (8.6%). This shapes the layered detection strategy across endpoints.

title: Scripting language abuse in 2024
description: PowerShell dominated scripting abuse at 45% of incidents, with JavaScript (15.6%) and batch files (14.7%) far behind. Legacy languages MSHTA, WMI, and WScript combined for just 8.4%.

title: Attackers most active 12:00-20:00 UTC
description: Hands-on-keyboard activity peaked between 12:00 UTC and 20:00 UTC, mapping closely to US East Coast business hours. Attackers likely operate during these windows to blend with normal activity or remain on active devices.

title: Identity threat (ITDR) incident frequency
description: Microsoft 365 attacks dominated identity threats in 2024 — VPN rule violations (30.3%) and inbox rule modifications (25.4%) led, with credential theft (8%), token theft (5.4%), and AitM attempts (1.9%) rounding out the picture.

title: Stolen browser tokens sell for under $10
description: Infostealers harvest browser, location, VPN, and OS metadata; brokers then sell complete victim sessions for less than $10 per individual, letting attackers mimic legitimate logins and bypass MFA.

title: VPN and proxy services abused by attackers
description: NordVPN topped attacker-favored VPN abuse at 20% in 2024, while SurfEasy and ExpressVPN combined for 23%. TOR was abused less than 2% — a sharp decline from its prior staple-tool status.

title: Most prevalent phishing themes
description: E-signature impersonation (28.8%) and image-based content (23.9%) led 2024 phishing themes. QR-code phishing (quishing) made up 8.1% but is forecast to escalate in 2025.

title: Chromeloader = ~70% of education infostealers
description: ChromeLoader dominated the education sector, accounting for nearly 70% of all infostealer activity across Huntress's education partner environments in 2024.

title: RMM abuse = 17.3% of remote access methods
description: Remote monitoring and management (RMM) abuse made up 17.3% of all remote access methods in 2024, making it the second-most common technique after RAT-based access. ScreenConnect drove most of the volume.

title: Ransomware pivots from encryption to extortion
description: Huntress flags a strategic shift among ransomware operators away from file encryption toward pure data theft and extortion — a cost-saving move as encryption defenses mature and DLP lags behind.
quote: "Attackers are becoming more aware of these circumstances and are opting to steal data and hold it for ransom."

title: Huntress protects 3M endpoints and 1M identities
description: Huntress's 2025 report draws on telemetry from over 3 million endpoints and 1 million identities worldwide, monitored by a 24/7 team of security analysts and researchers.

title: Cybercrime threat landscape grew more complex in 2024
description: KELA's CEO opens the report by framing the convergence of cybercriminals, hacktivists, and state-sponsored actors as the defining shift of 2024. Alliances, MaaS platforms, and credential marketplaces underpin a powerful, malicious infrastructure.
quote: "In 2024, the cyber threat landscape became more complex. Threat actors became increasingly diversified, forming alliances and using methods that blurred traditional distinctions between cybercriminals, hacktivists, and state-sponsored groups."

title: Machines infected by infostealers in 2024
description: KELA observed at least 4.3 million machines globally infected by infostealer malware in 2024 based on its data lake. The figure is slightly higher than 2023 and underpins the infostealer-as-initial-access narrative.

title: Compromised credentials from infostealer logs
description: The 4.3 million infected machines accounted for more than 330 million compromised credentials, fueling account takeover, espionage, and ransomware operations downstream.

title: ULP credentials lists shared by cybercriminals
description: Beyond direct infostealer logs, KELA observed 3.9 billion credentials shared as url:login:pass (ULP) compilations, most of which are sourced from infostealer logs aggregated by underground actors.

title: Monthly infected bots in 2024
description: KELA's data lake tracked monthly bot infections throughout 2024, peaking in April-May and tapering toward year-end (later months may rise as data is collected in 2025). Annual total exceeds 4.3 million machines.
pageOrSection: Bots infected by infostealer malware in 2024

title: Top countries by infostealer bot infections (2024)
description: Brazil and India led national infection counts in KELA's data lake, followed by Indonesia, Turkey, and Egypt. The US ranked seventh among individually identified countries, with a substantial long tail across LATAM and Asia.
pageOrSection: Bots infected by infostealer malware in 2024 per countries

title: Top infostealer malware strains in 2024
description: Lumma led infostealer market share at 40.38%, followed by StealC and Redline (disrupted October 2024). The top three strains accounted for more than 75% of infected machines in KELA's data lake.

title: Compromised credentials by sensitive service category (2024)
description: Business cloud solutions and CMS topped the list of compromised credential categories, followed by email and user authentication systems. Almost 40% of infected machines contained corporate credentials, totaling 7.5 million sensitive credentials across 1.7 million bots.
pageOrSection: Compromised credentials to sensitive services in 2024

title: Snowflake attack: companies affected
description: The UNC5537 group used infostealer-stolen credentials to access Snowflake customer accounts lacking MFA. The campaign became the largest infostealer-related attack of 2024, affecting at least 165 companies that later saw data leaked or sold on forums.

title: Ransomware and extortion victims tracked in 2024
description: KELA tracked over 5,230 ransomware and extortion victims in 2024, a 10.5% rise versus 2023. Victims were claimed by almost 100 distinct actors, 28.5% more than the prior year.

title: Growth in active ransomware actors
description: Almost 100 distinct ransomware/extortion actors claimed victims in 2024, a 28.5% increase over 2023. KELA also identified over 60 new groups, with 13 ceasing activity within the year.

title: Top countries affected by ransomware (2024)
