description: The US represented more than half of all ransomware victims at 52.52%, far outpacing Canada (5.18%) and the UK (4.89%). The top 10 list spans North America, Europe, LATAM, and Asia, underscoring the global but US-concentrated footprint.

title: Top sectors affected by ransomware (2024)
description: Professional Services (16.27%) and Manufacturing & Industrial Products (16.14%) led affected sectors, followed by Engineering & Construction, Healthcare & Life Sciences, Technology, and Consumer & Retail. Critical sectors like Government and Education round out the top 10.

title: Top active ransomware actors (2024)
description: RansomHub took the 2024 crown with 526 claimed victims, dislodging LockBit (502) from its 2023 top position. Play, Akira, and Medusa round out the top five most prolific groups.

title: RansomHub dethrones LockBit in record time
description: RansomHub launched in February 2024 and by year-end had claimed more victims than any other group. KELA highlights its rapid scaling and Golang/C++ locker targeting Windows, Linux, macOS, and ESXi.
quote: "It's worth highlighting that RansomHub is the first ransom group in recent years to surpass LockBit."

title: Victims claimed by multiple ransomware groups
description: Over 30 ransom victims were claimed twice or more in 2024, suggesting collaboration between groups, parallel attacks, or shared initial access via the same broker.

title: Most discussed 2024 CVEs on cybercrime forums
description: CVE-2024-21762 (FortiOS out-of-bounds write) led cybercrime forum chatter with 67 mentions, followed by another FortiOS flaw and D-Link, Microsoft Outlook, and Check Point VPN vulnerabilities. Fortinet and remote code execution dominated underground interest.
pageOrSection: Top 5 CVE-2024 mentioned on cybercrime forums

title: Time from CVE disclosure to cybercrime chatter
description: On average, CVE-related discussions by malicious actors appear within one month following disclosure. Some vulnerabilities are discussed the very same day, while others remain active topics nearly a year later.

title: New hacktivist groups tracked in 2024
description: KELA tracked over 200 new hacktivist groups in 2024, with approximately 300 notable groups active throughout the year. Activity was driven primarily by the Russo-Ukrainian war and the Israel-Hamas conflict.

title: DDoS attacks claimed by hacktivists
description: At least 3,500 DDoS attacks were claimed by notable hacktivist actors in 2024, identified via Telegram messages mentioning victim domains plus accessibility-report URLs as proof.

title: Top hacktivist groups by DDoS claim share (2024)
description: Pro-Indonesian Ethersec Team Cyber (8.05%) narrowly led the DDoS claim share, with pro-Russian NoName057(16) (8.00%) and Dunia Maya Team (7.58%) close behind. The top 10 groups accounted for almost half of all DDoS claims.

title: Average daily cyberattacks on Taiwan in 2024
description: Taiwan's government reported an average of 2.4 million cyberattacks per day in 2024, with a significant spike in the 24 hours before the election. Chinese cyber actors targeted telecommunications, transportation, and defense sectors.

title: Russian Doppelganger disinformation funding
description: The Russian Doppelganger disinformation campaign used 32 spoofed domains to impersonate US media. Two Russia Today employees facilitated the laundering of nearly USD 10 million to fund these election-influence activities.

title: LLM exploit-keyword mentions on cybercrime forums
description: KELA observed a 94% surge in mentions combining LLM names (ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, Claude, Llama) with exploit keywords like 'jailbreak' from 2023 to 2024. Cybercriminals are sharing techniques in dedicated forum sections.

title: Compromised ChatGPT accounts in 2024
description: The number of compromised ChatGPT accounts in KELA's infostealer dataset surged from 154,000 in 2023 to 3,000,000 in 2024 — a roughly 19x increase reflecting both ChatGPT adoption and credential theft.

title: Compromised LLM chatbot accounts: 2023 vs 2024
description: Both ChatGPT and Gemini saw explosive growth in stolen account counts year-over-year. ChatGPT compromised accounts climbed from 154K to 3M; Gemini from 12K to 174K — credentials harvested by infostealers can be reused to abuse LLMs.

title: GPT-4o jailbreak success via word transformation
description: KELA's AIFort simulation found that word transformation — replacing sensitive words with synonyms or splitting payloads — bypassed GPT-4o safety controls in 27% of tests, illustrating prompt-injection effectiveness against frontier LLMs.
pageOrSection: Top 10 security risks associated with LLMs

title: Convergence will define 2025's threat landscape
description: KELA's closing prediction emphasizes the blurring of cybercrime and state-sponsored operations, with AI amplifying disinformation and attacks, while infostealers and RaaS remain core access vectors.
quote: "The convergence of cybercrime and state-sponsored operations will further blur attribution lines, making threat intelligence and proactive defense strategies more critical than ever."

title: Global baseline Phish-prone Percentage
description: Across 14.5 million users in 62,400 organizations, KnowBe4 found that 33.1% of untrained employees clicked a simulated phishing link before any security awareness training — meaning roughly one in three workers is susceptible at baseline.

title: Training drives an 86% drop in click rates after one year
description: After 12 months of ongoing KnowBe4 security awareness training, the global average Phish-prone Percentage fell from 33.1% to 4.1% — an 86% reduction in phishing susceptibility.

title: Over 40% reduction after just 90 days of training
description: Organizations implementing security awareness training see Phish-prone Percentage drop by more than 40% within the first three months, demonstrating that meaningful human-risk reduction is achievable on a quarterly cadence.

title: Large enterprises have a 40.5% baseline click rate
description: Organizations with 10,000+ employees show a global baseline Phish-prone Percentage of 40.5%, compared with 24.6% for small organizations of 1–250 employees — larger workforces present a materially larger attack surface.

title: Healthcare's staggering 54.8% click rate in large North American orgs
description: Healthcare & Pharmaceuticals organizations with 1,000+ employees in North America showed an initial click rate of 54.8% — more than half of all users fell for the simulated phish before any training was delivered.

title: 67.7 million simulated phishing tests analyzed
description: The 2025 benchmark draws on 67.7 million simulated phishing tests delivered to 14.5 million users across 62,400 organizations spanning 19 industries and seven geographical regions over a three-year period.

title: North America posts the largest improvement rate at 89.5%
description: Among all regions tracked, North America achieved the highest average improvement rate (89.5%) after one year of ongoing training, narrowly ahead of South America at 88.9%. Every region surveyed exceeded 80% improvement.

title: Two out of five users in large NA orgs clicked
description: Erich Kron, KnowBe4 security advocate, on the gravity of the North American baseline finding: in large enterprises, more than two in five users took the bait — a sobering reminder of how exposed human risk leaves organizations before any training is layered in.
quote: "This means that in large organizations, more than two out of every five users clicked on simulated phishing attacks."

title: Social engineering is an attack on human emotions
description: KnowBe4 frames phishing, smishing, vishing and BEC as a fundamentally psychological problem — adversaries exploit emotional exhaustion and System-1 thinking to bypass otherwise capable defenders.
quote: "Social engineering — the primary way ransomware spreads and the key factor behind BEC attacks and other phishing/vishing/smishing attacks — is an attack on human emotions."
pageOrSection: Social Engineering Is a Mental Game

title: North America click rate progression: 37.1% → 3.9%
description: Average North American Phish-prone Percentage across the three KnowBe4 measurement phases: baseline, 90 days of training, and after one year. The trajectory shows steep, sustained reduction.

title: Healthcare large orgs: 54.8% → 3.7% after one year
description: Healthcare & Pharmaceutical organizations with 1,000+ employees in North America dropped their initial 54.8% click rate to just 3.7% after one year of continuous training — one of the most dramatic improvements in the dataset.
pageOrSection: Tools and Education Can Make the Difference

title: Baseline click rate climbs with organization size
description: Global baseline Phish-prone Percentage scales steadily with workforce size, jumping from 24.6% at sub-250-employee organizations to 40.5% at 10,000+ employee enterprises.

title: Baseline Phish-prone Percentage by region
description: Baseline (pre-training) Phish-prone Percentage across the seven KnowBe4 reporting regions. South America, North America and Australia & New Zealand top the at-risk ranking; Asia and the UK & Ireland sit at the bottom.

title: Phish-prone Percentage by region across all three training phases
description: Multi-series comparison of regional Phish-prone Percentage at baseline, after 90 days of training, and after one year. Every region collapses to single-digit click rates by the one-year mark.

title: North America: PPP by organization size across training phases
description: North American Phish-prone Percentage broken out by organization size and training phase. Large enterprises start the worst (42%) but show the biggest absolute improvement, dropping to 4.1% after one year.

title: Top three most phish-prone industries (global baseline)
description: Globally, Healthcare & Pharmaceuticals, Insurance, and Retail & Wholesale ranked as the three industries with the highest baseline Phish-prone Percentage in the 2025 dataset.

title: Global baseline PPP by organization size
description: Baseline Phish-prone Percentage scales clearly with workforce size: small organizations (1–250) sit at 24.6% while enterprises of 10,000+ employees reach 40.5%, a 16-point gap.

title: Global training journey: baseline → 90 days → 1 year
description: The headline KnowBe4 narrative in a single chart: global PPP collapses from 33.1% at baseline to roughly 19% after 90 days of training and to 4.1% after one year — an 86% net reduction.

title: Regional improvement rates after one year of training
description: All regions exceeded an 80% improvement rate after a year of training, with North America (89.5%) and South America (88.9%) leading. The chart visualizes the percentage reduction in PPP from baseline to one year for each region.

title: Sectors with the strongest training payoff (1,000–9,999 employees)
description: For mid-to-large organizations (1,000–9,999 employees), Healthcare & Pharmaceuticals, Hospitality, and Legal each achieved a 91% Phish-prone Percentage improvement after 12 months of training — the highest sector returns recorded.

title: Large NA orgs see the steepest 90-day drop
description: After only 90 days of training, large North American organizations (1,000+ employees) cut their click rate from 42% to 18.5% — the biggest absolute reduction at the 90-day mark, outpacing both small and mid-size peers.

title: U.S. accounts for 51.7% of global ransomware attacks
description: Per Intel 471 data cited in the KnowBe4 benchmark, the United States accounted for 51.7% of the 4,205 global ransomware attacks analyzed in 2024, with Canada the second most-targeted country — underscoring why North American human-risk reduction matters disproportionately.

title: Global median dwell time rose to 14 days
description: Mandiant's global median dwell time increased from 11 days in 2024 to 14 days in 2025, driven by long-term espionage and DPRK IT worker operations establishing stealthy, persistent access on edge devices that lack standard telemetry.

title: Time-to-hand-off collapsed to 22 seconds
description: The median time between an initial access event and the hand-off to a secondary threat group dropped from more than 8 hours in 2022 to just 22 seconds in 2025. Initial access partners now pre-stage tooling for follow-on groups instead of selling access on underground markets.
pageOrSection: A Minor Infection Today Can Be a Ransomware Attack Tomorrow

title: Over 500K hours of frontline IR
description: M-Trends 2026 is grounded in more than 500,000 hours of frontline incident investigations conducted by Mandiant in 2025, combined with Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) telemetry.

title: Hand-offs happening in under 30 seconds
description: Mandiant's foreword underscores how initial access partners now work directly with secondary groups instead of selling access on underground markets, collapsing the response window for defenders.
quote: "We are observing a rising trend where initial access partners work directly with secondary groups rather than selling access on underground markets. This results in a 'hand-off' that sometimes occurs in less than 30 seconds, creating a scenario where 'minor' alerts can very quickly become major compromises."

title: Ransomware is now recovery denial
description: Mandiant frames ransomware as a resilience problem: attackers are no longer just encrypting data, they are systematically destroying the ability to recover by targeting backups, identity services, and virtualization layers.
quote: "Ransomware groups are no longer just encrypting data; they are actively destroying the ability to recover. They target the most critical systems, effectively forcing a choice: pay or rebuild."
pageOrSection: Ransomware is Now a Resilience Problem

title: Initial infection vectors, 2025
description: Exploits remained the most common initial infection vector for the sixth consecutive year at 32%. Voice phishing surged to the second spot at 11%, while email phishing fell to 6% from 14% in 2024.

title: Voice phishing surges as email phishing declines
description: Voice-based social engineering rose sharply in 2025 to 11% of initial infection vectors, while email phishing fell from 14% in 2024 to 6% in 2025. The distinction matters because interactive attacks resist automated controls.

title: Threat cluster motivation shifted in 2025
description: Financially motivated groups fell to 41% of threat clusters observed in 2025 (down from 55% in 2024), while cyber espionage groups doubled their share to 16% (up from 8%).

title: Financially motivated activity at 41%
description: Financially motivated threat clusters represented 41% of activity observed by Mandiant in 2025, a notable decline from 55% in 2024 as espionage-aligned activity rose.

title: Cyber espionage share doubled to 16%
description: Cyber espionage threat clusters grew from 8% of observed activity in 2024 to 16% in 2025, reflecting heightened state-aligned operations and DPRK IT worker incidents.

title: How breaches were detected in 2025
description: Internal detection rose to 52% of incidents in 2025 (up from 43% in 2024), external notifications fell to 34% (down from 43%), and adversaries informed organizations of a compromise 14% of the time.

title: Internal detection climbed to 52%
description: Organizations first identified malicious activity themselves in 52% of investigations in 2025, an improvement from 43% in 2024 that suggests maturing detection capabilities.

title: Detection source for ransomware incidents
description: In ransomware cases, adversaries notified the target 44% of the time, internal detection occurred 41% of the time, and external entities notified 15%. The high adversary share is consistent with the ransomware business model.

title: Malware family categories observed
description: Of malware families observed in 2025 investigations, 36% were backdoors, 11% downloaders, 10% ransomware, 10% droppers, and 9% credential stealers, reflecting heavy reliance on stealth and follow-on access tooling.

title: 30% of ransomware starts with prior compromise
description: In ransomware-related incidents, prior compromise was the most frequently observed initial infection vector at 30%, reflecting the rise of initial access partners pre-staging access for follow-on groups.

title: Most-targeted industries in 2025
description: High tech overtook financial services as the most targeted vertical in 2025, followed by financial, business and professional services, and healthcare. Investigations spanned more than 16 industry verticals.

title: 16+ industries impacted
description: Mandiant investigations in 2025 spanned more than 16 industry verticals, signalling broad and indiscriminate threat actor targeting across the global economy.

title: Espionage dwell time: 122 days
description: Cyber espionage and North Korean IT worker incidents had a median dwell time of 122 days in 2025, reflecting deliberate, stealthy long-term access objectives.

title: BRICKSTORM averaging 393 days dwell
description: Cases involving the stealthy BRICKSTORM backdoor averaged 393 days of dwell time, far beyond standard 90-day log retention windows and leaving organizations blind to the initial access vector.

title: Top malware families and Cobalt Strike's drop
description: After five consecutive years as the most frequently observed malware family, Cobalt Strike BEACON fell to fourth in 2025. GOLDVEIN.JAVA downloader took the top spot, followed by REDBIKE (Akira) ransomware.

title: Hand-off time crashed from hours to seconds
description: The median window between initial access and hand-off to a secondary threat group has collapsed dramatically, from over 8 hours in 2022 to just 22 seconds in 2025 (values shown in seconds).
pageOrSection: A Minor Infection Today Can Be a Ransomware Attack Tomorrow

title: Adversaries inform victims 14% of the time
description: Across all 2025 investigations, threat actors themselves notified the targeted organization of a compromise in 14% of cases, primarily driven by ransomware extortion notes.

title: Edge devices as long-term blind spots
description: Mandiant highlights how undetected long-term access on edge devices that lack telemetry has become a defining trait of 2025 intrusions, fuelling the dwell-time rise.
quote: "A subset of adversaries are remaining undetected on networks for longer periods of time, often by establishing persistence in edge devices that typically lack standard telemetry."

title: Exploits remain top vector 6 years running
description: Exploits were the most common initial infection vector at 32% in 2025, marking the sixth consecutive year vulnerabilities have led Mandiant's rankings. Zero-day and n-day attacks against internet-facing systems continue to drive incidents.

title: 36% of malware families were backdoors
description: Backdoors dominated malware families observed in 2025 at 36% share, reflecting attacker emphasis on persistence and follow-on access over disruptive payloads.

title: Voice phishing climbs to second vector
description: Voice phishing surged to 11% of initial infection vectors in 2025, becoming the second most common entry point and overtaking email phishing for the first time as attackers shift to interactive social engineering.

title: 100 trillion security signals processed daily
description: Microsoft processes more than 100 trillion security signals every day from endpoints, cloud services, identity systems, and partner networks. This planet-scale telemetry powers the defenses and insights presented throughout the Microsoft Digital Defense Report 2025.

title: 5 billion emails screened daily
description: Microsoft screens roughly 5 billion emails each day on average to protect users from malware and phishing. The volume highlights both the dominance of email as an initial-access vector and the scale of defensive automation required to counter it.

title: 38 million identity risk detections per day
description: Microsoft analyzes 38 million identity risk detections on an average day, alongside blocking 4.5 million net-new malware files. The figure underscores why identity has become the dominant attack surface and the volume of telemetry required to keep ahead of it.

title: Espionage is rare; money rules
description: In Microsoft's incident response engagements where motive could be determined, only 4% of attacks were driven purely by espionage. The majority were financially motivated extortion, ransomware, and data theft operations.
quote: "Threat actors were motivated solely by espionage in only 4% of our engagements."
pageOrSection: How threat actors are shaping the cyber risk environment

title: Identified motivations in incident response engagements
description: Across Microsoft Incident Response and DART engagements, financially motivated outcomes dominate. Data theft, extortion, and destructive/human-operated ransomware together account for the vast majority of identified motivations; espionage trails far behind.
pageOrSection: How threat actors are shaping the cyber risk environment

title: Initial access vectors: FY24 vs FY25
description: Microsoft Incident Response compares the most common initial-access vectors across two fiscal years. Exploitation of public-facing applications and valid accounts climbed, while phishing remained a leading vector and supply-chain compromise more than tripled in share.
pageOrSection: How threat actors are shaping the cyber risk environment

title: Countries most frequently impacted by cyber threats (Jan-Jun 2025)
description: The United States accounts for nearly a quarter of impacted Microsoft customers, with the UK, Israel, Germany, and Ukraine rounding out the top five. The distribution reflects geopolitical hotspots and Microsoft's commercial footprint.
pageOrSection: How threat actors are shaping the cyber risk environment

title: Top 10 global sectors most impacted by threat actors
description: Government agencies and IT lead the most-impacted sectors during the first half of 2025, each accounting for 17% of observed activity. Research and academia rank third — a sector consistently exploited as a stepping stone into other targets.
pageOrSection: How threat actors are shaping the cyber risk environment

title: Identity-based attacks surged 32%
description: In the first half of 2025, identity-based attacks rose by 32% year over year. Research and academia accounted for 39% of all identity attacks — sectors with complex tenants and inconsistent MFA enforcement that frequently serve as adversary testing grounds.
pageOrSection: Identity, access, and the cybercrime economy

title: MFA still blocks the overwhelming majority of attacks
description: Despite years of evolving attacker tradecraft, modern multifactor authentication continues to block more than 99% of identity-based attacks, making it one of the highest-leverage controls organizations can deploy.
quote: "MFA still blocks over 99% of unauthorized access attempts."

title: How identity attacks break down (share of total)
description: More than 97% of identity attacks are password spray or replay; advanced techniques such as token theft, AiTM, and consent phishing remain a small minority by volume but carry higher impact when successful.

title: 20 ASNs drive 80% of password spray
description: Just 20 ASNs — only 0.04% of all autonomous systems carrying authentication traffic — account for more than 80% of malicious password spray activity globally. Concentration this extreme means targeted ASN-level blocking is highly effective.
pageOrSection: Password spray: Anatomy of a high-volume attack

title: Top five infostealers observed
description: Lumma Stealer dominated the infostealer landscape this year, accounting for more than half of observed infections among Microsoft Defender Threat Expert notifications, well ahead of Atomic, Node.js-based stealers, Sys01, and Rhadamanthys.
pageOrSection: Human-operated attacks and ransomware — From infostealers to ransomware

title: Five most prolific ransomware families
description: Akira led the ransomware leak-site landscape in 2025 with 22% of victims, followed by RansomHub, Fog, Qilin, and Play. The top five accounted for roughly 56% of all ransomware victims across 120 active variants tracked by Intel 471.

title: Top 10 industries impacted by ransomware
description: Industrial products and engineering/construction lead ransomware victim counts in 2025, with retail, healthcare, and technology rounding out the most-targeted verticals. Data is drawn from Intel 471 ransomware leak-site tracking.
pageOrSection: Top ten industries impacted by ransomware

title: Hybrid cloud now in 40%+ of ransomware
description: Two years ago, fewer than 5% of ransomware attacks involved hybrid components. Today over 40% leverage on-prem-to-cloud lateral movement, using compromised identities and tools like AADInternals to compromise cloud apps and delete VMs and backups.

title: Data exfiltration in 82% of ransomware incidents
description: With EDR slowing encryption-stage attacks (growth fell from 102% to 7% YoY), ransomware operators have pivoted to data theft. Microsoft observed large-scale data exfiltration in 82% of ransomware incidents this year, with 79% involving an RMM tool.

title: Top initial access methods seen by Defender Experts
description: ClickFix — a social-engineering technique that tricks users into pasting attacker-supplied commands — became the most common initial access method observed by Microsoft Defender Experts in 2025, ahead of traditional phishing and password spray.
pageOrSection: Social engineering exploits — Top initial access methods

title: AI phishing hits 54% click-through
description: AI-automated phishing emails achieved a 54% click-through rate versus 12% for standard attempts — a 4.5x lift. AI also has the potential to increase phishing profitability by up to 50x by scaling highly targeted attacks at minimal cost.

title: $4B in fraud blocked in one year
description: Between April 2024 and April 2025 Microsoft thwarted USD 4 billion of fraudulent transactions and scams — many likely aided by AI-generated content — and rejected 49,000 bogus partner-program enrollment attempts.

title: AI-generated IDs surged 195% globally
description: Use of AI-generated identity documents grew 195% globally year over year and now often outperforms classical forgeries in convincing verification systems — even defeating liveness checks used during selfie or document upload flows.
pageOrSection: Fraud and social engineering — The rise of deepfakes

title: Azure cloud alert increases (second 100 days vs first 100 days of 2025)
description: Microsoft Defender for Cloud telemetry shows sharp escalations across cloud attack categories in mid-2025. Destructive impact campaigns jumped 87%, data-collection alerts rose 58%, and credential-access attempts increased 23%.
comparison: second 100 days vs first 100 days of 2025

title: Cloud container infection types
description: Cryptojacking dominates Kubernetes and container attacks at 58% of cloud-native infections observed by Microsoft Defender for Cloud, followed by credential theft, known attack tools, and web shells.

title: Median time to compromise by container infection type
description: Crypto miners hit fastest, compromising new containers within ~6.8 days; credential theft averages 8.7 days; known attack tools 12.7 days; and web shells 19.3 days. Most container compromises occur within 48 hours of deployment.

title: Most-targeted sectors by nation-state actors
description: Nation-state cyber activity continues to prioritize espionage. IT alone accounted for 26% of nation-state targeting, with research and academia, government, and think tanks/NGOs together representing the largest share of intelligence collection.

title: Top targeted countries by nation-state activity
description: Israel, the United States, and Ukraine led nation-state targeting in 2025, reflecting active geopolitical conflicts. The UAE, UK, and Korea round out the top recipients of state-sponsored attacks observed in Microsoft notifications.
pageOrSection: Regional sample of nation-state activity levels observed

title: Unique orgs with identity compromise signals, by sector
description: Research and academia dwarf every other vertical with 4,647 unique organizations showing identity compromise signals between December 2024 and May 2025 — far ahead of services, technology, and manufacturing.
pageOrSection: Identity, access, and the cybercrime economy

title: 368 access brokers, 4,000+ victims
description: In the past year Intel 471 identified 368 distinct access brokers whose listings affected 68 industries across 131 countries and more than 4,000 victims. Brokers primarily targeted victims in the United States (31%), United Kingdom (6%), and Thailand (5%).
pageOrSection: Access brokers: The hidden gatekeepers of cybercrime

title: 2,300+ malicious domains seized in Lumma takedown
description: In May 2025 Microsoft's DCU, the US DOJ, Europol, JC3, and partners disrupted Lumma Stealer by seizing or blocking over 2,300 malicious domains. Follow-on takedown notices drove a 68% reduction in active C2 servers, cutting their average lifespan from 49 to 18 days.
pageOrSection: Disrupting cybercrime ecosystems: Lessons from the Lumma Stealer takedown

title: A 14-minute ransomware containment
description: In February 2025 a global shipping company narrowly averted catastrophe when its defenses stopped a ransomware attack 14 minutes after observation — with encryption halted one minute and eight seconds after it began.
quote: "The time from observation to disruption was a mere 14 minutes, with encryption stopped one minute and eight seconds after it began."
pageOrSection: A ransomware attack with potential global impact stopped in under two minutes

title: NCSC CEO: It is time to act
description: Richard Horne, NCSC CEO, frames the 2025 review with an urgent call to UK business leaders. He highlights that cyber attacks now have real-world operational consequences far beyond IT systems.
quote: "Empty shelves and stalled production lines are a stark reminder that cyber attacks no longer just affect computers and data, but real business, real products, and real lives."

title: Highly significant incidents up 50% for third consecutive year
description: The NCSC reports a 50% year-over-year rise in 'highly significant' cyber incidents — attacks with serious impact on central government, UK essential services, large portions of the population, or the UK economy. This marks the third consecutive year of growth in this top-severity category.

title: NCSC handled 429 incidents in 2024–2025
description: Of 1,727 incident tips received during the September 2024 to August 2025 review period, the NCSC's incident management team handled 429 incidents directly. The figure is in line with the prior year (430).

title: Nationally significant incidents more than doubled
description: Nationally significant incidents rose to 204 in the 2024–2025 review period, up from 89 the prior year — a 129% increase. This category now represents 48% of all incidents handled by the NCSC.

title: NCSC incidents handled and significant incidents, 2021–2025
description: Four-year trend of NCSC incident management activity. While the number of tips received has plateaued, significant and highly significant incidents have risen sharply, with 2024–2025 showing a dramatic step-change.

title: Cyber incident tips received by NCSC
description: The NCSC received 1,727 incident tips in 2024–2025, a slight decline from the 1,957 reported the prior year. Tip volume has remained broadly stable, while severity has escalated sharply.

title: China-linked Flax Typhoon botnet: 260,000+ devices
description: In September 2024 the NCSC and allies exposed Integrity Technology Group (Flax Typhoon), revealing a botnet of over 260,000 compromised devices worldwide. The disclosure was followed in August 2025 by an advisory linking three China-based companies to campaigns overlapping with Salt Typhoon activity.

title: China assessed as a highly sophisticated threat actor
description: The 2025 review characterises China as a top-tier cyber adversary, targeting a wide range of UK sectors. The NCSC singles out activity overlapping with state-aligned groups Flax Typhoon and Salt Typhoon.
quote: "China is a highly sophisticated and capable threat actor targeting wide-ranging UK sectors."

title: Russia: a capable and irresponsible actor in cyberspace
description: The review highlights Russia's continued cyber operations supporting its war in Ukraine, the exposure of the Authentic Antics credential-stealing malware, and the growth of pro-Russia hacktivist groups targeting the UK, Europe, US, and NATO countries.
quote: "Russia is a capable and irresponsible threat actor in cyberspace."

title: Four state cyber threats facing the UK
description: The 2025 review profiles four primary state-sponsored cyber threats to the UK. The bars indicate the NCSC's qualitative ranking of intensity and breadth of activity across China, Russia, Iran, and DPRK — China and Russia are the most sophisticated/prolific, with Iran and DPRK focused on regional and revenue-generation goals.

title: Co-op ransomware incident: 6.5 million members affected
description: Among the high-profile UK ransomware incidents called out in the 2025 review, the Co-op attack affected all 6.5 million Co-op members. The wave of incidents — including Marks & Spencer and Jaguar Land Rover — anchored the review's 'time to act' message.

title: Top UK ransomware-targeted sectors
description: The NCSC names six sectors as the most-targeted by ransomware operators during the 2024–2025 review period. The ranking reflects the NCSC's order of priority concern, with academia and finance leading.

title: Three CVEs drove 29 NCSC-managed incidents
description: Three vulnerabilities accounted for 29 separately-managed incidents in 2024–2025: Ivanti Connect Secure (CVE-2025-0282), Fortinet FortiManager (CVE-2024-47575), and Microsoft SharePoint (CVE-2025-53770). They illustrate the continued risk from edge-network and collaboration software flaws.

title: 10.9M suspicious emails reported in 2024–2025
description: The NCSC's Suspicious Email Reporting Service (SERS) received over 10.9 million reports in the past year. Cumulative SERS reports since April 2020 now exceed 45 million, and 412,000 malicious URLs have been removed by the NCSC since 2020.

title: Active Cyber Defence takedowns and disruptions
description: The NCSC takedown service removed 1.2 million cyber-enabled commodity campaigns and disrupted over 26,000 phishing campaigns targeting UK Government departments in 2024–2025. The chart compares the scale of the major takedown categories.

title: 79% of HMG phishing attacks taken down in 24 hours
description: Of confirmed phishing attacks targeting UK Government departments, 79% were resolved within 24 hours, and 50% were taken down in under one hour. The speed reflects automation across the NCSC takedown service.

title: Early Warning service: IPs flagged to UK organisations
description: Through Early Warning, the NCSC alerted 13,178 signed-up organisations about a total of 316,343 IP addresses during the year — split between 131,000 IPs suspected of malware/compromise and 187,000 with detected vulnerabilities.

title: NCSC Mail Check vs Web Check coverage
description: Two of the NCSC's free assurance services scanned a combined 536,000+ domains and URLs in 2024–2025 and raised over 1.5 million Urgent or Advisory alerts to UK organisations.

title: 13,000+ UK schools protected by PDNS
description: The NCSC's Protective DNS service for schools is now safeguarding more than 13,000 UK schools, blocking access to malicious domains by default and shielding the education sector from a range of online threats.

title: 39,790 Cyber Essentials certifications awarded
description: Cyber Essentials certifications grew 17.5% year-over-year to 39,790, and Cyber Essentials Plus rose 17.3% to 12,850. The number of certifying bodies grew 12.3% to 402.

title: Cyber Essentials growth across certifications and bodies
description: Year-over-year growth percentages for the Cyber Essentials scheme: certifications, the Plus tier, and the network of accredited Certification Bodies all grew double digits.

title: Cyber Essentials orgs are 92% less likely to file insurance claims
description: Organisations certified under Cyber Essentials are 92% less likely to make a claim on their cyber insurance — one of the strongest signals to UK boards that the baseline scheme materially reduces realised loss.

title: Cyber Essentials: certified user perception
description: Survey of certified Cyber Essentials customers shows broad positive impact on risk understanding, board engagement, customer confidence, and competitiveness — with 95% saying they would recertify.

title: Funded Cyber Essentials Programme intake by year
description: The funded Cyber Essentials programme has supported 853 organisations since December 2022. Intake peaked in Year 1 (369 orgs) and tapered as the pilot prioritised renewals and broader rollout.

title: CNI Threat Hunting workshops, Spring 2025
description: The NCSC's Spring 2025 threat hunting workshops engaged 140 experienced analysts across UK government and private-sector critical national infrastructure (CNI) — 60 from 28 government organisations and 80 from 55 private-sector CNI organisations.

title: NCSC for Startups: programme totals at close
description: As the NCSC for Startups programme concluded, it had supported over 70 startups, helped raise more than £550M in investment, and created 1,700+ UK cyber-sector jobs.

title: CyberFirst returns £5.94 of social value per £1 invested
description: CyberFirst generated £41.4 million in social value in 2024–25, delivering £5.94 for every £1 invested — up from £4.06 the prior year. Over 350,000 students have engaged with the programme since 2017.

title: 14,500 girls in the CyberFirst Girls Competition
description: The 2025 CyberFirst Girls Competition reached 14,500 participants, the largest cohort to date, supported by collaboration between the NCSC, DSIT and IBM. CyberFirst will now feed into the £187M TechFirst programme announced by the Prime Minister in June 2025.

title: AI Security Code of Practice endorsed by 18 countries
description: The UK's AI Security Code of Practice — developed by DSIT with NCSC support — has been widely adopted across sectors and internationally endorsed by 18 countries. The work informed ETSI's first global AI lifecycle security standard.

title: AI is amplifying — not replacing — attacker tradecraft
description: The 2025 review's view on AI as an offensive enabler: threat actors are not inventing new attacks, they are using AI to scale and accelerate the playbook they already have.
quote: "Threat actors are using AI to increase the efficiency, effectiveness, and frequency of their cyber intrusions — fully automated spear-phishing campaigns, hijacking cloud-based LLMs, automating post-breach attack stages and data exfiltration."

title: UK post-quantum cryptography migration milestones
description: The NCSC's PQC migration roadmap sets three checkpoints: a complete inventory and migration plan by 2028, highest-priority services migrated by 2031, and full PQC migration of all systems by 2035.

title: 64 NCSC guidance and blog products published
description: Across 2024–2025 the NCSC published 64 products — 35 blog posts and 29 formal guidance documents — including CAF 4.0, the Software Security Code of Practice, MFA guidance, and SPI principles.

title: 46.1% of all customer signup attempts were malicious in 2024
description: Across the Auth0 platform in 2024, the median daily proportion of registration attempts that met the criteria of a signup attack was 46.1% — reversing a prior downward trend and consistent with a surge in fraudulent signups reported across other large tech companies, attributed to AI-enabled attack workflows.
comparison: reverses a prior downward trend; surge attributed to AI
pageOrSection: Threats against customer identity — Signup attacks

title: Peak day: 92.5% of signups were attack attempts
description: On April 6, 2024, 92.5% of registration attempts on the Auth0 platform met the criteria of a signup attack. In contrast, the lowest day of the year (February 29) still saw 14.4% — a major outlier, as no other day fell below 30%.
pageOrSection: Threats against customer identity — Signup attacks

title: Retail/eCommerce and FinServ are the top targets for fake signups
description: Median daily proportion of signup attempts that met the criteria of a signup attack in 2024, by industry. Retail/eCommerce led at nearly 70%, with Financial Services close behind at ~65%, well above the all-industries mean of 44.5%.
comparison: vs. mean of per-industry daily medians (44.5%)
pageOrSection: Fraudsters focus on retail and finance

title: Enterprises absorb the most fake-signup traffic
description: Median daily proportion of signup attempts meeting attack criteria, broken out by customer segment in 2024. Enterprises faced 64.3% — more than three times the rate seen by mid-market organizations.
pageOrSection: Fraudsters focus on retail and finance

title: 120x: attack signups outnumbered real signups during a sustained retail campaign
description: During a multi-month sustained attack against the Retail/eCommerce sector — which endured the highest proportion of attack signups of any industry in 2024 — the number of signup-attack events exceeded the number of legitimate signups by a factor of 120.
pageOrSection: The massive scale of signup attacks

title: 16.9% of customer logins showed clear malicious behavior
description: Across the Auth0 platform in 2024, the median daily proportion of login attempts that exhibited clear malicious behavior was 16.9% — a baseline rate for account takeover (ATO) attempts driven primarily by brute-force techniques like credential stuffing and password spraying.
comparison: median across all Auth0 customers in 2024
pageOrSection: Account takeovers (ATOs) present a constant threat

title: Daily login-attack rate swung from 7.6% to 47.4%
description: The 16.9% median masked dramatic day-to-day variability: across all of 2024, the highest daily rate of login attacks was 47.4% and the lowest 7.6%, including sustained multi-week ATO campaigns.
comparison: min vs. max daily rate in 2024
pageOrSection: Account takeovers (ATOs) present a constant threat

title: Retail/eCommerce sees double the ATO attempts of the average industry
description: Median daily proportion of login attempts meeting attack criteria in 2024, by industry. Retail/eCommerce was a clear outlier at 22.2%, with Professional Services and Financial Services hovering close to the all-industries mean of 10.0%.
pageOrSection: Where suspected ATO attacks are concentrated

title: Enterprises see the highest rate of malicious logins
description: Median daily proportion of login attempts that met the criteria of a login attack in 2024, by customer segment. Enterprises endured the highest rate at 24.9%, while mid-market and small businesses faced ATO pressure at 7.6% and 9.4% respectively.

title: MFA abuse continues a multi-year decline
description: Mean proportion of MFA events on the Auth0 platform classified as malicious. Falling from 12.7% in H1 2023 to a 2024 mean of 7.8% — and under 7% in the second half of 2024 — reflects improving secondary factors and tougher controls against MFA-fatigue and SMS-pumping attacks.
pageOrSection: MFA abuse remains common, but may be declining

title: 7.3%: median rate of malicious MFA events in 2024
description: In 2024, the median daily proportion of MFA events detected as being malicious on the Auth0 platform was 7.3% — with the majority attributable to MFA-fatigue attacks and SMS pumping (toll fraud). The sparkline approximates the multi-year trajectory of malicious-MFA share.
pageOrSection: MFA abuse remains common, but may be declining

title: Media leads industries in malicious MFA events
description: Median daily proportion of MFA events meeting the criteria of malicious activity in 2024, by industry. Media topped the chart at >20%, followed by Professional Services (17.6%) and Manufacturing (8.2%) — all well above the all-industries mean of 6.0%.
pageOrSection: Lights, camera, attack: Media leads in malicious MFA events

title: 11.6% of enterprise MFA events were malicious
description: Enterprises experienced the highest proportion of malicious MFA events of any customer segment in 2024 — 11.6%, nearly double the overall 6.0% average. Mid-market organizations recorded the lowest abuse rate at 3.1%.

title: 68% of consumers admit to reusing passwords
description: Despite years of warnings, 68% of users reported either using the same password for every account (17%) or reusing only a small set of passwords (51%) — poor hygiene that directly fuels credential-stuffing and ATO campaigns. 53% blame the inability to remember unique passwords.
pageOrSection: More than two-thirds of respondents reuse passwords

title: 64% of consumers are concerned about identity fraud
description: Across the entire 6,750-respondent survey, 64% of users said they are concerned about identity fraud (32% very concerned, 32% concerned), while only 10% expressed little or no concern. Respondents from India were the most concerned (81% concerned or very concerned).
pageOrSection: Identity fraud is a top-of-mind issue

title: Banks earn the most trust to secure consumer data
description: Consumers were asked how much they trust different sectors to secure their personal data. 63% trust banks and financial institutions; at the bottom, only 29% trust social-media platforms with the same. This trust gap shapes signup, login, and identity-sharing decisions.
pageOrSection: With identity fraud emerging as a top concern…

title: Nearly 1 in 4 shoppers abandon purchases due to signup or login friction
description: 23% of respondents report either always (6%) or often (17%) abandoning an online purchase due to issues with signup or login processes; a further 40% report sometimes doing so. Tech Innovators are even more intolerant — 43% always or often abandon when faced with friction.
pageOrSection: Signup and login issues drive customers away

title: 62% say long signup or login forms are their top frustration
description: Having to fill out long signup or login forms stands alone as the most frequently cited source of signup or login frustration — selected by 62% of respondents, well ahead of needing to provide private or sensitive information (52%).
pageOrSection: Long forms are the most frustrating signup or login hurdle

title: 73% of users still rate passwords as 'convenient'
description: Despite the security weaknesses, 73% of respondents rated passwords as either very convenient (40%) or convenient (33%) — a full 10 percentage points above the second-most-convenient authentication method. The correlation between usage and perceived convenience was 0.92.
pageOrSection: Convenience and familiarity drive login habits

title: Biometrics dominate perceived security; social login lags
description: Share of respondents who rated each authentication method as 'very secure' or 'secure'. Fingerprint (71%) and FaceID (62%) topped the rankings, while only 35% considered social login secure — a flag for marketers nudging users toward social SSO.
pageOrSection: Customers point to fingerprints as the most secure

title: 37% of consumers encounter AI agents very frequently or frequently
description: Auth0's survey found that 37% of customers encounter AI agents on online platforms or websites either very frequently or frequently — a fast-rising baseline as GenAI-powered non-human identities (NHIs) begin acting on behalf of users.

title: Users prefer humans over AI agents by a 4.4-to-1 ratio
description: Across the global survey, 70% favored interacting with humans while only 16% favored AI agents — a 4.4:1 ratio. Every cohort preferred humans; Tech Innovators were the closest (1.1) while Baby Boomers preferred humans by a striking 41.5-to-1.
pageOrSection: Humans aren't sold on AI agents — yet

title: 60% of consumers worry about AI's impact on identity privacy
description: 60% of survey respondents reported being either very concerned or concerned about AI's impact on the privacy and security of their digital identities; only 9% were not concerned. Privacy fears are the top reason cited by non-adopters of AI agents (44%).
pageOrSection: Privacy concern: AI's impact on identity

title: 23% of consumers refuse to use AI agents at all
description: 23% of respondents exclusively selected 'I would not use AI agents' — a stance driven largely by Tech Avoiders (73%), Baby Boomers (42%), Tech Traditionalists (43%) and respondents from Japan (37%). The leading reason (44%) is distrust of AI agents with personal information.

title: The benefits of AI agents require trust above all
description: Auth0's authors frame the report's central thesis: that as autonomous GenAI agents take on more user-facing tasks, customer identity and access management becomes the control plane for the trust those agents must earn.
quote: "The benefits of AI agents are vast, but their actions require sensitive, valuable, and possibly even confidential information from businesses and consumers. Above all, their actions require trust."

title: 71% of users took a risky action in 2023
description: Across a survey of 7,500 end users in 15 countries, 71% admitted to taking a risky action such as reusing or sharing passwords, clicking unknown links, or handing credentials to an untrustworthy source. 96% of them did so knowing the action was risky.
pageOrSection: Key Findings / Security Behaviors and Attitudes

title: 71% of organizations suffered a successful phishing attack
description: 71% of organizations experienced at least one successful phishing attack in 2023, down from 84% in 2022. Even as the incidence dropped, financial penalties from phishing rose 144% year over year and reputational damage reports rose 50%.

title: 66 million BEC attacks blocked every month
description: Proofpoint detected and blocked an average of 66 million targeted business email compromise (BEC) attacks per month. BEC activity is rising in non-English-speaking markets, with Japan up 35%, Korea up 31%, and the UAE up 29% year over year — partly driven by attackers using generative AI to craft convincing multilingual lures.

title: 73% of organizations hit by BEC, but only 29% train for it
description: 73% of organizations reported a BEC attack in 2023, yet only 29% of security awareness programs teach users specifically about BEC threats — exposing a wide gap between attack prevalence and dedicated training coverage.
comparison: 29% of orgs train users on BEC

title: 10 million TOAD (callback phishing) messages per month
description: Proofpoint observes an average of 10 million telephone-oriented attack delivery (TOAD) messages every month, with a peak of more than 13 million in August 2023. These lures contain only a phone number and bait users into calling cybercriminal call centers that walk them into granting remote access or installing malware.

title: Only 23% of organizations train users on TOAD attacks
description: Despite an average of 10 million callback-phishing (TOAD) messages every month, just 23% of organizations train their users to recognize and prevent TOAD attacks — leaving employees largely unprepared for one of the fastest-growing social-engineering vectors.

title: 1 million+ MFA-bypass attacks via EvilProxy every month
description: Proofpoint tracks more than 1 million phishing threats per month using the EvilProxy MFA-bypass framework, which proxies authentication to steal session tokens and one-time codes. Despite this, 89% of security professionals still believe MFA provides complete protection against account takeover.
comparison: 89% of security pros still trust MFA fully

title: 89% of security pros still believe MFA stops account takeover
description: 89% of surveyed security professionals agree MFA can completely protect against account compromise, and 84% of their organizations rely on MFA as the primary control against account takeover — even though Proofpoint sees more than 1 million MFA-bypass phishing attacks every month.
comparison: 84% of orgs rely on MFA to prevent ATO

title: QR-code phishing (quishing) emerges as a major lure
description: Proofpoint observed a sharp increase in QR codes used in place of malicious links or attachments. Quishing evades automated URL scanning and shifts the victim onto a mobile device — a context many users have never been trained to evaluate, and where it is impossible to tell from a glance whether a code leads to a phishing site or malware download.
quote: It is also impossible to tell just by looking if a QR code leads to a phishing site or malware download.

title: 69% of organizations infected by ransomware
description: The share of organizations hit by a ransomware attack climbed five percentage points to 69% in 2023. Nearly 60% of those affected reported four or more separate ransomware incidents over the year, reinforcing that ransomware remains a persistent and lucrative form of attack.

title: Global ransom payment rate falls to 54%
description: Among organizations infected with ransomware, the rate that agreed to pay attackers fell to 54% in 2023 — down from 58% in 2022 and 64% in 2021. Fewer victims regained data after paying, and 15% of organizations refused additional ransom demands (up from 6% in 2022).

title: 68 million malicious messages abused the Microsoft brand
description: Microsoft remains the world's most abused brand in phishing, with more than 68 million malicious messages referencing Microsoft or its products in 2023. Office 365 alone appeared in over 20 million threat emails. Adobe (9.4M) and DHL (8.8M) rounded out the top three, each at less than one-seventh of Microsoft's volume.

title: 183 million phishing simulations sent in 12 months
description: Proofpoint customers ran 183 million simulated phishing tests over a 12-month period. Link-based tests made up 59% of simulations, data-entry tests 30%, and attachment-based tests 10%. Attachment-based tests carried the highest failure rate, at 17%.

title: Average simulated phishing click-through rate of 9.3%
description: Across 183 million Proofpoint phishing simulations, the average failure (click) rate dropped slightly to 9.3% in 2023, from 10% in 2022 — meaning roughly one in eleven users still clicks, enters credentials, or opens a malicious attachment.

title: User reporting rate climbs to 18.3%
description: Reporting rates for simulated phishing rose to 18.3% in 2023, up from 17% in 2022. Reporting is a critical indicator of awareness, showing users can recognize a suspicious message and flag it to security rather than ignore or delete it.

title: Average resilience factor reaches 2.0
description: Proofpoint's Resilience Factor — the ratio of users who report phishing to those who fall for it — rose to 2.0 in 2023, up from 1.7 in 2022 and 1.5 in 2021. For the third year running, organizations got better at turning users into a detection layer rather than a vulnerability.

title: Finance leads industries with 9% phishing failure rate (-7 pts)
description: Finance was the most-improved industry in 2023, with its simulated phishing failure rate dropping from 16% to 9% — a seven-point decline year over year and a tie for the lowest failure rate in the benchmark.

title: Construction and Agriculture saw the biggest failure-rate increases
description: Construction and Agriculture were tied for the worst year-over-year change, with simulated phishing failure rates each climbing three percentage points from 2022 — pointing to a widening human-risk gap in industries with high frontline and field-based workforces.

title: 24 million suspicious emails reported by end users
description: Proofpoint customers' end users reported 24 million suspicious emails over a 12-month period, up from 18 million the prior year. Those reports contained nearly 2 million unique threats — with credential phishing dominating at 930,707 unique threats, followed by malware (~877k) and banking trojans (~52.6k).

title: 99% of organizations run a security awareness program, but only 53% train everyone
description: 99% of surveyed organizations have a security awareness program of some kind. Only 53% say they train every employee in the organization (down from 56% the prior year), 41% train specific roles or departments, and 6% train only specific individuals — leaving meaningful population gaps.

title: Only 23% of organizations train users on generative AI safety
description: Despite attackers using generative AI to craft more convincing multilingual lures, only 23% of organizations educate users on generative AI safety. That mirrors the 23% who train on TOAD attacks — two of the fastest-growing 2024 threat vectors with the lowest training coverage.
comparison: Matches the 23% who train on TOAD

title: Only 34% of organizations run simulated phishing attacks
description: Despite the high volume of malicious email in the threat landscape, just 34% of organizations include simulated phishing in their security-awareness programs. Computer-based training (45%) remains the most common tactic, while smishing/vishing simulations and gamified contests are gaining traction (the latter up 23% YoY).

title: OneDrive deactivation lure has the highest 10% failure rate
description: Microsoft branding appeared in 7 of the top 10 phishing-simulation templates run by Proofpoint customers. A 'Microsoft deactivation of old OneDrive account' lure produced the highest failure rate (10%) — exploiting loss aversion and urgency, the emotional triggers at the core of effective social engineering.

title: 85% of security pros say employees feel responsible — but only 41% of users agree
description: 85% of security professionals say most employees know they are responsible for security. Reality from the user survey looks very different: only 41% of employees said they bear responsibility, 7% said they aren't responsible at all, and 52% weren't sure — a 44-point perception gap that explains why awareness alone fails to change behavior.

title: 94% of users say easier security would motivate them to follow it
description: 94% of end users agree that making security easier would motivate them to be more attentive to it — outranking rewards (89%), leadership engagement (87%), more training (85%), and punishment (71%). Yet 83% of security teams respond with more training and 81% with more controls or restrictions, widening the gap between security operations and user motivation.
comparison: 83% of security teams default to more training

title: Bulk phishing remains most prevalent attack type at 76%
description: Survey respondents say bulk phishing is the most prevalent attack they face (76%), followed by spear phishing (74%), social media attacks (73%), BEC (75%), ransomware (76%), smishing (75%), and vishing (67%). Even USB drop attacks were reported by 60% of organizations — proof that attackers will reuse any tactic if there is a chance it works.

title: Report draws on 7,500 users, 1,050 pros, and 15 countries
description: The 2024 State of the Phish is built on a survey of 7,500 end users and 1,050 security professionals across 15 countries, plus telemetry from 183 million simulated phishing messages and more than 24 million end-user-reported emails analyzed over a 12-month period.

title: Identity is the ultimate battleground
description: PwC's headline narrative for 2026 reframes the perimeter: adversaries are no longer breaking in, they are logging in by abusing credentials, session tokens, and federated access to bypass traditional defences.
quote: "Adversaries are increasingly choosing to log in rather than break in, exploiting credentials, session tokens, and federated access to bypass traditional perimeter defences. Identity has become the ultimate battleground."

title: 63% of manufacturing attacks are cybercrime-motivated
description: Manufacturing remained a top sector target in PwC's 2026 dataset, with the majority of observed incidents driven by financially motivated cybercrime rather than espionage or sabotage. Incidents frequently cascaded into broader supply-chain disruption.

title: Manufacturing attack motivations, 2025
description: PwC's breakdown of motivations behind attacks on the manufacturing sector shows cybercrime dominating, followed by state-aligned espionage. Sabotage and hacktivism account for small but strategically meaningful slices of activity against operational technology environments.

title: Threat actors treat AI as core tradecraft
description: PwC's incident-response team reports that AI-driven threats are now the most frequently raised client concern, with adversaries integrating generative AI into reconnaissance, malware development, and multilingual social engineering pipelines.
quote: "Threat actors are embracing AI not as an enhancement but as a core component of their tradecraft, using it to automate reconnaissance, craft highly convincing phishing campaigns, accelerate malware development, and scale social engineering across languages and platforms."

title: AI-automated spear-phishing click-through 4.5x generic phishing
description: PwC cites research showing AI-automated spear-phishing emails achieved a 54% click-through rate versus 12% for generic phishing, underscoring how generative AI raises the conversion rate of social-engineering campaigns at scale.

title: 88% of web-app breaches involve stolen credentials
description: PwC reinforces its identity-first thesis with Verizon data showing the overwhelming majority of breaches in web-application attacks rely on stolen credentials — a key reason identity remains the primary attack vector heading into 2026.

title: Identity abuse is the top entry point at 30%
description: PwC cites IBM data showing abuse of user identities is the single most common initial entry point for intrusions, reinforcing the report's central finding that identity has overtaken exploits and email as the primary attack vector.

title: AI-related incidents up 56.4% YoY
description: PwC cites Stanford HAI data tracking 233 AI-related incidents in 2024, a 56.4% increase over 2023 — quantitative confirmation that adversarial AI exposure is growing alongside enterprise AI adoption.

title: AI governance gaps are nearly universal
description: PwC highlights two governance failures that explain why AI is amplifying risk: nearly all organisations experiencing AI security incidents lacked proper access controls, and most have no AI governance policy in place at all.

title: GenAI prompts to SaaS apps up 6x to 18,000/month
description: PwC cites Netskope data showing organisational prompts to SaaS GenAI applications grew sixfold from roughly 3,000 to 18,000 per month, with an average of 223 GenAI data-policy violations per organisation per month — a rapidly expanding shadow-AI surface.

title: Personal AI app use for work falls to 47%
description: Personal AI app use for work declined from 78% to 47%, reflecting the maturing of enterprise-sanctioned AI tooling — though the gap is now being filled by sanctioned SaaS GenAI usage, which has grown sixfold.

title: Supply-chain compromises up nearly 4x since 2020
description: PwC cites IBM X-Force telemetry showing supply-chain and third-party compromise incidents have grown nearly fourfold since 2020, validating the report's emphasis on managing risk beyond the direct enterprise perimeter.

title: Top OT/IIoT security challenges for executives
description: PwC's executive-concerns data highlights two structural OT/IIoT security barriers: a shortage of qualified personnel and unclear governance over who owns OT security — both blocking the convergence of IT and OT defence programmes.

series.name: Share citing as top OT/IIoT challenge

title: Blurring boundaries between motivations
description: PwC argues the traditional clean lines between cybercrime, espionage, and influence operations have dissolved — with ransomware operators monetising strategic data, state actors using criminal tooling, and DPRK-linked operations industrialising fraudulent employment.
quote: "The boundaries between motivations continued to blur, as ransomware operators sold strategically sensitive data, espionage-motivated threat actors leveraged cyber criminal tooling, and North Korea-based threat actors industrialised fraudulent employment and cryptocurrency theft at unprecedented scale."

title: DPRK industrialised fraudulent IT-worker scheme
description: North Korea-linked operations scaled fraudulent remote-employment schemes and cryptocurrency theft to unprecedented levels in 2025, with stolen identities used to place operatives inside global enterprises while funnelling salaries and stolen funds to the regime.

title: China-based actor deployed autonomous AI red-team agent
description: Following the release of ReaperAI, a penetration-testing AI agent, PwC documented a China-based threat actor deploying a comparable tool capable of autonomous reconnaissance and exploit execution — an early example of agentic AI in offensive operations.
quote: "Following the release of ReaperAI, a China-based threat actor deployed a comparable tool capable of autonomous reconnaissance and exploit execution."

title: AWM sector hit by BEC, ransomware, and crypto heists
description: PwC's sector view of asset & wealth management (AWM) and financial services shows convergence of business-email compromise with AI-generated deepfakes, ransomware operations, and large heists targeting cryptocurrency platforms — all leveraging identity abuse as the common pivot.

title: Healthcare ransomware crosses into life-safety risk
description: PwC continues to flag healthcare and hospitality as ransomware-exposed sectors where attacks disrupt operations and, in healthcare specifically, can become life-threatening — elevating ransomware from an IT-availability issue to a patient-safety issue.

title: Adversaries deploy full-stack tradecraft
description: PwC characterises the 2026 threat landscape as one where adversaries move fluidly across identity, cloud, edge, and application layers — a 'full-stack' approach that breaks single-layer defensive models and demands integrated, identity-anchored security architecture.
quote: "We are seeing an increasingly capable and adaptive threat landscape in which adversaries employ full-stack tradecraft and are fluidly navigating identity, cloud, edge, and application layers with unprecedented precision."

title: AI is the #1 cyber investment priority
description: PwC reports that AI-driven defence has become the top cybersecurity investment priority among security leaders heading into 2026, paralleling the rise of AI-driven offence. AI is now identified as the most frequently raised client concern by PwC's incident-response team.

title: Post-quantum readiness becomes urgent
description: PwC flags quantum computing as a near-term cryptographic risk and pairs it with rapidly expanding SaaS ecosystems as the two emerging surfaces defenders must instrument now — recommending post-quantum cryptography transition planning and SaaS-identity governance.
quote: "Quantum computing threats to cryptography and expanding SaaS ecosystems widening attack surfaces make post-quantum cryptography transition an urgent strategic priority."

title: Disclosure-to-exploitation race tighter than ever
description: Rapid7 Labs Chief Scientist Raj Samani frames Q3 2025 as a quarter defined by zero-day mass exploitation, supply-chain fragility, and the operationalization of AI by adversaries.
quote: "The race between disclosure and exploitation has never been tighter, with many organizations caught in the gap."

title: 53 vulnerabilities first exploited in the wild in Q3
description: Rapid7's AttackerKB tracked 53 vulnerabilities reported as exploited in the wild for the first time in Q3 2025 — a continued quarter-on-quarter decline from this time last year, though Rapid7 cautions the macro drop hides troubling patterns in the data.

title: 5 of 5 Emergent Threat Response cases were zero-days
description: All five high-profile threats triaged by Rapid7's Emergent Threat Response (ETR) program in Q3 2025 had been exploited as zero-day vulnerabilities — before vendor patches were available. Targets included CrushFTP, SharePoint, NetScaler, GoAnywhere MFT, and Cisco ASA/FTD.

title: 18-year-old CVE first KEV-listed in Q3
description: CVE-2007-0671 — disclosed 18 years ago and reportedly exploited in the wild by the vendor circa 2007 — only received its first official exploitation-in-the-wild report this quarter when CISA added it to the KEV list. Rapid7 warns that relying solely on KEV for remediation is 'useful, but brittle.'

title: 10 Q3 vulns disclosed more than a year earlier
description: Of the 53 vulnerabilities first reported as exploited in the wild in Q3, 10 had CVE disclosure dates more than a year ago — some over a decade old. Rapid7 stresses that historical vulnerabilities remain potent attack vectors and cannot be ignored in remediation planning.

title: Top CWE classes for Q3 exploited-in-the-wild vulns
description: Unsafe deserialization (CWE-502) led the root-cause categories for Q3 2025 exploited-in-the-wild vulnerabilities by a notable margin, with command injection (CWE-78, CWE-77) in second and third place. Attackers favor these logic-level classes for reliability of exploitation over memory corruption bugs. (Illustrative ranks; chart in PDF.)

title: 88 active ransomware groups in Q3 2025
description: Rapid7 observed 88 ransomware groups actively posting to leak sites in Q3 2025, up from 65 in Q2 and 76 in Q1 — a signal of renewed energy and proliferation across the ransomware economy.
pageOrSection: The ransomware landscape — At a glance

title: Ransomware group churn: new vs. inactive in Q3
description: Of the 88 ransomware groups active in Q3 2025, 28 were brand-new additions to the active leak-site cohort. Meanwhile, 19 of the 65 groups that posted leaks in Q2 went silent during July–September 2025 — illustrating high churn in the ecosystem.
pageOrSection: The ransomware landscape — At a glance

title: Qilin retains #1 ransomware spot
description: Qilin retained the top position by number of leak-site posts in Q3 2025, with Akira and INC Ransom in second and third place respectively. Devman, WorldLeaks, and Everest were the only new entrants to the top 10 this quarter.

title: Top targeted industries — ransomware leak posts
description: Business services led ransomware victim posts in Q3 2025 at 18%, followed by manufacturing (15%) and healthcare (13%). Construction and financial services round out the top five most-targeted industries.

title: Top regional targets — ransomware victim share
description: The United States accounted for 67% of ransomware leak-site posts in Q3 2025, with Germany a distant second at 6%. The UK and Canada were tied at 5%, followed by Italy (4%) and France (3%).

title: US absorbs 67% of ransomware victim posts
description: The United States overwhelmingly dominated Q3 2025 ransomware victimology, accounting for roughly two-thirds of all leak-site posts — far ahead of Germany (6%) and the joint-third UK/Canada (5% each).

title: Qilin–LockBit–DragonForce coalition announced
description: A DragonForce admin post on the dark web site Ransombay formally announced a coalition with Qilin and a refreshed LockBit (sporting an all-new version 5.0). The merging of tactics and infrastructure could solidify these groups' dominance through Q4 2025 and the year as a whole.
quote: "The coalition between Qilin, LockBit, and DragonForce... If you have a partnership program, feel free to reach out to us, and together we can maximize our overall income!"

title: Crimson Collective hits 28,000 Red Hat repos
description: Crimson Collective rose to prominence after claiming responsibility for the compromise of 28,000 private Red Hat repositories, followed by AWS targeting via TruffleHog credential-hunting and an alleged breach of Nintendo's internal systems.

title: BRICKSTORM dwell time exceeded 12 months at F5
description: F5 confirmed that an unauthorized actor — linked by reports to BRICKSTORM/UNC5221 — accessed internal development systems beginning on or around August 9, 2025, exfiltrating BIG-IP source code, internal vulnerability data, and configuration artifacts. Dwell times in some cases exceeded 12 months.

title: SharePoint ToolPane chain — Q3's most impactful incident
description: The SharePoint exploit chain — initially demonstrated at Pwn2Own Berlin 2025 and leaked to a threat actor — saw mass exploitation just before Microsoft's July 2025 patch release. Patch bypasses CVE-2025-53770 and CVE-2025-53771 required an out-of-band Microsoft release.
quote: "Due to the pervasive deployment of SharePoint across multiple industry verticals, this threat campaign was likely the most significant and highly impactful incident in Q3."

title: 3 critical Cisco ASA/FTD vulns patched in late Sept
description: In late September 2025, Cisco published patches for three critical vulnerabilities (CVE-2025-20333, CVE-2025-20362, CVE-2025-20363) affecting ASA and FTD products. CVE-2025-20362 is trivial to exploit and is a patch bypass of CVE-2018-0296. The chain was exploited in highly targeted attacks by an unknown threat actor.

title: Managed File Transfer zero-days dominate Q3 ETRs
description: Two of the five Q3 2025 Emergent Threat Response cases — CrushFTP (CVE-2025-54309) and GoAnywhere MFT (CVE-2025-10035) — targeted enterprise managed file transfer platforms. The GoAnywhere exploit was attributed to Storm-1175 and used to deploy Medusa ransomware.

title: Top 10 MITRE ATT&CK techniques observed in Q3
description: Valid accounts (T1078) and external remote services (T1133) led the top 10 MITRE ATT&CK techniques observed across Rapid7-investigated incidents in Q3 2025 — reflecting the dominance of credential compromise and VPN/RDP exploitation as initial access vectors. (Ranks shown; counts illustrative.)
pageOrSection: Top 10 MITRE ATT&CK techniques for Q3

title: Most impacted sectors in Rapid7 IR cases
description: Across Rapid7 Incident Response investigations in Q3 2025, the most impacted sectors were retail, real estate, and manufacturing — overlapping but distinct from the ransomware-leak-site victimology, which skewed toward business services and healthcare.

title: LAMEHUG: LLM-driven malware operationalized
description: A Pawn Storm-affiliated Russian group deployed LAMEHUG — a malware family that uses a large language model to dynamically generate command-and-control logic, evading signature-based and static analysis. Rapid7 says this signals a 'new frontier' in malware development.
quote: "The theoretical risk of AI has been fully operationalized. Defenders must now assume attackers are using these tools and techniques against them."

title: 11,000+ customers powering Rapid7 telemetry
description: Rapid7's Q3 2025 Threat Landscape Report draws on telemetry, AttackerKB community vulnerability intelligence, Intelligence Hub correlations, and Incident Response engagements across more than 11,000 customers worldwide.

title: Threats analyzed in 2025
description: Red Canary's 2026 Threat Detection Report analyzed approximately 110,000 confirmed threats detected across 1,000+ customer environments throughout the past year. Each threat bypassed existing security controls.

title: Identity threats now majority of detections
description: Identity-based threats have overtaken endpoint detections in Red Canary's telemetry, signaling a fundamental shift in adversary tradecraft toward credential abuse and cloud account compromise.
quote: "Identity-based threats now account for more than half of our total confirmed threats, following an 850 percent increase in identity threat detections year-over-year."

title: Identity threat detections YoY increase
description: Identity threat detections grew 850 percent from 2024 to 2025, becoming Red Canary's fastest-growing detection category. Infostealers, device code phishing, consent phishing, and MFA bypass drove the surge.

title: Identity share of total detections
description: Identity-based threats accounted for 53% of overall detection volume in 2025, overtaking endpoint detections by a significant margin for the first time in Red Canary's reporting history.

title: Cloud Accounts climbs to #1 technique
description: Cloud Accounts (T1078.004) now ranks #1 in Red Canary's top 10 ATT&CK techniques, affecting 21% of customers with 2,480 detected threats. Detection volume increased 16-fold year over year as adversaries find it easier to log in than hack in.

title: Customers affected by Cloud Accounts abuse
description: 21% of Red Canary customers experienced threats involving Cloud Accounts (T1078.004) abuse in 2025. Most detections occurred at login, with adversaries authenticating from unusual VPNs, geographies, ASNs, or devices.

title: Top 10 ATT&CK techniques detected
description: Red Canary ranks the most prevalent MITRE ATT&CK techniques observed across its customer base in 2025. Cloud Accounts overtook traditional endpoint techniques, while PowerShell and Windows Command Shell remain core adversary tooling.

title: Customer impact of top techniques
description: Percentage of Red Canary customers affected by the two leading ATT&CK techniques in 2025. Cloud Accounts (T1078.004) hit 21% of customers, while PowerShell (T1059.001) affected 19.6%.

title: Detected threat volume for top techniques
description: Raw count of confirmed threats associated with each top technique. Cloud Accounts generated 2,480 confirmed threats — more than double PowerShell's 1,054 — reflecting the rapid pivot of adversaries to cloud-native tradecraft.

title: Amber Albatross #1 threat of 2025
description: Amber Albatross was the most prevalent threat in Red Canary's 2025 telemetry, affecting 11.1% of customers. A Pyarmor-obfuscated PyInstaller payload masquerades as PDF utilities and PUPs like PC App Store, then performs reconnaissance and browser credential theft.

title: Top 10 threats by prevalence
description: Red Canary's ten most prevalent threats in 2025 customer environments. Activity clusters Amber Albatross, JustAskJacky, and Tampered Chef topped the list, while stealers LummaC2 (rank 5) and Rhadamanthys (rank 10) continued to dominate the eCrime ecosystem.

title: LummaC2 reach before takedown
description: LummaC2 (Lumma Stealer) affected 3.7% of Red Canary customers in 2025, ranking #5 among top threats. After Operation Endgame's May 2025 infrastructure takedown, activity dropped sharply with no detections after October 2025.

title: LummaC2 source-code price
description: LummaC2 subscriptions started at $250 per month for the malware-as-a-service tier, with full source code available for a one-time payment of $20,000 USD before its May 2025 takedown.

title: Ransomware victims up 33%
description: 2025 saw approximately 33% more ransomware victims than 2023 and 2024, with a near-identical jump in active ransomware groups. Operators shifted from high-value targeting to a higher-volume strategy as payment rates fell.

title: Ransomware payout demands rising
