description: Phishing attacks against the education sector spiked 224% year-over-year, the largest jump of any industry in the report. Threat actors exploited academic calendars, financial-aid deadlines, and chronically under-funded security defenses.

title: Tech-support and job-scam hits
description: Tech support impersonation and fake job-recruitment scams together produced more than 159 million hits in 2024. Attackers exploit unemployment anxiety and IT-help-desk trust to harvest credentials and payment details.

title: Microsoft share of brand-imitation phishing
description: Microsoft accounted for 51.7% of all brand-impersonation phishing attacks in 2024, a sharp jump from 43.1% the prior year. Attackers concentrate on OneDrive, SharePoint, and Microsoft 365 login flows, increasingly fronted by CAPTCHA gates.

title: AI-driven phishing campaigns growth
description: Zscaler's research found a 60% year-over-year increase in AI-driven phishing campaigns leading into the 2025 report period. Generative AI is now the primary force multiplier behind vishing, deepfakes, and high-fidelity brand cloning.

title: Industry phishing trend (YoY % change, 2024)
description: Industries diverged sharply in 2024. Education surged 224%, while Finance & Insurance collapsed 78.2%, Technology fell 32.8%, and Manufacturing slipped 16.8% but kept the #1 spot by raw volume.

title: Top imitated brands in phishing (2024)
description: Microsoft dominated brand-imitation phishing in 2024 with 51.7% of all attempts. Telegram, Google, Netflix, and Facebook rounded out the top five. Telegram is notable as both a spoofed brand and the most-abused legitimate platform for distributing malicious content.

title: Microsoft share of brand-imitation phishing (multi-year)
description: Microsoft's share of brand-impersonation phishing has climbed steadily from 43.1% in 2023 to 51.7% in 2024, reinforcing its position as the runaway top spoofed brand for credential harvesting.

title: Top targeted countries (2024)
description: The United States remained the #1 phishing target despite a 31.8% drop, followed by India, Germany, and the United Kingdom. Brazil entered the top 10 for the first time on the back of accelerating digital adoption and lagging cybersecurity maturity.

title: Emerging high-growth target geographies
description: Three markets stood out as emerging phishing-growth hotspots in 2024: Brazil, Hong Kong, and the Netherlands. Each saw cybercriminals exploit rapid digital growth that outpaced security maturity, with Brazil's $186.6B digital-transformation push cited as the inflection point.

title: Phishing channel mix shift
description: As email authentication tightened, attackers diversified channels. Voice phishing (vishing), SMS phishing (smishing), QR-code phishing (quishing), and chat-platform abuse all grew as a share of the phishing mix in 2024 relative to traditional email.

title: Quishing flagged as fastest-growing initial access
description: QR-code phishing (quishing) was singled out as one of the fastest-growing initial-access tactics of 2024. Malicious URLs encoded in QR images bypass URL inspection and shift the click from corporate laptops to personal mobile devices.

title: Vishing impersonates IT support to steal credentials in real time
description: Vishing emerged as one of the most prominent tactics of 2024. Attackers call victims posing as IT helpdesk staff, walk them through credential and MFA prompts, and capture session tokens live — Scattered Spider-style social engineering went mainstream.
quote: "Voice phishing (vishing) has become a prominent tactic, with attackers impersonating IT support to steal credentials in real time."

title: CAPTCHA gates now standard on phishing pages
description: Attackers routinely place CAPTCHAs and Cloudflare Turnstile clones in front of phishing landing pages so the destinations look legitimate and crawler-based security tools cannot inspect them. The pattern is now baseline in adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) kits.

title: Fake AI-agent websites as a new phishing category
description: ThreatLabz flagged a new class of phishing: fraudulent 'AI agent' sites cloning ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and AI image generators to harvest credentials and payment cards. Attackers ride on surging public trust in AI tools.

title: Crypto wallet and exchange scams
description: Fake cryptocurrency exchanges and wallet sites continued to lure users with convincing decoys, enabling attackers to steal credentials, seed phrases, and drain digital funds. The category is now a fixture in the phishing landscape.

title: Most-targeted internal business functions
description: Attackers concentrate phishing on roles with payment authority or identity-workflow access. HR, payroll, and finance are the top three targeted internal functions, with IT helpdesk in the mix via vishing impersonation.

title: Phishing-as-a-Service lowers the bar
description: PhaaS kits with adversary-in-the-middle proxying, MFA bypass, session-cookie theft, and AI-generated lure pages drove down the skill required to run sophisticated campaigns. The barrier to entry collapsed in 2024.

title: Zero Trust as the structural answer
description: ThreatLabz closes by arguing that as phishing pivots from inbox to voice, SMS, QR, and chat platforms, a zero-trust architecture with TLS inspection, least-privilege segmentation, and DLP across AI tools is the only durable defense.
quote: "Attackers leaned into hyper-targeted social engineering techniques like vishing (voice phishing) and smishing (SMS phishing)."

title: Ransomware attacks skyrocketed 145.9% year-over-year
description: Zscaler's cloud blocked an unprecedented surge in ransomware attempts between April 2024 and April 2025. ThreatLabz says the 145.9% YoY growth shows attackers are scaling campaigns faster than ever before.

title: Public extortion cases jumped 70.1% YoY
description: Far more organizations were listed on ransomware leak sites year-over-year as attackers escalate pressure tactics. The growth in public shaming campaigns underscores extortion's central role in modern ransomware economics.

title: Data exfiltration volumes surged 92.7%
description: ThreatLabz observed a near-doubling of data theft volumes by ransomware operators year-over-year. The pattern confirms that stealing sensitive files — not just encrypting them — is now the primary lever for extortion.

title: 238.5 TB of data exfiltrated by top 10 families
description: Across 10 major ransomware families analyzed by ThreatLabz, attackers stole a combined 238.5 terabytes of data over the year. The figure quantifies how aggressively today's RaaS operations weaponize stolen information for ransom leverage.

title: 34 new ransomware groups emerged
description: ThreatLabz catalogued 34 newly active ransomware brands during the analysis window. The count includes rebrands, offshoots of defunct gangs, and entirely new entrants rushing to fill voids left by law-enforcement takedowns.

title: ThreatLabz on the new ransomware reality
description: ThreatLabz frames the 2025 landscape as a fundamental architectural challenge — not just a volume problem. The authors argue that legacy network defenses are structurally incompatible with how modern ransomware operates.
quote: "Today's ransomware threat landscape demands a new level of operational vigilance and a fundamentally different security architecture than traditional security models provide."

title: Three headline YoY surges shaping the 2025 ransomware year
description: ThreatLabz's three signature year-over-year metrics — blocked attacks, public extortion listings, and exfiltrated data volumes — all moved sharply upward. The chart contrasts how each dimension of the ransomware problem accelerated in parallel.

title: Sharpest YoY industry spikes: Oil & Gas and Government
description: While Manufacturing, Technology and Healthcare led in absolute attack volume, the most dramatic year-over-year jumps hit critical-infrastructure verticals. Oil & Gas saw a near-10x surge and Government attacks more than tripled.

title: Oil & Gas ransomware attacks up 935% YoY
description: Energy operators saw a nearly tenfold jump in ransomware activity, the steepest sector-level increase in the report. Critical infrastructure exposure and OT-adjacent systems make this vertical a high-value extortion target.

title: Government ransomware attacks up 235% YoY
description: Public-sector ransomware activity more than tripled year-over-year. Municipalities, agencies, and state entities remain attractive targets due to constrained security budgets and high pressure to restore citizen services.

title: Most-targeted industries by absolute attack volume
description: Manufacturing, Technology, and Healthcare remained the three most-attacked sectors in 2025. ThreatLabz cites their large attack surfaces, low tolerance for downtime, and rich data troves as the structural reasons they stay on top.

title: Top RaaS brands driving the 2025 surge
description: RansomHub, Clop, and Akira dominated leak-site victim totals in ThreatLabz's analysis window. Together they accounted for a disproportionate share of public extortion listings as new groups churned around them.

title: Extortion now eclipses encryption
description: ThreatLabz observed a strategic shift away from file encryption toward pure data-theft extortion. Reputational, regulatory, and IP-loss threats have become the primary coercion tools.
quote: "Some attackers are skipping file encryption altogether, opting to steal sensitive data and use the threat of public exposure via leak sites."

title: At least 1 notorious group used ChatGPT in attacks
description: ThreatLabz uncovered direct evidence that a high-profile ransomware crew leveraged ChatGPT to support attack execution. GenAI is now being used to automate tasks and write code that streamlines operations and improves attack effectiveness.

title: Tailored attacks impersonating IT staff
description: ThreatLabz reports a tactical shift away from opportunistic spam toward narrowly targeted social engineering. Attackers now impersonate internal IT to compromise employees with privileged access.

title: Ransomware actors pivot to IT impersonation
description: ThreatLabz characterizes 2025 as a turning point where bulk phishing gave way to surgical impersonation campaigns. The new playbook targets help-desk and admin personas to harvest privileged credentials.
quote: "Ransomware threat actors have largely shifted away from traditional large-scale spam campaigns... in favor of more tailored attacks that impersonate IT staff to target employees with privileged access."

title: 5 enterprise tech categories weaponized for initial access
description: ThreatLabz observes that ransomware operators consistently exploit a narrow set of widely-deployed enterprise tools to land first. Each represents an internet-exposed control plane attackers can scan and abuse.

title: Scanning + automated exploitation is enough
description: ThreatLabz emphasizes the unglamorous truth behind most ransomware breaches: simple internet scans and off-the-shelf exploits still work. Firewalls and VPNs leave too much exposed for opportunistic operators to ignore.
quote: "In most cases, attackers gained initial access through simple scanning and automated exploitation of internet-connected systems."

title: 10 ransomware families analyzed for exfiltration
description: ThreatLabz built its 238.5 TB exfiltration figure by deep-analyzing the 10 most active ransomware families during the year. This focused dataset underpins the report's data-theft conclusions.

title: Zero Trust coverage across the ransomware kill chain
description: Zscaler frames defense as four sequential capabilities aligned to attacker stages: hiding the attack surface, blocking initial compromise, killing lateral movement, and stopping exfiltration. The model anchors the report's prescriptive guidance.

title: 12-month analysis window: April 2024 – April 2025
description: All ThreatLabz findings — including the 145.9% attack increase and 238.5 TB exfiltration figure — were derived from a continuous 12-month observation window. Telemetry combined leak-site monitoring, Zscaler cloud signals, and reverse-engineered samples.

title: Top 5 ransomware groups to watch next year
description: Beyond today's dominant RansomHub, Clop and Akira, ThreatLabz nominated five rising groups whose extortion-first playbook signals where the ecosystem is heading. The list represents the report's forward-looking threat watchlist.
